map:edges-organisms.scope: organisms and templates (all 8 files in src/styles/organisms + both in src/styles/templates), read against abstracts/_mixins.scss, _tokens.scss, _generated.scss. Token values quoted are the built sorbet preset (dist/themes/sorbet.css, built 2026-09-27). Read-only; nothing changed.
map:edges-organisms.summary:
TAKEAWAYS (numbers: L* = perceptual lightness 0-100; "ratio" = WCAG contrast ratio, where 1.00 means identical lightness, i.e. distinguishable by hue only)

1. Organisms/templates draw almost no hard outlines already. 13 one-pixel lines exist in scope and 10 of them are the same hand-written declaration, `token(border-width) solid clr(border-subtle)`. Light border-subtle is #f1eeeb (L*94.2): 1.16 on white, 1.08 on the page #f8f7f5. So most of these are already near-invisible rather than harsh.

2. The dark-mode "no edges" problem is reproducible from the tokens, not from the components: dark border-subtle #38342f IS dark surface #38342f (ratio 1.00), and dark border #4b463f IS dark surface-raised. In the dark app-shell sidebar three things vanish at once: the rail's edge line (1.00), the hover fill bg-subtle (1.00) and the current-page fill primary-subtle #003d40 (1.02).

3. The only genuinely harsh gray in scope is border-strong #777168 (L*47.9, 4.5-4.8 on light surfaces): the chart crosshair and the command-trigger hover border. It is that dark because rules.ts holds it to 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11).

4. Modal and drawer are ALREADY shadow-only (border: none + shadow(xl)) and are the existing proof case. But today's shadows are not "similarly coloured": one per-preset tint (sorbet: rgb(38 35 31), a near-black warm gray) at alpha .06-.24 in light, pure black at 2.4x alpha in dark. Darkest possible composite on the page: xs 1.12, md 1.26, xl 1.62. Every shadow token is a downward drop with negative spread; none has a zero-offset all-round layer, which is what replacing a border needs.

5. Weakest usability signal in scope (matters more than any edge for a colourblind reader): current-page in navbar/sidebar is hue-only. Light: current fill #d2f7fb vs hover fill #f1eeeb = 1.01; current text #00686d (L*39.6) vs resting text #5f5a52 (L*38.5) = 1.04. No weight change, no bar, no underline. Same shape for the command palette's highlighted option (1.14 light / 1.29 dark), which is the ONLY keyboard-cursor indicator there because the input sets outline: none.

6. Nothing in scope uses elevate, popover-surface or control-glow. Modal, drawer and the chart tooltip hand-roll the same background + shadow pair, and there is no divider/edge mixin at all, so a one-place change today is only possible at TOKEN level (border-subtle / border / shadow-*), not mixin level.

7. No invalid / checked / selected / switch / slider / progress shapes are drawn in organisms or templates; those live in atoms and molecules. In-scope states are: focus (2 mixin uses + the global base rule), current page, highlighted option, hover, disabled, modality (scrim), chart crosshair and sparkline accent.

ALSO WORTH KNOWING FOR THE PLAN
- tokens/rules.ts is the WCAG gate ("the build fails otherwise"); organisms/_token-studio.scss styles its contrast report (__report / __failures). Dropping WCAG means deciding what that gate and report become, not just changing colours.
- The scrim is hard-coded black at 0.6 in both modes for a WCAG worst-case rule (on-scrim text over any photo); it is the one pure-black fill in scope.
- templates/_auth.scss paints tinted washes behind a card, so whatever soft edge the card gets has to hold against primary-subtle / accent-subtle / secondary-subtle, not only the page colour.
- Partial reads outside the brief, for values only: base/_root.scss, tokens/semantics.ts, emit.ts, rules.ts, presets.ts, and three component files to confirm how chart colours and the command highlight are driven.

uses.note: SVG gridline; box-shadow cannot apply to an SVG stroke, so recolour rather than replace. Light #f1eeeb = 1.16 on white; dark #38342f = 1.00 on a dark surface card (already invisible there).
Baseline that anchors bars/lines to zero; SVG stroke. Light #e3dfd9 (L*89.0) = 1.33 on white. Carries value-reading information; needs a lightness step, can be a tinted pastel.
Shows which x position is being read on hover. Today the harsh gray #777168 (L*47.9, 4.83 on white). Colour can soften but it must stay a clear lightness step; a shadow cannot mark a position.

Knockout ring separating an end/hover marker from its own line; fill is inline series colour. Not gray. Assumes the chart sits on `surface`; on a cream page or tinted card the ring shows as a white halo.

uses.declaration: border-radius: radius(xs); (fill is inline: style={{ background: seriesColor(i) }})
uses.note: 8-10px legend key with NO edge today. A pale pastel series fill on cream would vanish; a same-hue soft shadow could hold it. Series identity is hue-only, which is the colourblind risk (chart-1..8 tokens, tokens/charts.ts), not an edge problem.
White on white card: line is 1.16 light. Hand-rolled copy of popover-surface (radius sm / shadow md instead of md / lg), so a popover-surface change will NOT reach it.
Same pair as @mixin elevate(md) but written by hand. shadow-md peak composite on page = 1.26.
Data mark (2px polyline), de-emphasised. Light #b8b2a9 (L*72.8) = 2.10 on white. It is the data, not an edge.

Marks the current period by being darker than the base: light #008289 L*49.2 vs base L*72.8 (2.19); dark #4cc7d1 L*74.2 vs #999389 L*61.2 (only 1.51). The lightness gap IS the signal; keep it whatever the hue.

uses.declaration: (no own edge; inherits .sb-modal: border: none; box-shadow: shadow(xl); ::backdrop scrim)
uses.note: Follows whatever Modal becomes.
Search row from list, both on surface-raised. Light 1.16; dark 1.32.

uses.declaration: border: none; background: none; outline: none;
uses.note: Deliberately shapeless AND suppresses the focus ring on the element that holds DOM focus (role=combobox, aria-activedescendant). Overrides the base :focus-visible rule. Consequence: the highlighted option below is the only keyboard-position cue.

uses.declaration: background-color: clr(primary-subtle); color: clr(primary-text); (shape: border-radius: radius(md))
uses.note: The keyboard cursor. Fill #d2f7fb on white = 1.14 light; #003d40 on #4b463f = 1.29 dark; mostly hue. Text goes from L*22.0 to L*39.6. Must become a real lightness step or gain a non-colour cue.
Disabled shown by text colour only (#777168 L*47.9 vs text #38342f L*22.0). If body text is lightened toward a pastel, this gap closes; needs its own check.
Hint footer from list. Same measurements as __search.

uses.declaration: border: token(border-width) solid clr(border); border-radius: radius(md); background-color: clr(bg-subtle);
uses.note: Search-shaped button. Border #e3dfd9 on page = 1.24; fill #f1eeeb on page = 1.08. Remove the line and the control is gone in light mode, so it needs the shadow or a real fill step. Declared after control-reset's border: none.

uses.declaration: border-color: clr(border-strong); background-color: clr(surface); color: clr(text-muted);
uses.note: Hover only, non-essential. This is the harsh gray outline: #777168, 4.51 on page. Natural swap for a deeper soft shadow. The transition list names border-color; add box-shadow if the edge moves there.

uses.declaration: @include focus-ring; -> outline: none; &:focus-visible { outline: token(focus-ring-width) solid clr(focus-ring); outline-offset: 2px; }
uses.note: 3px ring, #008289 (L*49.2), 4.31 on page. Keyboard focus must be a lightness-distinct line; a page-coloured glow would recreate the no-edge problem. Does NOT use control-glow despite being field-shaped.

uses.declaration: @include control-reset; -> border: none; background: none; &:disabled, &[aria-disabled="true"] { cursor: not-allowed; opacity: 0.55; }
uses.note: Disabled = 55% opacity of an already pale control on a pale page. Check it still reads as present-but-off on cream.
Removes the browser's default black dialog border. Already line-free.

Hand-rolled elevate(xl). For a MODELESS drawer (dialog.show(), no backdrop) this shadow is the only separation: light fill vs page = 1.07. shadow-xl is `0 24px 48px -12px`, a downward drop with negative spread, so the panel's long vertical edge gets only the faint blurred fringe.

rgb(0 0 0 / 0.6), pure black in both modes, sized for a WCAG worst-case rule. Could become a tinted, lighter wash, but it also tells the user the page is inert, so it must stay an obvious lightness drop.
Header from scrolling body. Also the cue that content scrolls under it. Light 1.16, dark 1.32.
Action row from scrolling body. Same measurements.
Page from footer. #f1eeeb on page = 1.08, and it is the same hex as the footer's own fill, so the line is already redundant in light mode.
Separation by fill step, not line: #f1eeeb vs page #f8f7f5 = 1.08 light; #38342f vs #26231f = 1.27 dark.
Link columns from copyright row. #e3dfd9 on #f1eeeb = 1.15 light; 1.32 dark. Padding (space 6) already separates them.
The underline is a hover cue that does not depend on colour. Keep it.

uses.declaration: (none here; inherits base/_root.scss `:focus-visible { outline: token(focus-ring-width) solid clr(focus-ring); outline-offset: 2px; }`)
uses.note: Focus comes only from the global baseline rule.
Removes the browser's default dialog border. Already line-free. No header/footer dividers inside a modal, padding only.
Hand-rolled elevate(xl). The working shadow-only precedent; edge is carried mostly by the scrim behind it. Light tint rgb(38 35 31 / 0.24); dark rgb(0 0 0 / 0.576).
Same black 0.6 scrim as Drawer, plus a 3px blur. Signals modality; can be tinted but must stay a clear lightness drop.
Sticky header from page. 1.08 light, 1.27 dark. A soft downward shadow is the conventional replacement for a sticky bar.

uses.declaration: background-color: color-mix(in oklab, clr(bg), transparent 20%); backdrop-filter: blur(12px);
uses.note: Glass: same colour as the page, so at rest the bottom line is the ONLY boundary; the blur only shows when content scrolls beneath.

uses.declaration: color: clr(text); background-color: clr(bg-subtle); (shape: border-radius: radius(sm))
uses.note: No line; hover is a fill. #f1eeeb on page = 1.08. Non-essential, and text also darkens (L*38.5 to L*22.0), which is the readable half.
"You are here" is hue-only today: fill #d2f7fb vs page 1.06, vs the hover fill 1.01; text #00686d L*39.6 vs resting #5f5a52 L*38.5 = 1.04. No weight, bar or underline. Needs a non-hue cue.
No focus-ring mixin on navbar links; the global rule is their only focus indicator.

uses.declaration: @include focus-ring(-2px); -> outline: none; &:focus-visible { outline: token(focus-ring-width) solid clr(focus-ring); outline-offset: -2px; }
uses.note: INSET ring, drawn over the item's own fill, so it must contrast with the current-page fill too: #008289 vs #d2f7fb = 4.05 today.

uses.declaration: color: clr(text); background-color: clr(bg-subtle); (shape: border-radius: radius(sm))
uses.note: Fill-only hover. In the app-shell rail (bg = surface): 1.16 light, 1.00 dark (bg-subtle and surface are both #38342f, so the hover fill is invisible).
Current page. Light 1.14 on the white rail; dark #003d40 vs #38342f = 1.02 (hue-only). Text vs resting text = 1.04 light, 1.03 dark. Needs a non-hue cue.
Pinned footer from nav list. Light 1.16; dark 1.00 inside the app-shell rail (invisible today).

uses.declaration: border-block-end: token(border-width) solid clr(border-subtle); &:last-child { border-block-end: none; }
uses.note: Dense rows with 0.5rem padding; the rule is what stops them merging. Dev tool inside a Drawer (on surface-raised): 1.16 light, 1.32 dark.
Toolbar from rows.
Edited-token marker by weight plus darker text; no line. Weight is a cue that survives any palette. Keep.
Lists WCAG contrast-gate failures in danger text. Not an edge, but this whole report exists for the requirement being dropped; decide its fate with tokens/rules.ts.
Rail from main. Light #f1eeeb: 1.16 vs the rail, 1.08 vs the page. Dark: 1.00 against the rail's own fill, so the line does nothing there.
Rail by fill step: #ffffff vs page #f8f7f5 = 1.07 light; #38342f vs #26231f = 1.27 dark. In a pureSurfaces preset page and rail are both white and the line is the only edge.

uses.declaration: background-color: clr(bg); background-image: radial-gradient(... clr(primary-subtle) ...), radial-gradient(... clr(accent-subtle) ...), radial-gradient(... clr(secondary-subtle) ...);
uses.note: No edge drawn. Relevant because the .sb-card inside (molecules) sits on these tinted washes, so its soft shadow has to hold against #d2f7fb / #f9f0c4 / #ffe8ef, not just the page.

would_lose_boundary_without_a_line: .sb-command-trigger (light): fill #f1eeeb on page #f8f7f5 = 1.08; its 1px border #e3dfd9 (1.24) is the whole control shape. Dark keeps a 1.27 fill step.

.sb-navbar (sticky/glass): background is the page colour at 80% alpha, so the bottom rule is the only boundary at rest; with it gone the bar and page are one surface until something scrolls under the blur.

.sb-app-shell__sidebar (light): white rail on #f8f7f5 page = 1.07; and in any pureSurfaces preset (page = surface = white) there is nothing at all. In dark the line is ALREADY invisible (border-subtle = surface = #38342f); only the 1.27 fill step shows.
.sb-drawer__header / __footer and .sb-command__search / __footer: regions share one fill (surface-raised); without the rule nothing shows where the fixed rows end and the scrolling body begins.
.sb-sidebar__footer: same fill above and below; only the rule plus 0.75rem padding separates it. Already 1.00 in the dark rail.
.sb-token-studio__row and __toolbar: dense rows with 0.5rem padding and no fill difference; rows merge into one block without the rule.

.sb-footer and .sb-footer__meta: the top rule is the same hex as the footer fill (#f1eeeb), so removing it changes nothing in light; the meta rule (1.15) leaves only padding between link columns and the copyright row.
.sb-chart__tooltip: white tooltip over a white card. Remove the line and shadow(md) alone carries it (peak 1.26 on the page); remove both and it is text floating on the chart.

.sb-modal and .sb-drawer: already have NO line. Modal leans on the black scrim; a modeless drawer (no backdrop) leans on shadow(xl) alone with a 1.07 fill step in light. These show what shadow-only looks like today.
.sb-chart__grid / __axis: the strokes are the thing itself; removing them removes the value scale and baseline. Grid is already 1.00 on a dark surface card.
.sb-chart__swatch: never had an edge; a pale pastel series colour on cream would have no visible boundary.
.sb-command__input: by design has no border, fill or outline; only the caret and placeholder text show it exists.
Nav hover/current fills (.sb-navbar__nav a, .sb-sidebar__item): no line and fills at 1.06-1.16 light, 1.00-1.02 in the dark rail; they are bounded by hue alone.
state_or_usability_signals_that_must_sta: FOCUS, mixin-drawn: .sb-command-trigger:focus-visible (3px outline, offset 2px) and .sb-sidebar__item:focus-visible (3px, offset -2px, inset over the item's fill). Colour --sb-focus-ring #008289 L*49.2 light (4.31 on page, 4.05 on the current-page fill), #4cc7d1 L*74.2 dark (7.74). This is the one place a crisp, lightness-distinct line is the point; do not turn it into a page-coloured glow.

FOCUS, inherited: navbar brand, navbar links and footer links have no focus-ring mixin and depend entirely on base/_root.scss `:focus-visible`. Changing or removing that rule silently strips their focus indicator.
FOCUS, suppressed: .sb-command__input sets outline: none while holding DOM focus. The highlighted option is therefore the only keyboard-position cue in the palette.
ACTIVE OPTION: .sb-command__option[data-highlighted] (fill 1.14 light / 1.29 dark, mostly hue). Needs a real lightness step or a non-colour cue (weight, marker, inset bar).

CURRENT PAGE: .sb-navbar__nav a[aria-current=page] and .sb-sidebar__item[aria-current]. Hue-only today: fill vs hover fill 1.01, text vs resting text 1.04 (light); fill vs rail 1.02 (dark). The single weakest signal in scope for a colourblind reader.
HOVER (nice to have, not essential): nav/sidebar links (bg-subtle fill; 1.00 in the dark rail), command trigger (border-strong), footer links (underline, which is colour-independent and should stay).

DISABLED: .sb-command-trigger via control-reset (opacity 0.55) and .sb-command__option[aria-disabled] (text-subtle + cursor only). Both get harder to tell from enabled as body text is lightened toward a pastel; re-measure after the text colour is chosen.
MODALITY: ::backdrop scrim on modal, drawer and command palette. It may be tinted and lightened, but it must still read as the page being switched off.

CHART READING: crosshair (which x), sparkline accent vs base (current period; dark gap is only 1.51), the marker's knockout ring, and gridlines/axis. Series identity (swatch + line colour) is hue-carried; the legend labels, tooltip and the data-table twin are the non-colour path and must stay.
TOKEN STUDIO: dirty row (semibold + darker text) and the failures list (danger text only).

NOT PRESENT IN THIS SCOPE: invalid, checked, selected, switch/slider/progress/spinner/radio shapes. None are drawn in organisms or templates; they are in atoms and molecules. The only clr(primary-solid) use here is the sparkline accent.
shared_mixins_or_tokens_that_centralise_: --sb-border-subtle via clr(border-subtle): 12 of the 17 line/stroke uses in scope, 25 library-wide. Set in tokens/semantics.ts buildMode: light neutral[100] (#f1eeeb), dark neutral[900] (#38342f), which is the same step as dark surface and bg-subtle. That equality is the root of the dark-mode no-edge problem; one line fixes or breaks it everywhere.
--sb-border via clr(border): 3 in scope (chart axis, footer meta, command trigger), 18 library-wide. Light neutral[200] #e3dfd9; dark neutral[800] #4b463f, equal to dark surface-raised.

--sb-border-strong via clr(border-strong): 2 in scope (crosshair, trigger hover), 18 library-wide. Picked from neutral 500/600 to clear 3:1 (rules.ts lines 30-31). This is the token producing the harsh gray; relaxing its rule softens every strong outline at once.

token(border-width) = --sb-border-width: 1px (scales.ts static tokens): 13 uses in scope, 41 library-wide. Setting it to 0 removes every line in one move but also shifts layout by 1px per edge and removes the border that control-glow recolours on focus/invalid, so it is a blunt instrument.

shadow(xs|sm|md|lg|xl) = --sb-shadow-*: emitted by ONE function, tokens/emit.ts shadowDecls(mode, preset.shadowTint). 3 uses in scope (tooltip md, modal xl, drawer xl), 19 library-wide. Light uses the preset's single shadowTint (sorbet: ramps.sand[950], rgb(38 35 31)); dark ignores the tint and uses #000 at 2.4x alpha. Two limits for the owner's wish: (a) one tint per preset cannot be 'similarly coloured' to each surface, which needs a per-surface shadow colour (e.g. a --sb-shadow-color custom property the tokens consume, overridable per component); (b) every level is a y-offset drop with negative spread, so none can stand in for a border; that needs a zero-offset spread/blur layer added to the scale.

@mixin elevate($level) (background surface-raised + shadow): the obvious single place for raised surfaces, but it has exactly ONE caller library-wide (segmented-control). Modal, drawer and chart tooltip write the same pair by hand, so they must be moved onto it before it centralises anything.

@mixin popover-surface (1px border-subtle + radius md + surface-raised + shadow lg): 5 callers (popover, color-input, calendar, combobox, menu), none in organisms/templates. The chart tooltip duplicates it by hand with different radius/shadow.

@mixin control-glow($color) (border-color + 2px halo of the same colour at 30% opacity): already the house's soft-same-colour-shadow idiom and takes `danger` for invalid. 8 callers, none in scope; the command trigger is field-shaped but uses the outline ring instead.

@mixin focus-ring / focus-ring-style plus base/_root.scss `:focus-visible`: three definitions of one ring, all reading --sb-focus-ring and --sb-focus-ring-width (3px). In scope: command trigger (offset 2px), sidebar item (offset -2px). The colour is chosen in semantics.ts from the primary ramp for 3:1 on page and surface.
@mixin control-reset: the single definition of the button-like disabled look (opacity 0.55, not-allowed) and of `border: none` for controls. 1 caller in scope (command trigger), ~25 library-wide.

NO MIXIN EXISTS for a divider or a container edge. All 13 border-block-*/border-inline-*/border lines in scope are hand-written copies of `token(border-width) solid clr(border-subtle|border)`. Changing edges in one place means either doing it at token level, or introducing an edge/divider mixin (or an --sb-edge-shadow token) and swapping these 13 call sites: chart tooltip; command search, footer, trigger; drawer header, footer; footer top, meta; navbar; sidebar footer; token-studio row, toolbar; app-shell sidebar.
--sb-scrim: semantics.ts, withAlpha('#000000', 0.6) in both modes, gated by rules.ts (on-scrim / on-scrim-muted at 4.5:1 worst case). One place for modal, drawer and command-palette backdrops.

Fill-step tokens that carry separation where no line exists: --sb-bg (#f8f7f5), --sb-bg-subtle (#f1eeeb), --sb-surface and --sb-surface-raised (both #ffffff in light, so 'raised' has no fill step there and depends wholly on shadow), --sb-surface-sunken.

State-fill tokens: --sb-primary-subtle + --sb-primary-text drive current-page (navbar, sidebar) and the command highlight; fixing the hue-only problem there is one token pair plus a non-colour cue in three selectors.

--sb-primary-solid (and the unused-in-CSS secondary-solid / accent-solid): the shape-maker token, defined for WCAG 1.4.11 3:1 (rules.ts lines 55-60). In scope only the sparkline accent uses it; 23 uses library-wide in atoms/molecules.

Chart tokens: --sb-chart-muted and --sb-chart-1..8 (tokens/charts.ts, gated at 3:1 light / 2.25 dark in rules.ts lines 93-100). Swatches and series strokes take them inline from the components, not from SCSS.

tokens/rules.ts RULES: the WCAG gate that fails the build. Every softened token above will trip it until the rules are rewritten for the new goal (text legibility only); it is the control point for what 'legible' is allowed to mean.

map:edges-molecules.scope: molecules (25 partials in src/styles/molecules) + abstracts/_mixins.scss, _tokens.scss, _generated.scss, _glyphs.scss, _index.scss. Read-only; nothing was changed. Colour values are read from the existing built file packages/design-system/dist/themes/sorbet.css (built 2026-09-27, same timestamp as abstracts/_generated.scss); ratios and L* computed from those hexes.
map:edges-molecules.summary:
Terms used: "contrast ratio" = lightness gap between two colours (1:1 identical, 21:1 black on white). "L*" = perceived lightness, 0 black to 100 white. For a colourblind reader a state is only reliable if L*, thickness or shape changes; a hue swap at the same L* is not.

TAKEAWAYS (most consequential first)
- The harsh grey outline is ONE token: border-strong #777168 (L* 47.9, 4.83:1 on white). In molecules it draws 4 control frames (combobox field, date-range control, input-group addon, dropzone dashed zone) plus the calendar "today" ring and the carousel dots. Softening those 6 uses (and the 3 matching atoms) removes every hard grey line in scope.
- Container edges are already nearly invisible in light mode, so a soft shadow there is low-risk: border-subtle #f1eeeb is 1.16:1 on white and 1.08:1 on the page bg #f8f7f5; a white surface on the page is itself only 1.07:1. Accordion, table wrapper, flat card, inline calendar and dropzone file row have a border and NO shadow, so they are the ones that vanish if the line is simply deleted.
- The dark-mode "no edges" problem has a measurable cause: dark border-subtle (#38342f) is the SAME hex as dark surface (1.00:1), shadows are pure black over an L* 13.9 page (invisible), and card--sunken equals the page bg (1.00:1). Separation there rests only on fill steps of 1.27:1 to 1.67:1.
- Six state signals are hue-only today, so they are already unreliable for the owner regardless of WCAG, and must gain a lightness/thickness/shape cue rather than be softened: invalid border (danger L* 45.2 vs resting border L* 47.9, 1.10:1 apart), control-glow's border swap on focus (L* 47.9 to 49.2), dropzone hover and drag-over border (1.05:1 apart), toast tone stripe (success/danger/info L* 49.9/45.2/47.6), carousel current-dot colour (its 2.5x width is what actually carries it), alert tone fills (all four within L* 94.0 to 95.1).
- Weak fill-only states at 1.14 to 1.30:1 that a paler palette will erase unless redesigned: menu item keyboard focus (ring explicitly removed, fill 1.16:1, identical to hover), combobox highlighted option (1.14:1), pagination current page (1.30:1, no weight change), calendar selected day (1.30:1) and in-range band (1.14:1).
- Text-control focus is the weakest focus cue in scope: a 2px halo at 30% alpha (#b3dadc, 1.50:1 on white). The 3px solid focus ring elsewhere is 4.61:1.
- Centralisation is thin. popover-surface is the only shared container edge (3 molecule users). The same container border is hand-written 5 more times, the input frame 3 times in molecules (plus 3 atoms), dividers 4 times, and elevate() has exactly 1 user in the whole stylesheet. Shadows have a single neutral tint per preset, so "similarly coloured shadow" needs a new token or mixin, not a value tweak.

MECHANICAL CONSTRAINTS FOR THE REFACTOR
- box-shadow slot contention: control-glow writes box-shadow, so a soft-edge shadow on the same element must be composed into one declaration or focus will delete the edge.
- input-group joins neighbours with border-inline-start/end: none; that trick has no equivalent for shadows.
- Clipping parents cut off children's outer shadows: .sb-card (overflow hidden), .sb-table-wrap, .sb-tabs__list, .sb-carousel__viewport (overflow-x auto), .sb-combobox__panel (overflow-y auto), .sb-marquee (overflow hidden). Existing negative focus offsets (-2px, -4px) are there for the same reason.
- color-transition does not transition box-shadow.
- tokens/rules.ts is the WCAG gate (border-strong, focus-ring and the -solid trio must be 3:1 or more); a pastel value fails the build until that file changes with it.

NO EDGES AT ALL: _section, _wizard, _field (text only), _stat (glyphs only), _empty-state (one decorative disc), _breadcrumb (text separators), base _description-list.

Entry count: 104, one per edge-drawing declaration, with line numbers.

uses.note: 3px solid ring. Light #008289 L* 49.2, 4.61:1 on white, 4.31:1 on bg; dark #4cc7d1 6.11:1. Direct users: card--interactive, dropzone zone, marquee toggle. Keyboard position must stay a hard, high-lightness-gap ring.

17 includes in molecules, offsets 0 / 2px / 3px / -2px / -4px. Negative offsets exist because a scrolling or pill parent would clip an outer ring. Same ring is also set globally in base/_root.scss L42-44.

uses.declaration: border-color: clr($color); box-shadow: 0 0 0 calc(token(focus-ring-width) - 1px) color-mix(in oklab, clr($color), transparent 70%)
uses.note: Focus and invalid-focus for input-shaped frames (4 users: atoms input, number-input; molecules combobox field, date-range control). Border swap is hue-only (L* 47.9 to 49.2). ALREADY BOUNDARYLESS TODAY, no line to remove: .sb-card--sunken in dark mode (surface-sunken #26231f == page bg #26231f, 1.00:1); .sb-segmented and .sb-tabs--pills tracks inside a card in dark mode (bg-subtle == surface, 1.00:1); .sb-alert inside a card in dark mode (tone fills 1.01 to 1.06:1 vs surface); every border-subtle container in dark mode (border-subtle #38342f == surface #38342f).

FOCUS, text controls (control-glow): combobox field and date-range control. Border swap is hue-only (L* 47.9 to 49.2); the visible part is a 2px halo at 30% alpha, #b3dadc, 1.50:1 on white. Already weak; a soft-edge shadow sharing the box-shadow property must not overwrite it.
FOCUS, menu item (molecules/_menu.scss L36-40): outline: none, replaced by a bg-subtle fill at 1.16:1 that is identical to hover. Weakest keyboard cue in scope.
KEYBOARD POSITION in combobox list ([data-highlighted], L131): primary-subtle fill 1.14:1 plus text colour.

INVALID: combobox field and date-range control swap the 1px border to danger #cb2c31, L* 45.2 against a resting L* 47.9 (1.10:1 apart): hue-only, not reliable for the owner today. The dependable invalid cue is .sb-field__error text appearing and the hint hiding (molecules/_field.scss L27-44). Dropzone error is text too (L87).

SELECTED / CHECKED / CURRENT: calendar selected day (fill 1.30:1 + semibold), in-range band (1.14:1 + squared corners), today ring (4.83:1 + bold); combobox selected tick (shape); pagination current page (fill 1.30:1 on white, 1.21:1 on page, no weight change); segmented checked (raised white pill + shadow-sm + semibold); tabs selected (2.5px bar, 4.31:1 on page); tabs--pills selected (pill + shadow, no weight change); stepper complete (ring + fill + rail) and current (ring colour only); carousel current dot (2.5x width; its colour change is 1.05:1); table aria-sort (arrow shape + opacity 0.4 to 1); accordion open (caret rotation).

Opacity on an already pale pastel will read weaker than it does today.

HOVER-ONLY cues: card--interactive (shadow-lg + border + 2px lift), carousel arrow (border L* 89.0 to 47.9), table --hover row (same colour as --striped rows, so invisible on even rows), icon buttons (bg-subtle fill).
shared_mixins_or_tokens_that_centralise_: popover-surface mixin (abstracts/_mixins.scss L176-186): 1px border-subtle + surface-raised + shadow(lg). One edit changes menu, combobox panel, calendar (and atoms popover, color-input). Toast copies the same chrome by hand and would need converting to use it.

elevate($level) mixin (abstracts/_mixins.scss L90-93): surface-raised + shadow. Only ONE user in the entire stylesheet (segmented checked option). Card, card--raised, tabs--pills selected, marquee toggle and toast all hand-write the same pair. The obvious single place for a soft-edge definition.

control-glow($color) mixin (abstracts/_mixins.scss L100-103): the focus and invalid-focus chrome for every input-shaped frame (atoms input, number-input; molecules combobox field, date-range control).
focus-ring / focus-ring-style mixins (abstracts/_mixins.scss L29-42) plus the global :focus-visible rule in base/_root.scss L42-44; driven by --sb-focus-ring and --sb-focus-ring-width (3px).
control-reset mixin (abstracts/_mixins.scss L73-87): border: none and the shared disabled opacity 0.55.
color-transition mixin (abstracts/_mixins.scss L111-116): transitions color, background-color, border-color; would need box-shadow added once edges are shadows.

Colour tokens --sb-border (#e3dfd9), --sb-border-subtle (#f1eeeb), --sb-border-strong (#777168), derived in packages/design-system/src/tokens/semantics.ts L200-202 (light) and L216-218 (dark). Changing border-strong alone softens every control frame, the dropzone dashes, the today ring and the carousel dots at once (it is also used as a FILL for the dots, and --sb-border as a fill for the stepper rail).

Shadow tokens --sb-shadow-xs..xl, generated in packages/design-system/src/tokens/emit.ts shadowDecls L34-43 from ONE shadowTint per preset (sorbet: sand-950 #26231f at 5 to 24% alpha in light; pure black at 2.4x alpha in dark). The shadow() accessor takes only a size, so a shadow coloured like its surface needs a new token family or a mixin that takes a colour.

Width tokens --sb-border-width (1px) and --sb-border-width-thick (2px) in tokens/scales.ts L113-115. Exceptions written as raw values: toast tone stripe 3px, tabs bar 2.5px, the 2px chevron/caret/tick borders.

Surface tokens --sb-surface, --sb-surface-raised, --sb-surface-sunken, --sb-bg-subtle (semantics.ts L180-185 light, L204-208 dark): fill steps are the other half of separation and are where dark mode collapses (bg-subtle == surface, surface-sunken == bg).

-solid trio (--sb-primary-solid etc., semantics.ts L147 and L249-251): the 'shape-maker' colour used in scope for the tabs bar, stepper ring and rail, carousel current dot, dropzone hover/drag-over and icon.

tokens/rules.ts (L28-33, L55-60): the contrast gate that requires border-strong, focus-ring and the -solid colours to reach 3:1. It must change in the same commit as the palette or the token build fails.

NOT centralised (hand copies an orchestrator would have to touch one by one, or first fold into a mixin): container border 'border: token(border-width) solid clr(border-subtle)' in accordion, card, dropzone file, table wrap, toast; input frame 'border: token(border-width) solid clr(border-strong)' in combobox field, date-range control, input-group addon (plus atoms input, number-input, color-input); 1px dividers in description-list, menu separator, table cells, tabs list; icon-button hover fill (bg-subtle) in 7 places; disabled opacity in 5 places with 3 different values.

map:edges-atoms.scope: Edges and separation in sorbet's stylesheet for atoms, base, layout and the shared abstracts: all 41 .scss files under packages/design-system/src/styles/{atoms,base,layout,abstracts}, read in full. Also read for context (not inventoried): styles/index.scss (layer order), src/tokens/{semantics,rules,emit,presets}.ts (where the edge tokens get their values and the contrast gate lives), dist/themes/sorbet.css and dist/css/sorbet.css (built values). Molecules, organisms and templates are OUT of this scope (cards, tables, modals, tabs, menus live there). Read-only: nothing written, built or checked out; hex and ratio figures were computed in memory from src/tokens with the repo's own contrast() for the current `sorbet` preset.
map:edges-atoms.summary:
TAKEAWAYS (most important first)

- Numbers below are contrast ratios: how different two colours are in lightness, 1.00:1 = identical, 21:1 = black on white. Hue plays no part in the figure, which is why it is the right yardstick for a colourblind reader. All measured on the current `sorbet` preset.

- The harsh lines come from exactly two token families, and both are held dark by the build gate (src/tokens/rules.ts), not by the SCSS:
  - `border-strong` = #777168 (4.51:1 on page #f8f7f5, 4.83:1 on white). It is the SAME hex as `text-subtle`. Draws every text field, select, number input, checkbox/radio box, outline button, eyedropper.
  - `primary-solid` #008289 (4.31:1), `secondary-solid` #c42876 (5.01:1), `accent-solid` #8a6f00 (4.50:1). They ring the pastel buttons (fills are only 1.21-1.26:1 against the page) and fill every unlabelled affordance.

- The soft edge the owner describes ALREADY EXISTS in one place: atoms/_button.scss L49-80. A `--edge` knob plus three hue-matched shadows (`--shadow-rest/hover/press`, color-mix of --edge at 22%/12%, 26%/14%). Today it is garnish on a 1px 3:1 border. Promoting it to a shared abstracts mixin and dropping the border is the shortest path. `flat-elevation` (same file) is its off-switch.

- Sorbet already ships many shapes with NO line and near-zero lightness separation: soft button 1.06:1, badge 1.08:1, progress track 1.08:1, skeleton, prose pre/code, avatar 1.09:1, chip border 1.24-1.33:1, popover border 1.16:1. So "elements need not separate from the background" is already half true; the WCAG cost is concentrated in controls, not containers.

- Three state signals are hue-only today and will NOT survive a pastel retune unless redesigned (these are real defects for a colourblind user, not style preferences):
  - Switch on vs off track: #008289 vs #777168 = 1.05:1. Only the thumb position tells them apart.
  - Invalid field border vs normal: #cb2c31 vs #777168 = 1.10:1.
  - Text selection: #d2f7fb on page = 1.06:1.

- Dark mode constraint (the "NO emphasis on edges" problem, measured): `border` #4b463f == `surface-raised` #4b463f (1.00:1) and `border-subtle` #38342f == `surface` == `bg-subtle` (1.00:1). Shadows there are hard-coded black (emit.ts L34-44) on a #26231f page, so they cannot separate anything. A shadow can only darken; in dark the soft edge has to be a LIGHTER tinted rim or glow. The rule needs a per-mode definition.

- Layout primitives draw nothing: center, cluster, container, grid, masonry, split, stack have no edge of any kind. frame only strips the iframe border; layer only paints the image scrim. base/_reset and base/_utilities draw nothing.

- Shared levers exist for most of it: 3 border tokens, 3 -solid tokens, 5 shadow tokens, `focus-ring` (31 includes in 23 partials), `control-glow` (8), `popover-surface` (5), `control-surface` (input/textarea/select). `elevate` has ONE consumer and none in this scope.

- Forced-colors mode (Windows high contrast) strips box-shadow and keeps borders; there is no forced-colors rule anywhere in the stylesheet. Pattern to keep: a `transparent` border stays in place (invisible normally, drawn by the OS in forced colours). The flat button variants already do this.

- If the text colour is lightened, three things move with it: tooltip background (`clr(text)`), slider track (20% of currentColor), colour-slider thumb ring (`clr(text)`).

EXISTING DEFECTS FOUND IN PASSING (wrong, not different)
- `@include focus-ring(2)` / `(1)` in atoms/_color-input.scss pass unitless numbers; built CSS contains invalid `outline-offset: 2` (x2) and `outline-offset: 1` (x1), so the base 2px applies by accident.
- `.sb-divider--strong` has no effect on the labelled `div` flavour (its lines are pseudo-elements with their own colour).
- Button loading spinner is hard-wired to `on-primary` on every variant, including outline/ghost/link where no primary fill is behind it.
- Progress tone bars use the pale fill tokens: secondary 1.17:1, accent 1.14:1, warning 1.87:1 against the track.
- Checkbox tick/radio dot paint `on-primary` (#26231f) on `primary-solid` (#008289) = 3.39:1; rules.ts checks on-primary against `primary`, never against `primary-solid`.
- The focus ring is written three times: the mixin, base/_root.scss L42-45, and color-input L263-266 (where it means "selected", so selected and focused look identical).

state_or_usability_signals_that_must_sta: FOCUS - outline 3px #008289 (4.31:1 on page, 4.61:1 on white) at 2px offset, from mixin focus-ring (31 includes) and the global :focus-visible in base/_root.scss. Text fields swap it for control-glow (border recolour + 2px halo at 30%). Number input shows it on the wrapper only. Deliberately removed on .sb-popover. Must remain a crisp, high-lightness-contrast ring; it is the one place a hard line is the correct answer.

INVALID - border-color: clr(danger) on input, textarea, select, number-input. #cb2c31 vs the normal #777168 is 1.10:1, i.e. hue only. Already not readable by lightness; needs a non-hue cue at the control (thicker edge, icon, or a clear lightness jump), not just the message text.

CHECKED - checkbox/radio: white box becomes a #008289 fill (4.61:1) with a tick or dot; indeterminate shows a dash. Tick on fill is 3.39:1 and unchecked by the build gate. The fill must stay dark enough to carry the tick, or the tick colour must change with it.

SWITCH ON/OFF - track #008289 vs #777168 = 1.05:1 (hue only); thumb position is the only reliable cue. Whatever the palette does, on and off need different LIGHTNESS, and the white thumb needs a track it can be seen on.

SELECTED - chip: border jumps 1.33:1 to 4.61:1, plus tinted fill (1.14:1), primary-text colour and weight 500. Colour swatch-chip: draws the focus ring for aria-pressed, so selected and focused are indistinguishable.

DISABLED - opacity 0.55 (control-reset consumers, switch, slider, colour swatch); text fields: bg-subtle fill + text-subtle text; checkbox/radio: bg-subtle fill + weak border; choice label: text-subtle; number-input steps: text-subtle with opacity 1. On a pastel palette, re-measure that 55% of a pastel still reads as 'present but off'.

UNLABELLED AFFORDANCES (no text to fall back on) - slider thumb and track, progress bar vs track, spinner arc, button loading arc, rating filled vs empty stars (2.24:1, filled is the lighter), select caret, close X and other mask glyphs, icon tints (warning icon 2.02:1 today), badge dot, colour-area and colour-slider thumbs, FAB (icon-only). These are what `primary-solid` exists for; each needs a lightness step against what it sits on, though that step does not have to be 3:1.

HOVER - bg-subtle wash on ghost/outline button, chip, eyedropper, number steps (1.08-1.16:1, weak today); solid button: deeper fill + wider shadow + 1px lift; FAB: shadow lg to xl. Lift and shadow growth are the non-hue cues worth keeping.
PRESS - shadow tighter than rest plus scale(0.97); removed under prefers-reduced-motion.
LINKS - underline on a:not([class]) and .sb-button--link. Keep: it is what distinguishes a link without relying on colour.
REQUIRED - the ' *' glyph on .sb-label[data-required]; the character carries it, not the red.
TEXT SELECTION - ::selection is primary-subtle at 1.06:1 vs page; hue-only today.
TEXT OVER IMAGES - the .sb-layer scrim wash and its on-scrim text pair; a legibility device, independent of the palette.
TOOLTIP - background is the text colour; if text is lightened the tooltip and its label contrast change with it.

FORCED-COLORS (Windows high contrast) - box-shadows are stripped, borders are kept, and the stylesheet has no forced-colors rules. If edges become shadows, keep a `transparent` border on controls so the OS still draws one. The flat button variants already do this.

ARIA / SEMANTICS - nothing in this inventory touches roles or labels; state selectors key off :checked, :disabled, :user-invalid, [aria-invalid], [aria-disabled], [aria-pressed], [data-selected]. A visual refactor that keeps those selectors leaves screen-reader behaviour unchanged.

dark_edge_problem.what_happened:
WHAT THE OWNER MEANS: the September 2026 episode on the imagefeed admin page (the lab's densest sorbet UI: ~500 controls across 33 cards, four levels of nesting) in dark mode. The text was fine; the containers had no visible boundaries. The owner's phrase 'NO emphasis on edges' echoes the diagnosis given at the time ('Nothing has edges').

Terms used below: 'dE' = how far apart two colours look (OKLab distance x100 from the kit; under ~5 is hard to tell apart, 10+ is clearly different). 'WCAG ratio' = the retired contrast rule (1:1 identical, 21:1 black on white). 'L' = OKLCH lightness, 0 to 1.

TIMELINE (transcript times are UTC):
- 2026-07-19 and 2026-07-23, inside sorbet itself: two early symptoms of the same root cause, each patched per component. PR #27: the slider track was invisible in dark because the `border` token equals `surface-raised`. PR #38: the selected pill was invisible because `surface` equals `bg-subtle`.
- 2026-09-09: first complaint on the imagefeed admin (noir preset, forced dark): buttons 'getting lost as they just look like more txt'. Treated as an app-level button-variant problem.
- 2026-09-11 01:58Z: 'Everything is very hard to discern' in dark mode. Measured that night: body text 13.5:1 on the page (fine), but card vs page 1.26:1, border vs its own card 1.32:1, raised vs card 1.32:1, subtle text on a card 4.05:1. A stopgap override went into imagefeed's admin.html (imagefeed commit baf9d09).
- 2026-09-11 19:12Z: owner asked to switch the theme to sorbet instead of fixing noir. The switch proved the collapse is not a noir bug: sorbet's dark block measures the same to two decimals (1.27 / 1.32 / 4.05). The fault is the dark branch shared by all five presets (imagefeed commit 64bd4eb).
- 2026-09-11 19:22Z: owner: 'the edges are still an issue yeah so let's table that.' Minutes later they asked for light mode and said 'much better'. Light became imagefeed's default.
- 2026-09-27: for the buylist app: 'Dark mode in general needs some work so lets just use light mode.'

ROOT CAUSE IN CODE (/Users/homelab/code/sorbet/packages/design-system/src/tokens/semantics.ts, dark branch, unchanged since the first commit ac4662c of 2026-07-15):
- page `bg` = neutral-950, `surface` = `bg-subtle` = `border-subtle` = neutral-900, `surface-raised` = `border` = neutral-800. Three adjacent steps of one ramp are shared between fills and the borders meant to outline them.
- So a `.sb-card` (fill `surface`, 1px `border-subtle`, `shadow-sm`) has a border identical to its own fill (dE 0), sits dE 6.9 from the page (WCAG 1.27), and casts a black shadow onto a near-black page (at most dE 3.4).
- The build gate never caught it because /Users/homelab/code/sorbet/packages/design-system/src/tokens/rules.ts has no rule for surface-vs-page or border-vs-surface; it only checks text and `border-strong`. A page with no edges passes the WCAG contract.
dark_edge_problem.how_it_was_fixed:
It was NOT fixed in sorbet. It was patched around three times and then avoided.

- sorbet PR #27 (2026-07-19): slider track drawn as 20% of the current text colour instead of the `border` token (atoms/_slider.scss).
- sorbet PR #38 (2026-07-23): selected segment / tab pill moved to `surface-raised` plus `shadow-sm` (molecules/_segmented-control.scss, molecules/_tabs.scss).
- imagefeed app-level stopgap, STILL LIVE at /Users/homelab/homelab/imagefeed/site/admin.html lines 36-66: `:root[data-theme="dark"] { --sb-surface: #413d38; --sb-surface-raised: #54504c; --sb-border: #8a8782; --sb-text-subtle: #aca79e }`. Measured with the kit: surface vs page dE 10.4 (WCAG 1.45); border vs card dE 26.2 (3.01:1). In other words the 'fix' was a hard mid-grey outline solved to hit WCAG's 3:1, which is exactly the look the owner now says they do not want.
- Avoidance: imagefeed defaults to light since 2026-09-11 and its theme toggle was moved off the viewer on 2026-09-12; buylist is pinned to light (2026-09-27).
- Upstream state: `git log -S` on the dark surface/border lines and on the shadow multiplier returns only the first commit. No sorbet issue or PR was ever opened for the dark ramp. pantry, wallpaper-admin and musicdisco still load noir with no override (pantry follows the OS setting), so they have the collapse whenever the device is in dark mode.
dark_edge_problem.lesson_for_soft_edges:
1. A SHADOW DARKER THAN THE PAGE CANNOT MAKE AN EDGE IN DARK MODE. Upper bound measured with the kit (shadow colour at full alpha over the dark page #26231f; a blurred shadow is always weaker): shadow-sm dE 3.4, md 4.3, lg 5.8, xl 8.9. The same sm shadow on the light page #f8f7f5 reaches dE 5.7 (md 7.6, lg 10.3). 'A soft shadow gives the separation' works on a light page and fails on a dark one by construction, because there is almost no room below L 0.258 to get darker.

2. WHAT DOES SEPARATE ON DARK, MEASURED:
- A real lightness step for the fill. Current surface #38342f on page #26231f is dE 6.9; the stopgap's #413d38 is dE 10.4; sorbet's own sand-800 #4b463f is dE 13.9.
- A halo that is LIGHTER than the page and tinted like the element (a glow, not a shadow). sorbet already ships this on filled buttons (PR #108, atoms/_button.scss: two box-shadow layers at 22% and 12% of the button's own colour). In dark that composites to #2e4746 for the #4cc7d1 button = dE 12.4 from the page (protan 13.3, deutan 11.8, tritan 12.7); #ff85b6 at 22% = dE 12.9; #d4b000 at 22% = dE 13.3. A neutral light edge (#f1eeeb at 12% to 16% over surface #38342f) gives dE 8.4 to 11.3.
- All of these are lightness differences, so they hold under every colour-blindness simulation (the numbers barely move).

3. THE RULE TO CARRY: an element, or its halo, must differ from what it sits on by roughly dE 10 or more in LIGHTNESS, in both modes. In light mode the halo is darker / more saturated than the page; in dark mode it must be lighter than the page. The direction flips with the mode; a single shadow recipe multiplied by 2.4 (what emit.ts does today) does not.

4. NEVER LET AN EDGE TOKEN EQUAL THE FILL IT OUTLINES. Today in dark `border-subtle` == `surface` and `border` == `surface-raised` (dE 0 each).

5. GATE IT, OR IT COMES BACK. The collapse shipped because the contract only measured text. Whatever replaces the WCAG gate needs a separation check (surface-or-its-halo vs page, raised vs surface, normal vision and the three simulations). This problem surfaced three times (slider, pill, cards) and was fixed locally each time; a derived check is what stops a fourth.

6. NESTING NEEDS MORE THAN ONE STEP. The page that broke had four levels (page, card, group, control). One dE-7 step per level is invisible; the model needs page -> surface -> raised each clearly apart, or edges carried by halos.

7. LIGHT MODE HAS THE SAME WEAKNESS IN MILDER FORM. Today a light card is #ffffff on #f8f7f5 (dE 2.4), with a border-subtle of dE 5.0 against its own fill; the neutral shadow (at most dE 5.7) is doing nearly all the work. And the pale aqua button fill #adedf3 against the page is dE 9.7 for normal vision but 5.0 under protan simulation, so the tinted falloff (dE 10.4 normal, 8.8 protan at 22%) is what actually carries that shape.

map:history.dark_mode_today:
Source: /Users/homelab/code/sorbet/packages/design-system/dist/themes/sorbet.css, the [data-theme="dark"] block (repeated under prefers-color-scheme). All numbers from the kit. Everything here comes from one warm-grey ramp ('sand', hue ~78, chroma at most 0.016), so results are the same under protan/deutan/tritan simulation.

FILLS (three lightness steps, about 0.07 L apart)
- bg (page) #26231f, L 0.258. surface-sunken is the same hex.
- surface #38342f, L 0.327. bg-subtle is the same hex.
- surface-raised #4b463f, L 0.397.
- surface vs page: dE 6.9, WCAG 1.27, APCA 0 (just over the 'hard to tell apart' line).
- raised vs surface: dE 6.9, WCAG 1.32. raised vs page: dE 13.9, WCAG 1.67.

BORDERS
- border-subtle #38342f = the surface hex. On a card: dE 0 (invisible). On the page: dE 6.9.
- border #4b463f = the surface-raised hex. On surface: dE 6.9. On a raised surface: dE 0. On the page: dE 13.9.
- border-strong #999389 (L 0.665; the same hex as text-subtle). dE 40.8 on page (5.13:1), 33.8 on surface (4.05:1), 26.9 on raised (3.07:1). This is the only visible edge token, and it is a hard light-grey line (it outlines inputs, checkboxes, the outline button).

SHADOWS (emit.ts shadowDecls)
- Dark mode ignores the preset's shadow tint and uses pure black #000000 at min(light alpha x 2.4, 0.7): xs 0.144; sm 0.216 + 0.12; md 0.288 + 0.144; lg 0.384 + 0.144; xl 0.576. Offsets and blur are identical to light.
- Most a shadow can differ from the page (full alpha, no blur): xs dE 2.1, sm 3.4, md 4.3, lg 5.8, xl 8.9. Over a surface: sm 4.5, lg 8.3. Real blurred shadows are weaker. For comparison the light-mode set (tint #26231f at 0.06 to 0.24 on #f8f7f5) reaches 3.9 / 5.7 / 7.6 / 10.3 / 15.5.

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR COMPONENTS
- Card (.sb-card): fill surface + 1px border-subtle + shadow-sm = border dE 0, fill dE 6.9 from the page, shadow at most 3.4. No edge.
- Card --raised: no border, shadow-md (at most 4.3), fill still `surface`.
- Popover / menu: fill surface-raised, border border-subtle (darker than the popover itself, dE 6.9), shadow-lg. Reads because raised vs page is dE 13.9.
- Inputs: 1px border-strong #999389 on surface, 4.05:1.

TEXT (not the problem)
- text #f1eeeb: 13.53:1 on page (APCA Lc -94.4), 10.69:1 on surface (Lc -90.8), 8.09:1 on raised.
- text-muted #d2cdc5 on surface: 7.81:1, Lc -70.3.
- text-subtle #999389: 5.13:1 on page, 4.05:1 on surface (Lc -38.1), 3.07:1 on raised (Lc -32.5). This is the one weak text token.

BRAND FILLS (already 'pale on dark', never split)
- primary #4cc7d1, secondary #ff85b6, accent #d4b000; each `-solid` equals its fill; label colour on all three is #26231f (7.74 / 6.91 / 7.46:1).
- Fill vs page: dE 52 to 53. Filled controls are clearly separated; it is the containers that are not.
- The button's hue-matched falloff (22% and 12% of its own colour) composites to a glow LIGHTER than the page: #2e4746 for primary = dE 12.4 from the page. This is the only soft edge in dark mode that currently works.

map:history.summary:
Terms: 'dE' = how far apart two colours look (kit's OKLab distance x100; under ~5 hard to tell apart, 10+ clearly different). 'APCA Lc' = perceptual lightness-contrast score (0 invisible, ~106 black on white; 75 body text, 60 labels, 30 floor). 'WCAG ratio' = the rule being retired. 'L' / 'C' = OKLCH lightness (0 to 1) and colourfulness.

TAKEAWAYS

1. The 'dark mode problem' is found and documented. On 2026-09-10/11 the imagefeed admin in dark mode was 'very hard to discern'. Measurement showed text was fine and the containers had no boundaries: card vs page 1.27:1 (dE 6.9), card border vs its own card dE 0. Owner on 2026-09-11: 'the edges are still an issue yeah so let's table that.'

2. It was never fixed in sorbet. The dark surface/border lines in semantics.ts are unchanged since the first commit (2026-07-15). There are two per-component patches in sorbet (PRs #27, #38), one app-local override still live in imagefeed (a hard 3:1 grey border, #8a8782), and since then every app has simply been run in light mode.

3. Root cause: in dark, borders reuse the fill hexes (border-subtle == surface, border == surface-raised) and shadows are black on a near-black page. The WCAG gate passed it because it only measured text.

4. Lesson for the soft-edge model: a shadow darker than the page cannot make an edge in dark mode (at most dE 3.4 for shadow-sm, 5.8 for lg). What works, measured: a real lightness step for the surface (dE 10+), and a halo LIGHTER than the page tinted like the element. sorbet already has that recipe on filled buttons from PR #108 (22% + 12% of the element's colour): dE 10.4 from the page in light, 12.4 in dark, and it survives all three colour-blindness simulations. Extending that recipe to cards and inputs, plus a build check on separation, is the direct fix.

5. WCAG compromises catalogued: 13 items with hexes and numbers. The most visible in the light theme are (a) deep `-solid` colours on every checkbox / switch / slider / tab (#008289, #c42876, #8a6f00); (b) a hard 1px deep outline on every pastel button; (c) a mid-grey #777168 outline on every input; (d) near-black neutral text (#38342f, Lc 93.4, about 18 Lc above the body-text guideline) and near-black labels (#26231f) on every pastel fill; (e) deep coloured text and links (#00686d, #c42876, #6f5800); (f) vivid status colours with white text; (g) deep chart colours.

FINDINGS NOBODY ASKED FOR BUT THAT CHANGE THE WORK

- The pastels are separated by hue alone, which is the one thing the owner cannot rely on. All three fills sit at L 0.905 to 0.906. Aqua #adedf3 vs pink #ffd2e1 is dE 11.5 for normal vision but 4.4 (protan) and 3.2 (deutan). This comes from the equal-lightness ramp design (ramps.ts), a contrast-safety choice. A palette for this owner should stagger the lightness of pink, blue, lilac and yellow, not only their hue.
- The 'warm cream' page is not cream today: #f8f7f5 measures C 0.003 (essentially neutral off-white) and cards are pure #ffffff, dE 2.4 from the page. Not WCAG-forced; it is the neutral ramp's chroma curve.
- The checkbox tick (#26231f on #008289) is Lc 29.2, the weakest pairing in the theme, a side effect of the split.
- The focus ring is the one 'compromise' that also serves keyboard use; keep it clearly visible.
- 'Accessibility from a usage perspective' is currently untested: sorbet issue #85 (open) records zero behavioural or ARIA tests; the only enforced half of the contract is colour.
- A stored memory now contradicts the request: /Users/homelab/homelab/claude-memory/sorbet-design-system.md says 'the gates are the point of the project, not an obstacle to it'. Today's request retires that premise; the note should be superseded when the refactor lands.

LIMITS

- Transcripts on this machine start 2026-09-03, so the owner's words from the August pastel work (PRs #103, #108) are second-hand, quoted from PR text an agent wrote.
- The owner's colour-blindness type is still unrecorded; every number is given for normal vision and all three simulations.
- Read-only: nothing was changed. Two helper scripts were written to the scratchpad only (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-homelab/06652a5c-23e2-4a00-8579-52c3b446d84b/scratchpad/hist/batch.mjs and shadow.mjs); both call the kit's own functions and sorbet's compositeOver, so no colour maths was done outside the kit.

KEY FILES

- /Users/homelab/code/sorbet/packages/design-system/src/tokens/semantics.ts (choosers; dark branch), rules.ts (the contract), emit.ts (shadowDecls), ramps.ts (equal-lightness curve), charts.ts

- /Users/homelab/code/sorbet/packages/design-system/dist/themes/sorbet.css (emitted values measured here)
- /Users/homelab/code/sorbet/docs/pastel-primary-role-split.md

map:wcag-gate.summary:
TAKEAWAYS (most important first)

- WCAG is encoded in three layers, and none of them knows which preset it is judging:
  1. ONE global rule list, `RULES` (rules.ts:25-101). Each rule is a pair plus a minimum contrast ratio (contrast ratio = how many times brighter the lighter colour is than the darker; 1:1 is identical, 21:1 is black on white). Measured: 86 entries, 70 apply per mode, so 700 checks over 5 presets x 2 modes. (README says 47, the playground says 790 - both stale.)
  2. The builder `buildMode` (semantics.ts), which does not just check shades, it CHOOSES them: 15 ramp walks with 4.5 and 3 typed in as literals.
  3. Five checkers: the real build gate, three hand-copied report loops (design-system tool, CLI, scaffold) and the live check inside TokenStudio. `checkColors` receives a preset NAME string and nothing else.
- Of the 70 per-mode rules, 46 are text rules. Only 6 are the edge/shape rules the owner objects to (border-strong x2, primary-solid x2, secondary-solid, accent-solid), plus 2 focus-ring and 16 chart-mark rules. The harsh grey outline is one value: border-strong = #777168 (4.51:1 on the page), used in 18 Sass places.
- Per-preset is a contained change IF sorbet moves by hand-picked `overrides` plus its own rule list, and the shared builder's walks are left alone. Measured: turning the thresholds down does NOT give pastel anyway, because the candidate lists are WCAG-shaped - primary-solid still picks #008289 at floors of 3, 2 and 1.5.
- Agent instructions currently FORBID this refactor and must change first: sorbet CLAUDE.md:68-69 ('rules.ts is a legal requirement... never lower a min'), contract-auditor.md:59-62 (deleting a rule is a finding), author-theme and debug-contrast skills. Lab memory `sorbet-design-system` (lines 17-19) says 'the gates are the point of the project' - that is the stored premise this request retires for the sorbet preset.
- Three things nobody asked about that matter for a colourblind reader, measured on today's sorbet light with the repo's own contrast():
  - switch off #777168 vs on #008289 = 1.05:1, and input resting border #777168 vs focused border #008289 = 1.05:1. Both are told apart by hue alone today, WCAG-compliant or not.
  - 'Passes AA' is not 'passes AA for a dichromat' (someone missing one cone type). Re-measured after colour-vision simulation, ratios drop up to 16%: danger-text on danger-subtle 4.58 -> 3.91, secondary-text on secondary-subtle 4.61 -> 4.00.
  - The dark-mode 'no edges' problem as a number: a black shadow over the dark page #26231f reaches only 1.06:1 (xs) to 1.22:1 (xl) at its densest point. A darker shadow has no headroom on a near-black page.

WHERE WCAG IS NOT ENCODED (read, nothing found): scales.ts, tools/pack-vendor.ts, tools/check-consumable.ts, tools/check-catalog.ts, .github/dependabot.yml, eslint/stylelint config, the add-component and sorbet-classes skills, apps/admin, apps/meal-kit. There is no package-level README; only the root one.

PATTERN NAMES worth knowing here: a 'policy object' (the contract as data a preset points at, instead of rules baked into code); a 'golden file' or snapshot test (store the known-good output, fail on any byte of drift) - the one tool that would catch a silent re-pick of noir; APCA (Accessible Perceptual Contrast Algorithm, the contrast model drafted for WCAG 3; it scores mid-tone text closer to how readable it actually looks and is the standard answer to 'how light can text go').

METHOD: read-only. Numbers came from node scripts in the session scratchpad importing sorbet's own src/tokens; nothing was built or written in the repo, and `git status` there is clean. Full per-site detail is in `sites`; mechanics in the other two fields.

ASSUMPTIONS I MADE (no one to ask): 'left exactly as they are' means the four other presets' emitted CSS must stay byte-identical; and the legibility contract is measured on lightness only, since hue cannot be relied on.

DECISIONS NEEDED FROM THE OWNER
1. Focus ring: keep its 3:1 floor inside the legibility contract (recommended - it is the only keyboard-focus cue and only shows while focused, so it costs the resting pastel look nothing), or drop it with the other non-text rules.
2. Marks that carry information with no text (progress fill, tab indicator, checkbox fill, chart marks): keep a distinct mid-depth 'mark' colour with a small floor (recommended; if it collapses to the pale fill #adedf3, progress fill vs its track is 1.12:1), or let them go fully pastel.
3. Starting text floor. Recommended: keep 4.5 for body text to begin with - it already allows non-grey text (#6739b4 violet-700 = 6.95:1, #00686d aqua-700 = 6.13:1 on #f8f7f5; anything with relative luminance up to 0.168 passes) - and lower it deliberately from there. Alternative: 3.5 or 3.0 from day one (luminance ceiling 0.230 / 0.277).
4. Colour-vision type is unrecorded. Recommended: gate on all three simulations (protan, deutan, tritan) until it is known; alternative: plain luminance only.
5. Lilac: there are four named pastels and three brand roles (primary, secondary, accent). A fourth role is a global token change touching all five presets; the alternative is giving lilac an existing slot (info, links, or text tint).
6. Does sorbet's DARK mode move in the same change, or light first?
map:wcag-gate.how_shade_selection_depends_on_wcag:
THE TWO FUNCTIONS

- `pick(ramp, candidates, against, min)` - semantics.ts:76-83. In words: walk the candidate steps in the order given and return the first one whose contrast against EVERY colour in `against` is at least `min`. If none qualifies it returns the LAST candidate, silently. Nothing errors at pick time; only the gate afterwards can notice.
- `solid(ramp, onColor, candidates, hoverDir)` - semantics.ts:109-118. The label colour is fixed; the fill is `pick(ramp, candidates, [onColor], 4.5)` with 4.5 typed in at line 111. Hover is one ramp step along, active is two. Hover and active are positional, not walked.

WHAT EACH WALK RETURNS FOR SORBET LIGHT TODAY (line, result, measured ratio)

- Not walked at all: bg = sand-50 #f8f7f5 (180-181); surface and surface-raised = literal #ffffff (183-184); bg-subtle and surface-sunken = sand-100 #f1eeeb; text = sand-900 #38342f, fixed at line 196 (11.54:1); border = sand-200 #e3dfd9; border-subtle = sand-100.
- text-muted (197): sand [600, 700] at 4.5 against page, white and sand-100 -> sand-700 #5f5a52 (6.39:1).
- text-subtle (198): sand [500, 600] at 3 -> sand-600 #777168 (4.51:1).
- border-strong (202): sand [500, 600] at 3 -> sand-600 #777168. This is the grey outline.
- Brand fills, pastel branch (129-130): `solid(ramp, sand-950, [200, 300, 100], darker)` -> always step 200, because near-black text clears 4.5 on anything pale: primary #adedf3 (12.05:1 under its label), secondary #ffd2e1, accent #f3e096. The label colour on-primary/on-secondary/on-accent is hard-wired to sand-950 #26231f, near black.
- primary-text / secondary-text / accent-text (137): [600, 700, 800, 900] at 4.5 against bg, surface and the ramp's 100 step -> #00686d (aqua-700), #c42876 (raspberry-600), #6f5800 (lemon-700).
- primary-solid / secondary-solid / accent-solid (146-148, light + pastel only): [600, 700, 800] at 3 against bg -> #008289 (4.31:1), #c42876 (5.01:1), #8a6f00 (4.50:1). These are the deep 'shape-maker' colours on checkboxes, sliders, tab indicators and button edges (23 Sass uses of primary-solid).
- Status (160-177): `brandStyle: pastel` never reaches this function. success/danger/info are white text on [500..800] at 4.5 -> #008944, #cb2c31, #0f70d5 (all deep); warning is dark text on #efa024.
- focus-ring (235-238): primary [500, 600, 700] at 3 against bg and surface -> #008289.
- link = primary-text, copied at line 239; link-hover = primary-800, fixed.
- Charts: fixed steps from charts.ts, not walked, but gated at 3:1.
- Dark mode: every fill walks [400, 300, 500, 200] with sand-950 text at 4.5 and lands on 400.

THRESHOLDS ALONE DO NOT PRODUCE PASTEL (measured by re-running the walks with a lower floor)

| floor | text-muted | border-strong | primary-solid | primary-text | focus-ring |
| 4.5 | sand-700 | sand-600 | aqua-700 | aqua-700 | aqua-700 |
| 3 | sand-600 | sand-600 | aqua-600 | aqua-600 | aqua-600 |
| 2 | sand-600 | sand-500 | aqua-600 | aqua-600 | aqua-500 |
| 1.5 | sand-600 | sand-500 | aqua-600 | aqua-600 | aqua-500 |

The candidate lists themselves ([600,700,800], [500,600]...) were written for WCAG, so the lightest thing a walk can ever return is still a deep mid-tone. A per-preset threshold inside the builder would touch shared code and still not deliver the palette. Hand-picked values are the mechanism that works.

WHERE OVERRIDES LAND - THE ORDER IS THE WHOLE STORY

1. Lines 179-240: every walk runs and fills `out`.
2. Line 242: `merged = { ...out, ...recipe.overrides?.[mode] }` - overrides are spread on top, last.
3. Lines 249-251: for primary, secondary, accent: `merged[role-solid] ??= merged[role]` - 'if no solid value exists yet, copy the final fill'.

Three consequences:
- (a) An override never re-runs a walk. Everything picked 'against bg' was picked against the builder's own bg (#f8f7f5) and literal white. Override bg to a cream and text-muted, text-subtle, border-strong, the -text roles, the -solid roles and focus-ring are all still the values chosen for the old page. The gate checks the final merged values, so a failure is caught, but nothing adapts.
- (b) Values copied before the merge do not follow it. `link` keeps the walked primary-text even if primary-text is overridden; hover and active keep their walked steps. That is why noir overrides primary, primary-hover, primary-active, on-primary, primary-text, link, link-hover and focus-ring all by hand (presets.ts:112-133).
- (c) `??=` only fills a MISSING value. In light mode with `brandStyle: pastel` the builder has already written primary-solid at line 147, so overriding `primary` alone leaves primary-solid at #008289. In dark mode, and in any vivid preset, no -solid exists yet, so it becomes the final fill, overrides included. For sorbet light, the three -solid names must be overridden explicitly, or the `if (pastel)` at line 146 must become contract-aware. Only sorbet sets brandStyle pastel, so that branch cannot reach another preset.

ROLES THAT WOULD CHANGE IF SORBET SUPPLIED HAND-PICKED PASTEL VALUES

- Page and surfaces: bg, bg-subtle, surface, surface-raised, surface-sunken (cream instead of #f8f7f5 / #ffffff).
- Text, as one decision: text, text-muted, text-subtle. They must be picked together - a hand-picked lighter `text` can end up LIGHTER than the walked text-muted #5f5a52, which inverts the hierarchy.
- Lines: border, border-subtle, border-strong.
- Brand, per role: fill, -hover, -active, -subtle, -text, on-, -solid for primary, secondary and accent (21 values), plus focus-ring, link and link-hover.
- Optional: status fills and their on- colours (the memory note records the hazard: pastel danger #ffd4d0 vs pastel pink #ffd2e1 measures 1.001:1); chart-1..8.
- Unchanged: scrim, on-scrim, on-scrim-muted (text over photographs).
- In the WCAG presets nothing changes, provided buildMode's walks are not edited.
map:wcag-gate.what_a_legibility_contract_would_need:
THE MINIMAL HONEST GATE HAS FOUR PARTS. 'Just text' is not quite enough, because three things besides text carry meaning.

1. TEXT FLOORS - KEEP ALL 46 PAIRS (the pairs survive; only the number becomes the contract's)
- text and text-muted on all five surfaces (10); text-subtle on bg and surface (2); link and link-hover (3).
- on-primary/secondary/accent on fill, hover and active (9); on-success, on-warning, on-danger x2, on-info (5).
- primary/secondary/accent-text on bg, surface and their subtle fill (7); the four status -text roles on bg and subtle (8).
- on-scrim and on-scrim-muted on the scrim (2) - text over photos, checked against a white and a black image.
- Two gaps to close while here: text-subtle is used as real small text in 47 Sass places (placeholders, captions) but is only held to 3:1, the large-text number; and it is never checked on bg-subtle, which is where a disabled input puts it.
- Floors become named tiers on the contract (body, muted, subtle), each one number with a one-line reason and what would retire it. Starting point recommended: body 4.5 unchanged, because that already permits coloured text (relative luminance up to 0.168 on #f8f7f5; e.g. #6739b4 = 6.95:1). The owner's experiment is then one number to turn down, not a code change.

2. RULES THAT SIMPLY GO for a legibility preset
- border-strong on bg and surface (2) - the grey outline #777168.
- primary-solid on bg and surface (2), secondary-solid on bg, accent-solid on bg - the 3:1 shape and button-edge rules.
- chart marks at 3:1 against the surface (16 light) and 2.25 (16 dark), replaced by part 3.

3. WHAT REPLACES THEM - small floors on things that carry information without a label
- Focus: keep focus-ring at 3:1 against bg and surface. It is how keyboard focus is seen at all, so it is 'usage accessibility', and it only appears while focused. Add one pair that has never been ruled: focus-ring against border-strong, because an input shows focus by swapping its border colour (measured 1.05:1 today).
- Marks: measure each against the thing it must be told apart from, not against the page - progress fill vs its track, slider fill vs track, tab indicator vs page, checkbox fill vs surface, chart marks vs surface. A floor around 1.5 to 2.0 is a judgement, not a standard, and should be labelled as one. Evidence it is needed: with primary-solid collapsed to the pale fill #adedf3, progress fill vs track #f1eeeb is 1.12:1 and tab indicator vs page is 1.21:1. Already unruled today: the secondary progress bar #ffd2e1 on #f1eeeb = 1.17:1.
- Tell-apart pairs: any two colours whose difference IS the message (danger vs the pink brand; a selected vs unselected state with no weight or icon change) need a lightness gap or a non-colour cue.

4. EDGE PRESENCE - the owner's 'never NO emphasis on edges', as a number
- Rule in words: every raised element must differ from what it sits on, by fill or by shadow, by at least a small floor (about 1.1:1).
- It is checkable with code that already exists: `compositeOver()` (color.ts:126-134, written for the scrim) blends a translucent colour over a backdrop. Blend the shadow colour at its alpha over the page and measure the result against the page.
- Today's readings: light 1.12 (xs) to 1.62 (xl); dark 1.06 to 1.22. So in dark mode the soft edge has to be a glow or surface LIGHTER than the page; a similarly-coloured darker shadow cannot do it.
- To gate it, shadow colour and alpha must become data the checker can read; they are currently strings assembled in emit.ts:34-43.

HOW TO MAKE IT A RULE RATHER THAN PROSE
- Give every Rule a `kind` (text, focus, mark, edge, non-text) and a `why` sentence. The existing proposal doc already asked for `why` (docs/pastel-primary-role-split.md:177-182).
- Make the contract a named data object the preset points at: `contract: 'wcag-aa' | 'legibility'`, REQUIRED on the Preset type so all five declare it and no default can be flipped later.
- DERIVE the legibility list from the WCAG list by kind (keep text and focus, drop non-text, add its own mark and edge rules). Then a text pair added later joins both contracts automatically; restating 46 pairs by hand is how the two would drift.
- Measure after colour-vision simulation and take the worst case: the unsimulated ratio and the ratio under protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia. The simulation code (Machado 2009 matrices) already exists in tools/check-cvd.ts:29-81 but lives outside src/tokens, so TokenStudio and the scaffold cannot reach it; it has to move into src/tokens. Today it covers protan and deutan only.
- One checker function, called by all five places that check today.
- A golden-file gate for the untouched presets: the emitted colours of ocean, forest, noir and midnight are stored and any byte of drift fails the build. This is the permanent form of 'left exactly as they are'; today nothing would notice.
- Failure output prints the rule's `why`, so a red build says what the reader would lose, not just a ratio.

Any edit to a walk or candidate list in semantics.ts, to the shared lightness or chroma curve (ramps.ts:16-43), or to a shared ramp changes other presets with no error, because pick() falls back to its last candidate instead of failing. Shared ramps: sand = sorbet + forest neutral; lemon = sorbet + noir accent; green, amber, red, blue, coral = all five. No golden file of emitted themes exists and dist/ is gitignored, so nothing would notice. What breaks: noir is the theme pantry, wallpaper-admin and musicdisco vendor. Guard: byte-compare dist/themes/{ocean,forest,noir,midnight}.css before and after, then make that comparison a permanent gate.

ONE CONSUMER IS NOT THE OWNER'S OWN EYES. ~/code/buylist (the friend's game-store app) imports themes/ocean.css. The memory note 'every consumer is the user's own app' is true of who builds it, not of who reads it. This is a concrete reason ocean stays on the WCAG contract, and a reason 'the rule will eventually be universal' should be an explicit per-preset opt-in rather than a default that flips.

FIVE CHECKERS, ALREADY DISAGREEING. The build gate measures the two scrim rules; the three report loops (design-system tool, CLI, scaffold) skip any translucent colour and then print 'all 86 pairings pass' when 68 were measured per mode. Converting some but not all leaves a green report beside a red gate, or the reverse. One shared checker function is the fix; the scaffold copy is a hand-maintained template and is the one most likely to be missed.

AGENT INSTRUCTIONS WILL FIGHT THE CHANGE. CLAUDE.md:68-69, contract-auditor.md:59-62, author-theme and debug-contrast all tell an agent that removing or lowering a rule is forbidden and that 'the palette is the thing that is wrong'. An agent following them correctly will refuse or flag the refactor. They have to be amended first, in their own commit, and only the owner can authorise that.

TOKENSTUDIO WILL MISREPORT. It checks the live page against the global WCAG list regardless of the loaded theme, and its `preset` prop is label-only (.design-sync/NOTES.md:168-171). On a legibility sorbet it would show a permanent list of WCAG failures; if switched by the prop instead of the loaded stylesheet it could show 'all passing' for the wrong contract.

OVERRIDES DO NOT RE-RUN WALKS, AND THREE TRAPS FOLLOW. (a) A lighter hand-picked `text` can end up lighter than the walked text-muted #5f5a52, inverting the hierarchy. (b) `link`, hover and active are copied before the merge and keep their walked values. (c) In light + pastel, overriding `primary` leaves `primary-solid` at #008289 because `??=` only fills a missing value. All three build green and look wrong.

HUE-ONLY STATE CUES GET WORSE, AND SOME ARE ALREADY BROKEN FOR THIS READER. Today: switch off vs on 1.05:1; input resting vs focused border 1.05:1; secondary progress bar vs its track 1.17:1. Dropping the 3:1 shape rules with nothing in their place takes progress fill and tab indicator to 1.12-1.21:1. Position, weight and icons carry some of these (the switch thumb moves; a selected chip goes medium weight); progress, tabs and the input focus state have no such backup.

A WCAG RATIO IS NOT A COLOURBLIND RATIO. Measured after simulation, coloured text loses up to 16%: danger-text on danger-subtle 4.58 -> 3.91, secondary-text on its subtle fill 4.61 -> 4.00 (deuteranopia), info-text on bg 6.44 -> 5.59 (tritanopia). A lower text floor measured the WCAG way could be materially lower for the owner. The owner's type is unrecorded and the existing colour-vision gate covers only protanopia and deuteranopia.

DARK MODE CANNOT GET ITS EDGES FROM A 'SIMILARLY COLOURED' SHADOW. A black shadow over the dark page #26231f measures 1.06-1.22:1 at its densest, less once blurred; dark border-subtle equals dark surface exactly (#38342f, 1.00:1). The edge there has to be something lighter than the page (a glow, an inset highlight, or a lighter raised surface). This is the earlier 'no emphasis on edges' problem (commit b9b0ed8) and it will come back unless the edge rule is gated in both modes.

CHART OVERRIDES BYPASS THE COLOUR-VISION GATE. check-cvd.ts reads `chartThemes`, not the preset's final colours, so a chart colour set through `overrides` is never validated. Sorbet's chart floors (14.6 light, 14.9 dark) are regression baselines and will fail the build the moment its steps move; the scaffold has no colour-vision gate at all.

LILAC HAS NO ROLE. Four named pastels, three brand roles. A fourth role extends SEMANTIC_COLOR_NAMES, which is global: every preset must supply it, the generated Sass list changes, and TokenStudio's brand grouping regex (token-studio.tsx:66) needs it. That is a change to the four presets that are meant to stay exactly as they are - emitted CSS for all of them gains new lines.

MOVING EDGES FROM BORDERS TO SHADOWS REMOVES THEM IN FORCED-COLORS MODE (Windows high-contrast), which strips box-shadow and keeps borders - the reason _button.scss:58-62 gives for the border. Acceptable for personal use, but it is a real loss and should be a stated decision, not a side effect.

A FAILED GATE STILL WRITES CSS. build-tokens.ts writes dist/themes/*.css (lines 20-27) and only then checks (29-36). pack-vendor stops on the non-zero exit, but anything that copies dist without checking the exit code would ship a theme that failed its contract. The debug-contrast skill states the opposite order.

NOTHING REACHES AN APP UNTIL IT IS RE-VENDORED. All four site copies are at sorbet 5e1bf6b (2026-09-09) and linecook and buylist hold tarballs. linecook and imagefeed load the sorbet theme, so they change on the next sync-sorbet or pack:vendor; the four sync-sorbet scripts have drifted before (lab CLAUDE.md). Staging in sorbet is safe; the rollout is per app and by hand.

STALE NUMBERS WILL BE COPIED FORWARD. README says 47 pairings (measured 86 entries, 70 per mode); the playground says 790 checks (measured 700); README:570 claims a colour-vision separation of 14.7 for every preset when the gate's floors go down to 3.9; README:398 describes sorbet as raspberry, mint and grape; the role-split doc still says 'proposed, not implemented'. Any rewrite of the contract docs should re-derive these rather than edit around them.
