usage_accessibility_guarantees: WHERE IT LIVES: every ARIA attribute, role, key handler and focus call is in /Users/homelab/code/sorbet/packages/component-library/src (81 files, 8,892 lines) and /Users/homelab/code/sorbet/packages/design-system/src/behaviors (11 vanilla files, 892 lines). The TSX holds no CSS: components emit `sb-*` class names plus attributes. So a palette/edge change made in tokens + Sass leaves all of the following byte-identical.

Native elements first: Button is a real <button type=button> (or `as`); Checkbox/Radio are <input>; Switch is <input type=checkbox role=switch>; Select is <select>; Slider is <input type=range>; Accordion is <details>/<summary> with `name` for exclusive groups; Modal, Drawer and AlertDialog are <dialog>.showModal(), so focus trap, Escape and the backdrop come from the browser; Menu, Popover, Combobox panel and Tooltip use the Popover API (top layer).

Tabs (molecules/tabs.tsx): role tablist/tab/tabpanel, aria-selected, aria-controls <-> aria-labelledby ids from useId, roving tabindex (only the selected tab is tabbable), Arrow/Home/End via core `rovingIndex` with automatic activation, inactive panels `hidden`. The vanilla twin (behaviors/tabs.ts) does the same for the static pages.
SegmentedControl: role radiogroup/radio, aria-checked, roving tabindex, arrows move and select.

Combobox, MultiCombobox, CommandPalette: role combobox + listbox/option, aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-autocomplete=list, aria-activedescendant (focus never leaves the input), aria-selected, aria-disabled, aria-multiselectable; ArrowUp/Down, Enter, Escape, Tab handled; group headings role=presentation; CommandTrigger sets aria-keyshortcuts.

Field (molecules/field.tsx): generates the id, wires <label htmlFor>, aria-describedby to hint and error ids, aria-invalid; Input/Textarea/Select/NumberInput/ColorInput/Combobox accept and forward aria-invalid and aria-describedby.

Calendar / DatePicker / DateRange: role grid/row/columnheader/gridcell, aria-selected, aria-current=date, aria-disabled, roving tabindex, Arrow/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown/Enter/Space/Escape; month title is a visually-hidden aria-live=polite region; the popup is role=dialog with aria-label, its trigger carries aria-haspopup=dialog, aria-expanded, aria-controls.

NumberInput: role spinbutton with aria-valuenow/min/max, Arrow/Page/Home/End keys; stepper buttons labelled and tabIndex -1. ColorInput: swatch button aria-haspopup/expanded/controls, panel role=dialog, saturation area role=slider with aria-valuetext and keyboard, native ranges labelled Hue/Opacity, swatch chips aria-pressed + aria-label=hex.

Status and live regions: Alert role=status (caller may pass role=alert), Spinner role=status aria-label Loading, Progress role=progressbar with aria-valuemin/max/now, toast region role=region aria-live=polite aria-label Notifications, Dropzone error role=alert.

Accessible names on icon-only controls: every built-in close/dismiss/remove/prev/next button has an aria-label with an overridable prop (Chip removeLabel, Alert dismissLabel, ModalHeader/DrawerHeader closeLabel, Pagination `Page N`, Carousel, Calendar). Icon is aria-hidden unless `label` is given, then role=img + aria-label. Decoration is aria-hidden (badge dot, skeleton, rating stars, chart SVG, sparkline, stepper marker, marquee duplicates).

Wayfinding: Breadcrumb <nav aria-label><ol> with aria-current=page; Pagination <nav aria-label=Pagination> with aria-current=page; Navbar/Sidebar <nav aria-label> with aria-current=page; Stepper <ol> with aria-current=step; Carousel role=group aria-roledescription=carousel/slide, `i of n` labels, aria-controls, focusable viewport.

Focus management: AlertDialog is role=alertdialog with aria-labelledby/aria-describedby and focuses Cancel for a destructive action, Confirm otherwise; Menu focuses its first item on open, returns focus to the trigger on select, closes on Tab; Popover focuses its panel and returns focus to the trigger on Escape; Tooltip shows on hover AND keyboard focus, hides on Escape, role=tooltip wired by aria-describedby; Combobox returns focus to the input after select/clear.

Tables: real <table> with scope=col/row, aria-sort on the sorted header, the sort trigger is a real <button> (DataTable). Charts: <figure role=group aria-label>, SVG aria-hidden, legend role=list/listitem, and a `View as table` toggle (aria-pressed) that renders the same data as a real table - series identity never rides on colour alone. Rating is one role=img announcing `4.3 out of 5`. Marquee has a pause button (WCAG 2.2.2), pauses on hover/focus and under reduced motion.

THE PART THAT IS NOT IN TSX AND IS IN THE BLAST RADIUS: the keyboard focus indicator and several state signals are painted by the stylesheet. Focus ring = `outline: var(--sb-focus-ring-width) solid var(--sb-focus-ring)` on :focus-visible at 35 include sites (abstracts/_mixins.scss:28-41); --sb-focus-ring is #008289 in the sorbet theme, 4.31:1 against the #f8f7f5 page. Text controls use `control-glow` = border-color + a box-shadow halo (8 sites) - box-shadow is ONE property, so a box-shadow edge and a box-shadow focus glow overwrite each other unless composed. Checked checkbox, switch on, tab indicator, selected-chip border, stepper done/current, slider and progress fill are all painted in `primary-solid`. Also in Sass: `.u-visually-hidden`, 9 prefers-reduced-motion blocks, coarse-pointer touch sizing, and state styling keyed on the ARIA attributes themselves (aria-selected, aria-checked, aria-pressed, aria-current, aria-invalid, aria-sort, aria-disabled) so the look cannot drift from what is announced. If the refactor makes the focus-ring or `-solid` colours pastel, keyboard focus and checked/selected states stop being visible - that is the one way a `visual only` change damages usage accessibility.

Forced-colors (the OS high-contrast mode, which repaints a page in a few system colours and DROPS box-shadow): sorbet has no `@media (forced-colors)` rule; it survives today only because edges are real borders (atoms/_button.scss:58-63 says so in a comment). Shadow-only edges leave controls edgeless in that mode. Not the owner's setup, so a known trade rather than a blocker - but it is the one usage-accessibility cost of borders -> shadows.

Pre-existing gap, a real defect rather than a style choice, and not caused by this refactor: React Menu (molecules/menu.tsx) sets aria-haspopup=`menu` on the trigger but the panel has no role=menu, the items are plain buttons with no role=menuitem, and the trigger gets no aria-expanded (the vanilla behaviors/menu.ts does set aria-expanded). Keyboard works; a screen reader hears a promise of a menu and gets a group of buttons.

map:consumers.summary:
READ-ONLY survey, nothing changed. Measured 2026-10-03 17:17 EDT against sorbet main @ 5e1bf6b (clean tree). Terms: "vendored" = a copy checked into the app rather than a live link; "contrast ratio" = WCAG luminance ratio, 1:1 identical, 21:1 black on white; "L" = OKLab perceptual lightness, 0 black to 1 white - the axis a colourblind reader can rely on.

TAKEAWAYS
- Sorbet is a safe staging ground by construction. All seven out-of-repo consumers hold COPIES: four static pages (pantry, imagefeed, wallpaper-admin, musicdisco) via per-app `sync-sorbet` scripts, three React apps (linecook, buylist, bananasplit) via `vendor/*.tgz`. Nothing outside ~/code/sorbet changes until someone runs a sync or `pnpm pack:vendor`. Only the in-repo playground, meal-kit, admin and demo page see changes live.
- The build blocks before anything can ship. `pnpm build` fails on any rules.ts contrast violation or check-cvd floor, so a truly pastel palette produces no dist/ and therefore no sync and no tarball. rules.ts is the first file to change; sorbet's own CLAUDE.md calls it a non-negotiable, which has to be retired in the same PR.
- Palette and edges travel to different apps. The `sorbet` THEME file is loaded only by imagefeed (viewer + admin) and linecook. pantry, wallpaper-admin and musicdisco load noir; buylist loads ocean. A palette change reaches two apps; an edge change in the shared sorbet.css reaches all of them.
- Usage accessibility is separable and the separation is checkable. All ARIA, roles, key handling and focus management live in component-library TSX and the vanilla behaviours, which contain no colour except four couplings (chart slot names, ColorInput's `contrast` import, TokenStudio's WCAG badge, the three-role BrandTone type). Proof on the refactor branch: `git diff main --stat -- packages/component-library/src packages/design-system/src/behaviors` should be empty or list only those files.
- There are no accessibility tests. No test runner, no axe, no jsx-a11y lint. `pnpm test` is the colour-contrast report plus a "use client" directive check. The diff above and check:consumable's server-render of 126+ components are the only evidence available.

WHAT CAN BREAK SILENTLY, worst first
1. Keyboard focus and checked/selected states are painted by the stylesheet, not TSX: the focus ring is an outline in --sb-focus-ring (#008289, 4.31:1 on the #f8f7f5 page, 35 sites) and checkbox/switch/tab/chip/stepper states use `primary-solid`. If those go pastel, focus and selection vanish. This is the one route by which a "visual only" change damages usage accessibility. Text inputs also use box-shadow for their focus glow, and box-shadow is a single property - an edge shadow and a focus glow overwrite each other unless written as one list.
2. imagefeed admin hard-codes four dark-mode hexes "in sorbet's own hue" (admin.html:61-66) as a stopgap for the collapsed dark ramp (theme: card vs page 1.27:1, border vs card 1.32:1). A new palette leaves the old browns underneath in dark mode. That block is the written record of the "dark mode problem"; fixing the ramp in sorbet lets it be deleted.
3. imagefeed marks states by re-colouring a sorbet control's border (`.arm`, `.danger`, `.done`, `.nudge.on`, `#fav.on`). If buttons and chips lose their border outright, those rules do nothing. A 1px transparent border in the base class keeps them alive.
4. Any removed or renamed --sb-border*, --sb-bg or --sb-surface* token: six apps read them as raw var() with no fallback, so hairlines disappear and sticky bars turn transparent with no error. Keep names, change values.
5. linecook's vendored design-system is two changes behind main (touch sizing #120, accordion #123); the first re-vendor mixes those with the palette. It also pairs on-primary #26231f with primary-solid #008289 at 3.39:1, a pairing no rule watches.
6. buylist's users are a friend's store staff, not the owner - the "legible for me" bar does not fit that one app.
7. Marketing copy becomes false: "WCAG AA - enforced at build time", "Provably accessible", "790 checks" in the playground, demo page, CLI strings, README section "The accessibility contract". check:cli asserts the CLI prints "holds".

FINDINGS THAT BEAR ON THE COLOURBLIND GOAL (measured, today's output)
- The contrast-driven builder equalises lightness, which removes the cue the owner depends on. The three brand fills are L 0.905 / 0.906 / 0.906 (#adedf3, #ffd2e1, #f3e096); success, warning and info text are L 0.471 / 0.469 / 0.471 (#006e35, #7f4e00, #0059af). They differ by hue only. Pantry's stock levels are drawn in exactly those three.
- Edges today are already faint: card on page 1.07:1, card border 1.16:1, --sb-border 1.24-1.33:1; only inputs carry a strong edge (#777168, 4.83:1). The owner's "no harsh grey outlines" is mostly about form controls.
- The soft hue-matched shadow already exists on one component: filled buttons (`--edge` + three tinted box-shadows in _button.scss). The refactor generalises it.
- The only colourblind-specific gate (check-cvd, protanopia + deuteranopia simulation) covers chart slots and nothing else.
- Shadow-only edges disappear in OS forced-colors (high-contrast) mode; sorbet has no rule for it. A known trade, not the owner's setup.
- Separate from the refactor, a real defect: React Menu advertises aria-haspopup="menu" but renders no role=menu / menuitem and no aria-expanded.

PRACTICAL NOTES FOR STAGING
- Do the work in a `git worktree`: every sync-sorbet copies whatever dist/ the main checkout currently holds, so an experimental build there can be shipped into a lab app by any routine "after a sorbet change" sync.
- Best review surfaces are listed with paths in react_layer.review_surfaces. No existing page prints hex + ratio + lightness per pairing; one new file in apps/playground/src/demos/ would add it (demos self-register).
- The playground binds localhost:5183 on the headless lab; viewing it elsewhere needs `--host` + the tailnet IP or a Serve route.

OPEN QUESTIONS FOR THE OWNER
1. Lilac has no slot. Three brand roles are typed in (primary, secondary, accent). Add a fourth role (additive - consumers unaffected, touches the BrandTone type, Sass variant loops, token names, TokenStudio) or give lilac an existing role such as `info`?
2. buylist: keep it on ocean with bordered edges (an opt-out for the one app other people use), or let the new edge rule reach it on its next re-vendor?
3. Is dark mode in scope for this pass? imagefeed can switch to dark and carries the stopgap; buylist is light-only by the owner's own call on 2026-09-27.
4. Should pantry, wallpaper-admin and musicdisco move from noir to the new sorbet theme, or stay monochrome and take only the edge change?

propose:reference-fidelity.lens: Fidelity to what the five names mean. Each colour starts from recognised references, measured with colorkit.mjs, then moved as little as needed to sit in one pastel family. Units used throughout: OKLCH = L lightness 0..1, C chroma (colourfulness, 0 = grey), h hue angle in degrees. 'sep' = how far apart two colours look (OKLab distance x100; under ~5 hard to tell apart, 10+ clearly different), always quoted as normal/protan/deutan/tritan (the three simulated colour-blindness types). 'Lc' = APCA lightness contrast (75+ body paragraphs, 60+ short labels, 45 large headings, 30 floor). References from web search: Wikipedia/Crayola robin egg blue #00cccc and #1fcecb, Tiffany Blue #81d8d0, Pantone Rose Quartz #f7cac9, classic blush #f4c2c2, Wikipedia lilac #c8a2c8 and pale lilac #dcd0ff, artyclick pale lilac #e4cbff, Wikipedia cream #fffdd0, xkcd butter yellow #fffd74, Valspar Like Butter #fee59c (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_egg_blue, /Tiffany_Blue, /Lilac_(color), /Cream_(colour), /Blush_(color); artyclick.com; hextoral.com; w3schools colors_2016). From my own knowledge, not searched: CSS named colours (cornsilk, oldlace, pink, thistle), RAL 9001, pale robin egg blue #96ded1, vanilla #f3e5ab, and the brand inks measured for comparison (Slack aubergine #4a154b, Stripe navy #0a2540, Mailchimp peppercorn #241c15, brunswick green #1b4d3e, dark brown #5c4033). Edge numbers are NOT estimates: the recipes were rendered in headless Chromium at 2x and the actual edge pixels sampled. Things to look at (scratch, not in the repo): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-homelab/06652a5c-23e2-4a00-8579-52c3b446d84b/scratchpad/fidelity/specimen.png (palette, how each colour is seen under each simulation, six ink ladders as real 16px paragraphs on the cream page, inks on the four fills) and .../fidelity/edges.png (every edge recipe, light and dark side by side); sources specimen.html and edges.html beside them. Nothing in /Users/homelab/code/sorbet was edited.

cream.why: Sits between RAL 9001 Cream #fdf4e3 (sep 0.9) and CSS cornsilk #fff8dc (sep 1.1). 11x the chroma of today's page #f8f7f5 (C 0.003, effectively neutral), so it is visibly warm. It keeps its yellow under red-green simulation (seen as #faf3db protan, #fdf6dd deutan). Wikipedia's cream #fffdd0 (C 0.058) was rejected for a page: that yellow would swallow butter.

surface.why: 'Milk': a warm white for cards and fields, never pure #ffffff (which reads cold on cream). Only 2.8/3.0/2.7/2.4 from the page on purpose: the fill is not what separates a card, the tinted shadow is (see edge recipes). Supporting tones in the same hue: sunken well #f9ecce (L 0.946, 5.1 from surface), deep cream #efdcb5 (L 0.900) for switch and slider tracks.

blush.why: Pantone Rose Quartz #f7cac9 moved by 0.8; 2.6 from classic blush/baby pink #f4c2c2. The references for 'blush' cluster at hue 16-20 (a warm pink), so this is warmer than today's secondary #ffd2e1 (hue 356, a cool blossom pink). Crayola Blush #de5d83 (L 0.65, C 0.164) is a lipstick colour, not a pastel.

robin.why: The textbook references are too strong for a pastel: Crayola #1fcecb is L 0.77 C 0.128, Tiffany Blue #81d8d0 is L 0.825 C 0.085 h 188. Kept their hue (190, between Tiffany 188 and Crayola 193), kept Tiffany-level chroma, and lifted lightness to the pastel floor: 1.9 from 'pale robin egg blue' #96ded1, 4.1 from Tiffany. Today's primary #adedf3 sits at hue 203, drifted toward sky blue; a robin's egg is greener than that.

lilac.why: Between pale lilac (ISCC-NBS) #dcd0ff at hue 297 (sep 2.5) and artyclick's pale lilac #e4cbff at hue 307 (sep 1.9). Wikipedia's lilac #c8a2c8 is L 0.76 (too dark for a pastel) and hue 326 (pinker); measured, moving toward it makes lilac collapse into its neighbours (at hue 320: lilac/blush 3.6 tritan, lilac/robin 2.3 deutan), so it stays at 303, still plainly purple rather than periwinkle.

butter.why: Valspar 'Like Butter' #fee59c moved by 0.8; 1.5 from vanilla #f3e5ab; 1.6 from today's accent #f3e096. xkcd's butter yellow #fffd74 (C 0.158) is neon lemon, not pastel. Chroma sits at the 0.09 cap deliberately: butter shares the page's hue, so colourfulness is the only thing keeping it apart from cream (7.5/8.1/7.2/5.6).

roles.primary: Lilac #dbc6fa. It is the only pastel that stays 10+ from the cream page in every view (14.9/14.7/14.8/10.8), and under red-green simulation it is the only fill besides butter that is still a colour (seen as #bdcefc protan, #c0cff8 deutan, a clear pale blue, C 0.06) rather than a grey.
roles.secondary: Blush #fbcbcd. Next to a lilac primary it holds 8.1/7.4/8.5/5.9; robin's egg in the same seat falls to 4.2 under deutan. From the page: 10.1/10.5/8.5/9.8.
roles.accent: Butter #f9e49f. It is lilac's opposite on the blue-yellow axis, which is the axis red-green-deficient vision keeps: lilac/butter is the best-separated pair in the palette, 17.0/16.7/16.6 (7.0 tritan). Its weakness is the page: only 7.5/8.1/7.2/5.6 from cream, so it is used small (highlights, badges, 'new' markers, selected day) and always carries its own-hue ring; on a milk card it is 10.2/11.1/9.9/7.9.
roles.fourth_pastel_job: Robin's egg blue #98e3dd is the success / done / progress colour (success status, completed steps, progress fill) and the decorative fourth (charts, avatars, illustration). It is kept OUT of the button trio because under red-green simulation it turns grey and is indistinguishable from blush (3.2 protan, 4.5 deutan) and from lilac under deutan (4.2). As a status it always arrives with an icon and a word, so that collapse costs nothing.
roles.rationale: Chosen by measurement, not by today's tagline. Tested every way of picking three button colours from four: any trio containing robin's egg has a pair under 5 (robin/blush 3.2 protan, robin/lilac 4.2 deutan). Lilac + blush + butter is the only trio whose worst pair stays readable: 7.4 across the red-green views, 4.6 at worst under tritan. The honest summary for a red-green-deficient reader: this palette is three things, not five: yellow (cream, butter), blue (lilac), pale grey (blush and robin's egg). So the two colours that survive as colours get the two jobs that most need recognising (primary, accent), and the two that grey out get jobs that always carry a label. This changes sorbet's identity (robin's egg was primary); if that matters more than the measurement, the fallback is primary robin's egg / secondary blush / accent butter with lilac for focus, links and info, accepting that primary and secondary then look the same grey under red-green simulation.
roles.statuses: The four statuses ARE the four pastels, no extra hues: success = robin's egg #98e3dd, warning = butter #f9e49f, danger = blush #fbcbcd, info = lilac #dbc6fa. A separate mint green for success was measured and is worse (mint #b9eec2 is 4.3 from butter under protan and 2.2 from blush under deutan). Pair separations: warning/info 17.0/16.7/16.6/7.0, warning/success 13.5/9.5/12.6/15.0, warning/danger 10.1/9.7/8.2/4.6, danger/info 8.1/7.4/8.5/5.9, success/info 12.5/7.5/4.2/11.1, success/danger 13.1/3.2/4.5/16.4. Two pairs collapse, so colour is never the signal. Three hue-free signals instead: (1) every status has its own icon silhouette (tick-in-circle, triangle, cross-in-octagon, i-in-circle); (2) every status says its word; (3) danger alone carries a heavy 2px rose rim, #ba5566 at 50% (lands as #dca5a1 on cream): 20.5/21.9/19.5/20.4 from the page and 14.8/15.7/12.4/15.4 from success's light rim, a lightness cue that holds in every view. Status text is the normal ink, not coloured.
roles.focus_and_links: Focus ring: a deep lilac #8962c5 (L 0.58 C 0.15 h 300) as 'outline: 3px solid; outline-offset: 2px'. This is the one deliberately firm edge, because keyboard use depends on it: 42.7/43.0/43.3/39.2 from cream and at least 28.4 from every pastel fill. Dark mode ring is lilac #dbc6fa itself (64.7/64.7/64.3/64.3 from the dark page). Links: grape #574173 (Lc 83.6 on cream), hover #412b5c, ALWAYS underlined: a link is only 3.9/3.3/3.7/4.3 from the body ink, so the underline is the signal, not the colour. Dark mode links: #dbc6fa underlined (Lc 76 on the dark page).
roles.surfaces: Light: page cream #fef4dc; cards and fields milk #fffbf1 (fields #fffdf8); sunken #f9ecce; tracks #efdcb5. Text: body #643d60, headings and on-fill labels #4d284a, muted #7c5378 (Lc 74.8 cream / 78.7 milk), captions and placeholders #8e648a (Lc 67.3 / 71.2), nothing lighter. Dark: the page becomes the ink and the ink becomes the cream. Page aubergine #211520 (L 0.216 C 0.028 h 329, the body ink's own hue, not black); card #2e202d (5.0 from page); raised #3a2a39; sunken #160d16. Text cream #f2e7ce (Lc 91.5 on page, 89.9 on card); muted #d7c9ae (Lc 73.4); captions #beaf95 (Lc 58.7). The four pastel fills and their label ink do NOT change between modes (same hexes, same label contrast); only page, surfaces, text and edge recipes swap.

text_families.name: Plum (aubergine) - my pick
text_families.why_on_brand: The hue halfway between the lilac primary (303) and the blush secondary (15): the shadow colour of both. Real-world anchor: Slack's aubergine #4a154b is L 0.31, Lc 93.8 on this cream, so #643d60 is already a full step lighter than a brand that is famous for purple ink. Body step on every background, Lc normal/protan/deutan/tritan: cream 83.8/84.2/84.0/82.7, milk 87.7/88.5/87.6/86.9, blush 66.5/64.7/67.7/65.3, robin 65.9/70.4/62.8/65.8, lilac 62.2/63.2/61.8/62.3, butter 74.6/73.6/75.6/72.7. Under red-green simulation it stays a colour (seen as #3c4761 protan, #454c5f deutan: dark slate blue, C 0.03-0.05), so it does not turn into the dark grey you are leaving. Lightest for paragraphs: #7c5378 (Lc 74.8, right on the 75 line; cream and milk only, it drops to 53-57 on fills). Captions only: #8e648a (Lc 67.3). #a0769c (Lc 59) is too light for anything but large headings.

text_families.name: Grape (deep lilac) - runner-up, used for links
text_families.why_on_brand: The primary's own hue taken deep: a violet ink. Body step Lc normal/protan/deutan/tritan: cream 84/83/84/83, blush 66/63/68/65, robin 66/69/63/66, lilac 62/62/62/62, butter 74/72/76/73. Of all six it keeps the MOST colour under red-green simulation (seen as #354b75 protan, #394b72 deutan, C 0.07). Cooler and more obviously 'purple text' than plum in normal vision; plum reads warmer against cream. If you prefer this to plum, swap freely: the contrast numbers are within 1 Lc of each other.

text_families.name: Cocoa
text_families.why_on_brand: The deep tone of the cream and butter hue: the classic cocoa-on-cream stationery pairing (reference dark brown #5c4033 is L 0.40, Lc 85.4 here; Mailchimp's peppercorn #241c15 is nearly black at L 0.23). Body step Lc: cream 83/84/83/83, blush 66/64/67/65, robin 65/70/62/66, lilac 62/63/61/62, butter 74/73/75/73. Equally robust as plum. The catch: at this low chroma it is seen as a dull olive under red-green simulation (#4d4836 / #544e37, C 0.03), the closest of the six to the dark grey-brown sorbet uses today (#38342f).

text_families.name: Ink blue
text_families.why_on_brand: Fountain-pen blue on cream paper (Stripe's navy #0a2540 is L 0.26, Lc 96.1 here). Keeps its colour under red-green simulation (#405073 / #394a70). But it loses 2-5 Lc under protan because blue inks do not darken the way reddish ones do: body step cream 83/81/85/82, blush 66/61/68/64, robin 65/67/63/65, lilac 61/60/62/61, butter 74/70/76/72. That is why its lightest paragraph step is one notch deeper (#44587d, Lc 78.5) than plum's. It also belongs to none of the five named colours.

text_families.name: Forest teal (deep robin's egg) - not recommended
text_families.why_on_brand: The deep tone of robin's egg, the forest-green-on-cream look of paper-goods brands (brunswick green #1b4d3e is L 0.38, Lc 85.9 here). In normal vision it is handsome. For a red-green-deficient reader it is seen as plain dark grey (#515255 protan, C 0.005; #494c55 deutan, C 0.015), which is exactly the look you asked to leave. Body step Lc: cream 82/80/84/81, blush 65/61/68/64, robin 64/66/63/64, lilac 60/59/62/61, butter 73/69/76/71: the weakest of the six.

text_families.name: Mulberry (deep blush) - not recommended
text_families.why_on_brand: The deep tone of blush: a berry or wine ink. Contrast is fine and even gains under protan (reddish inks darken): cream 84/86/83/83, blush 66/66/67/65, robin 66/72/62/66, lilac 62/65/61/62, butter 75/75/75/73. But like teal it is seen as neutral dark grey under red-green simulation (#414347 protan, C 0.007; #514e46 deutan, C 0.013). Worth keeping only as the optional tint for danger text, never as the body ink.

propose:reference-fidelity.on_fill_text: One ink family everywhere, not tone-on-tone. Body ink #643d60 clears the 60 label line on every fill in every view (worst case 61.8, lilac under deutan), but lilac is tight, so labels that sit ON a fill use the same family one step deeper, #4d284a (L 0.34): blush 74.1/72.2/75.5/73.0, robin 73.5/77.9/70.6/73.5, lilac 69.8/70.7/69.6/70.0, butter 82.2/81.1/83.3/80.4 (Lc normal/protan/deutan/tritan; worst 69.6). Tone-on-tone was measured and buys nothing: a label in the fill's own deep hue at the same lightness lands within 2 Lc of plum and is sometimes worse (on blush: own-tone mulberry 66.4/66.4/67.0/65.1 vs plum 66.5/64.7/67.7/65.3; on robin: own-tone teal 64.1/66.1/62.8/64.2 vs plum 65.9/70.4/62.8/65.8; on lilac: grape 61.9/61.5/62.0/62.2 vs plum 62.2/63.2/61.8/62.3; on butter: olive #5a4c24 73.5/72.1/74.5/72.2 vs plum 74.6/73.6/75.6/72.7). Turning the chroma up does not help either (within 1 Lc), because contrast comes from lightness, not hue. It would cost four inks to maintain, and the hue harmony it offers is invisible on blush and robin for this reader (both are seen as grey). Hover and press: do NOT darken the fill much. Each 0.03 of lightness taken off a fill costs the label about 5 Lc (lilac hover #d3baf8 gives the label ink 64/65/64/65; pressed #cbadf6 gives 59/60/58/59). So hover = same fill with a lifted shadow, pressed = one step deeper plus an inset shadow. Muted #7c5378 and caption #8e648a inks are for cream and milk only (on fills they fall to 53-66 and 45-58).

light.why: The shadow colour is 'toffee' #9e7943 = the cream's own hue taken down to L 0.60, so the edge is a deeper cream, never grey. Three layers: a barely-there seam all the way round (lands as #f1e3c7), a tight contact shadow, a wide soft one. Measured from the rendered pixels: the fill alone is only 2.8 from the page; the weakest side (top) reaches 7.4/7.7/7.3/7.0 and the bottom 14.5/15.1/14.4/14.1. Soft, but present on all four sides in every view.

light.css: background:#dbc6fa; color:#4d284a; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / .55), 0 0 0 1px rgb(131 90 180 / .16), 0 1px 2px rgb(131 90 180 / .32), 0 4px 10px -2px rgb(131 90 180 / .30);  /* blush #fbcbcd: rgb(186 85 102) at .16 / .30 / .28 - butter #f9e49f: rgb(164 128 43) at .24 / .36 / .32 - robin #98e3dd: rgb(29 126 123) at .16 / .30 / .26 */  /* hover: same fill, shadow grows to 0 2px 4px + 0 8px 18px -4px; pressed: drop the outer shadows, add inset 0 2px 4px rgb(131 90 180 / .30) */
light.why: Each fill is shadowed by a deep tone of ITS OWN hue (lilac #835ab4, blush #ba5566, butter #a4802b, robin #1d7e7b), plus a white top highlight so it reads as raised. Measured weakest side, worst view: lilac 10.8, butter 10.1, blush 8.5, robin 7.8; bottom edges 18-22 for all four. Butter needs the stronger ring (.24): its fill alone is only 5.6 from cream under tritan, the ring brings the top edge to 10.7/11.2/10.5/10.1.

light.css: background:#fffdf8; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgb(158 121 67 / .28), inset 0 2px 4px rgb(158 121 67 / .22);  /* focus: */ box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgb(131 90 180 / .55), inset 0 2px 4px rgb(131 90 180 / .16), 0 0 0 4px rgb(137 98 197 / .38);
light.why: Inset, so a field reads as a shallow well rather than a raised card, in the same toffee tint (the ring lands as #e4d8c5, a deep cream, not a grey line). Measured: 8.7 at its weakest on the page (13.0 at the top), 10.9 to 15.1 on a card. Focus swaps the tint to lilac and adds a 4px halo: 22 to 26 in every view.

light.element: (d) unlabelled affordance: checkbox, switch track, slider
light.css: /* checkbox off */ background:#fffdf8; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px rgb(131 90 180 / .50), inset 0 2px 3px rgb(131 90 180 / .22);  /* checkbox on */ background:#ae8bdc; color:#fffbf1; box-shadow: inset 0 -1px 0 rgb(77 40 74 / .18), 0 1px 2px rgb(131 90 180 / .40), 0 3px 8px -2px rgb(131 90 180 / .35);  /* switch or slider track, off */ background:#efdcb5; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px rgb(121 86 43 / .30), inset 0 2px 4px rgb(121 86 43 / .28);  /* track on / slider fill */ background:#ae8bdc; box-shadow: inset 0 2px 4px rgb(77 40 74 / .22), 0 1px 2px rgb(131 90 180 / .30);  /* thumb */ background:#fffbf1; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgb(77 40 74 / .30), 0 2px 5px rgb(77 40 74 / .18);
light.why: These have no text, so the edge is the whole signal and gets the strongest treatment, about twice a field's. Still tinted, never grey: the checkbox ring lands as a mid lilac #c1acd6. Measured weakest side, worst view: checkbox off 19.7, switch off 20.1, slider track 19.4 (21.7 to 22.3 on a card). The ON state uses a mid lilac #ae8bdc (L 0.70, the one deliberately non-pastel tone): 30.7/30.9/30.8/27.0 from the page, with a milk tick (Lc 56, fine for a bold glyph). State is always carried by shape too (tick present, thumb position), never by colour alone.

dark.why: A drop shadow cannot show against a dark page, so three things replace it: the card is a lighter step than the page (#2e202d on #211520, 5.0 apart), a lit top edge in cream at 10%, and a luminous seam in lilac at 12% (lands as #372a3a, a lighter plum, not grey). Measured: top 13.2, bottom 6.5, identical in every view. This is the fix for the old dark-mode problem: the edge is drawn with light instead of with shadow.

dark.css: background:#dbc6fa; color:#4d284a; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / .50), 0 0 0 1px rgb(219 198 250 / .30), 0 0 18px rgb(219 198 250 / .28);  /* other fills: the same recipe with that fill's own rgb in the ring and the glow */
dark.why: Same fill and same label ink as light mode. A pastel on the dark page is already 64 to 71 away in every view, so the edge needs no help; the drop shadow becomes a soft halo of the button's own colour, which gives the softness without an outline.

dark.css: background:#160d16; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgb(219 198 250 / .26), inset 0 2px 5px rgb(5 2 5 / .70), 0 1px 0 rgb(254 244 220 / .08);  /* focus: */ box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgb(219 198 250 / .75), inset 0 2px 5px rgb(5 2 5 / .70), 0 0 0 4px rgb(219 198 250 / .30);
dark.why: A well darker than everything around it, ringed in lilac light (lands as #493d51), with a faint cream lip underneath. Measured: 13.9 at its weakest on the page, 10.6 on a card; focused 48. Text inside is cream #f2e7ce at Lc 92.

dark.element: (d) unlabelled affordance: checkbox, switch track, slider
dark.css: /* checkbox off */ background:#160d16; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px rgb(219 198 250 / .60), inset 0 2px 3px rgb(5 2 5 / .60);  /* checkbox on */ background:#dbc6fa; color:#4d284a; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / .50), 0 0 10px rgb(219 198 250 / .40);  /* switch track off */ background:#160d16; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px rgb(219 198 250 / .45), inset 0 2px 4px rgb(5 2 5 / .60);  /* track on / slider fill */ background:#dbc6fa; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / .50), 0 0 12px rgb(219 198 250 / .40);  /* slider track */ background:#160d16; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgb(219 198 250 / .40), inset 0 1px 3px rgb(5 2 5 / .60);
dark.why: Brightest rings in the system because nothing else carries these controls: the checkbox ring lands as #8c7c9f. Measured weakest side, worst view: checkbox off 38.6 (33.6 on a card), switch off 28.2 (23.2), slider track 24.9 (19.9); any ON state is the pastel itself with a glow, 64.3 from the page, with a plum tick or thumb (Lc 70).

measured_cvd_findings: For a red-green-deficient reader (protan and deutan simulations) the five colours become three groups: yellow (cream seen as #faf3db, butter as #f2e19a), blue (lilac seen as #bdcefc / #c0cff8), and pale grey (blush seen as #d3d1cd / #dedacc, robin's egg as #dbdbdd / #cdd1de). Robin's egg sits almost exactly on the hue that red-green-deficient vision sees as colourless, and pink is its opposite on the same line.

Blush vs robin's egg: 13.1 apart in normal vision, 3.2 under protan, 4.5 under deutan. This cannot be tuned away inside 'pastel': a search over 15,552 combinations of lightness, chroma and hue within the pastel bounds topped out at 4.8. The reason is that protan makes blush darker and robin lighter (L 0.861 vs 0.892) while deutan does the reverse (0.888 vs 0.861), so no lightness offset helps both, and the type is not recorded.
Robin's egg vs lilac: 12.5 normal, 7.5 protan, 4.2 deutan. Together with the line above, robin's egg is the colour that cannot be one of the three button colours.

Lilac is the only fill 10+ from the cream page in every view (14.9/14.7/14.8/10.8). Blush 10.1/10.5/8.5/9.8. Robin 13.6/7.8/12.1/15.5 (it loses to protan). Butter is the weakest, 7.5/8.1/7.2/5.6, because it shares the page's hue.

Lilac vs butter is the best-separated pair for red-green deficiency, 17.0/16.7/16.6 (7.0 tritan): they sit at opposite ends of the blue-yellow axis that red-green-deficient vision keeps. That is why they are primary and accent.

Does any of this matter for READING: no. Reading rides on lightness contrast, which barely moves between views. Body ink #643d60 on cream is Lc 83.8/84.2/84.0/82.7; the on-fill label ink #4d284a never drops below 69.6 on any fill in any view. Every edge recipe is a lightness step too: rendered edge measurements differ by under 1.5 between normal vision and any simulation.

Where it DOES matter: telling two fills apart with no label. Rule that follows: never let blush-vs-robin or robin-vs-lilac be the only difference between two things. Buttons carry words, statuses carry an icon and a word, toggles carry a tick or a thumb position.

Ink colours under red-green simulation: plum (#3c4761 / #454c5f), grape (#354b75 / #394b72) and ink blue (#405073 / #394a70) stay visibly coloured; forest teal (#515255, C 0.005) and mulberry (#414347, C 0.007) are seen as plain dark grey; cocoa is a dull olive (C 0.03). So 'not black or grey' is only true for this reader with plum, grape or ink blue.

Statuses: success/danger collapse under red-green simulation (3.2 protan, 4.5 deutan), the classic red-green status trap in pastel form, and success/info collapse under deutan (4.2). A separate mint green would be worse (4.3 from butter under protan, 2.2 from blush under deutan). Hence icon + word + danger's heavy rim (20.5/21.9/19.5/20.4 from the page).

Tritan view (blue-yellow deficiency, rare, and not what the one data point suggests): the picture flips. Blush and robin's egg separate strongly (16.4), lilac goes grey (#d6cdd8), butter turns pinkish (#ffdad2) and sits 4.6 from blush and 5.6 from cream. Text contrast is unaffected (worst 80.4 for labels on butter, 82.7 for body on cream).

All simulations are Machado 2009 at full severity (complete absence of one cone type). Most colour-blind people have the milder 'anomalous' form, so these are worst-case numbers; real separation is likely somewhat better.
risks: Identity change: lilac as primary replaces robin's egg, which is sorbet's current primary and first word of its tagline. The measurement is clear, but it is a brand decision as well. Fallback mapping is in roles.rationale.

Butter on the bare cream page is the palette's thinnest margin (7.5 normal, 5.6 tritan). It depends on its ring (measured 10.1 with it). A butter highlight behind text on cream, with no ring, will be subtle; on a milk card it is 10.2.

Labels on lilac are the tightest text pairing. Body ink there is Lc 62; that is why on-fill labels use the deeper #4d284a (Lc 70). If hover states darken fills the way sorbet does today (pastel 'deepens on hover'), labels on pressed lilac fall to 58-60. Keep hover as a shadow lift.
Links are only 3.9 from body ink. They must be underlined everywhere; a link styled by colour alone is invisible as a link.

The lightest paragraph step, #7c5378, sits at Lc 74.8, a hair under the 75 guideline, at 16px regular weight. Smaller or thinner text (12px captions, light weights) needs a deeper step, not the caption ink. The Lc guidelines themselves are the APCA authors' rules of thumb, not a guarantee for your eyes: the specimen image exists so you can judge the ladder directly.

Colour-blindness type is not recorded. The proposal is built to hold under all three simulations, but if you turn out to be tritan (unlikely), lilac loses its advantage (it greys) and butter drifts toward blush.

Cards are soft by design: 7.0 at the top edge. That is well above 'no emphasis' (the fill alone would be 2.8) but it is not a hard boundary. On a dim or warm-shifted screen (Night Shift pushes everything toward cream) the top edge of a card and butter-on-cream both get weaker. The seam alpha (.14) is the one number to raise if cards feel lost.
The page is now genuinely cream (#fef4dc). Anything with a pure white background (photos, embedded images, third-party widgets) will look like a white card on it, and whiter than the milk surfaces.

Dark mode keeps the full-strength pastel fills (64-71 from the page). Large pastel areas may glare at night. A dimmed set was measured as an option (blush #eeb2b5, robin #7ecfc9, lilac #c9b0ee, butter #e6d088 with ink #421e3f: Lc 65/65/62/74), at the cost of one more set of fills to maintain.

The mid lilac #ae8bdc for ON states (L 0.70, C 0.12) breaks the 'L 0.86+' pastel guide on purpose, for unlabelled controls only. If that reads too strong, the alternative is pastel lilac fill + plum tick (15.4 from a card instead of 31.7).

Chart colours, the scrim, and the other four presets (ocean, forest, noir, midnight) were not examined. sorbet's build currently enforces WCAG 4.5:1 and 3:1 inside buildMode and tools/check-contrast.ts; this palette passes 4.5:1 for text (body 8.07, labels 7.84+) but its edges and pastel fills will fail the 3:1 non-text gate by design, so that gate has to be retired or replaced (an APCA text gate plus a minimum 'sep' for edges would be the like-for-like swap).

propose:colour-science.lens: Colour science first. Every value was derived in OKLCH (L = lightness 0..1, C = chroma, i.e. how colourful, h = hue angle) and measured with colorkit.mjs; nothing is estimated. Terms used below: 'separation' = OKLab distance x100 between two colours (under ~5 hard to tell apart, 10+ clearly different), always quoted as normal / protan / deutan / tritan (the three simulated colour-blindness types, at full severity, so a worst case). 'Lc' = APCA lightness-contrast score (75+ paragraphs, 60+ short labels or larger/bolder text, 45 large headings, 30 the floor). 'Worst view' = the lowest of the four. Method: grid-searched ~4 million pastel combinations for the best worst-case separation, swept ink hue every 10-15 degrees at fixed chroma, composited every shadow colour over its backdrop and measured the resulting edge band. Headline result: for this reader lightness does all the work. Hue changes text contrast by under 2 Lc, and raising the chroma cap from 0.05 to 0.08 improves the worst pastel pair by only 0.5 (5.63 -> 6.12), so the palette can be as soft as wanted provided the four pastels sit on staggered lightness tiers. Scratch scripts: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-homelab/06652a5c-23e2-4a00-8579-52c3b446d84b/scratchpad/cs/ (nothing in the repo was touched).

cream.why: Page backdrop. Visibly warm: chroma 0.029 against today's page #f8f7f5 at 0.003 (ten times more), 4.1 from pure white and 2.7 from today's page. Stays warm under protan/deutan (#faf4df / #fdf7e1, chroma 0.027-0.028). Chosen from a sweep of L 0.955-0.98 x C 0.015-0.035 x h 75-95: at L 0.968 the best worst-case fill separation fell to 5.83, at L 0.98 sRGB clips chroma to 0.020-0.024 (no longer reads as cream), L 0.972 gave 6.0-6.25.

blush.why: Deep tier (L 0.86). 13.0 / 13.7 / 11.0 / 13.3 from cream. Protan simulation darkens it (L 0.860 -> 0.830) while it lightens robin's egg, so blush has to be the darker of the two; the reverse order collapses under protan. Hue 14 rather than a cooler pink (h 2-10) because that widened blush-lilac from 6.4 to 7.6 worst view.

robin.why: Light tier (L 0.905). At equal lightness it collapses into blush (deutan 4.0) and lilac (deutan 2.2), so it must sit on its own tier, and protan lightens it (0.905 -> 0.922), so it must be the light one. That forces it close to cream: 9.2 / 6.1 / 8.8 / 10.1. Kept at low chroma because more chroma pulled it toward lilac under deutan (6.0 -> 5.0 at C 0.07) and a greener hue (h 188) pulled it toward cream under protan (4.7). Hue 205 is sorbet's own 'aqua' ramp hue (204).

lilac.why: Deep tier. Under both red-green simulations it becomes a pale blue that keeps its chroma (#bdcffe / #c0cffa) while cream stays yellow: opposite ends of the one hue axis red-green colour blindness keeps. Result 14.9 / 14.7 / 14.9 / 11.1 from cream, the best of the four.

butter.why: Light tier, at the yellow pole. 8.8 / 9.3 / 8.5 / 7.2 from cream. A lighter butter was measured and rejected: L 0.925 (#f5e7aa) is 4.9 from cream under tritan, L 0.93 is 4.2-4.6. Shares a tier with robin's egg safely because those two differ on the surviving blue-yellow axis (10.5 / 10.0 / 10.3 / 10.4).

surface.why: 'Milk': cards and text fields. Deliberately only 2.3 / 2.5 / 2.2 / 2.0 from the page, i.e. invisible by fill alone; the soft edge recipes carry it, as asked. Body ink gains 3 Lc on it (87.2 vs 83.9). Companion sunken tone for switch/slider tracks: #f7ecd1 (L 0.945 C 0.037).

roles.primary: Lilac #d9c7fc. Best separation from the cream page in every view (14.9 / 14.7 / 14.9 / 11.1), and its deeper tones, which become links, focus ring and control rings, are the most even across simulations: lilac at L 0.68 is 32.7 / 32.7 / 33.0 / 29.5 from cream, where the robin's-egg mid-tone drops to 26.2 under protan and the blush mid-tone to 28.7 under deutan.
roles.secondary: Blush #fbbfc3. Second-best against cream (13.0 / 13.7 / 11.0 / 13.3). Shares the deep tier with lilac but stays 8.7 / 8.0 / 8.6 / 7.6 from it because lilac turns blue and blush turns neutral.
roles.accent: Butter #efdea1. Third against cream (8.8 / 9.3 / 8.5 / 7.2) and clearly apart from both other brand fills for a red-green reader: 15.4 / 15.1 from lilac, 9.5 / 7.2 from blush (protan / deutan).
roles.fourth_pastel_job: Robin's egg #bee9ee gets the jobs where it never stands alone against the page: the 'success' status, and passive or decorative tint (tags, avatars, illustration, progress and skeleton fills, a selected-row wash only where a tick or bold text accompanies it). Never a lone call-to-action. Reason: it is the weakest of the four against cream under protan (6.1) and sits 5.9-6.0 from blush and lilac under deutan. Today's sorbet has it as primary, where it measures 5.0 from today's page under protan.
roles.statuses: Four statuses reuse the four pastels, each with a fixed glyph and a word, always: success = robin's egg #bee9ee + check-circle, warning = butter #efdea1 + triangle, danger = blush #fbbfc3 + octagon-cross, info = lilac #d9c7fc + i-circle. Worst-view separation between status fills: danger-success 5.9, success-info 6.0, warning-info 6.2, danger-warning 6.4, danger-info 7.6, success-warning 10.0. That is tellable side by side but not identifiable alone, so the glyph and the word carry the meaning and colour only reinforces. Danger additionally gets a structural cue no other status has: a 4px leading bar in deep rose #ac505c (43.8 / 47.3 / 41.7 / 43.8 from cream). A fifth, green 'mint' pastel for success was measured and rejected: no mint between L 0.86 and 0.94 clears 4 against everything (best worst case 3.8); it lands 0.4-2.4 from blush under deutan (the literal red-green confusion), 1.0-2.9 from robin's egg under tritan, 0.9-2.2 from cream under protan. Status-coloured text cannot signal status for this reader: the danger text tone #812a39 is 2.5 from body ink under deutan.
roles.focus_and_links: Focus ring: lilac L 0.60 #8e6ac7, 3px, shown on keyboard focus only. 40.7 / 40.9 / 41.2 / 37.5 from cream, Lc 61.1 worst view, at least 26.4 from every pastel fill. It is the one deliberately firm edge, kept for keyboard use. Links: #654199 (L 0.46 C 0.14 h 300), always underlined. Lc 80.4 on cream (78.9 worst view); 18.8 / 19.4 / 18.4 / 8.5 from the recommended cocoa body ink, so a link differs from body text by colour as well as underline in every view (brown vs blue is the axis red-green colour blindness keeps).
roles.surfaces: Page #fef5e0, card/field surface #fffbf1, sunken track #f7ecd1. Dark mode: page #201710 (L 0.214 C 0.020 h 59), surface #2f241c, raised #3b2f25, well #160f09, text #f0e7d2 (Lc 90.5 on page, 88.7 on surface), muted text #c8bca5 (Lc 64.6). The four pastel fills and their ink labels keep the same hexes in dark mode (fills are 62-69 from the dark page).
roles.rationale: Decided by measurement, not by listing order. Separation from the cream page, worst of the two red-green simulations then worst of all four views: lilac 14.7 / 11.1, blush 11.0 / 11.0, butter 8.5 / 7.2, robin's egg 6.1 / 6.1. That ranking is the role order. The structure behind it: blush, robin's egg and lilac collapse pairwise under deutan at equal lightness (blush-robin 4.0, robin-lilac 2.2), so one of the three must sit on its own lightness tier; blush-lilac is the only pair that survives sharing a tier, and protan forces robin's egg to be the light one. Two tiers result: deep (L 0.86: lilac, blush) and light (L 0.90: butter, robin's egg). Every one of the ten pairs among the five colours is at least 5.9 apart in every view, against 2.2 (blush-butter, tritan) and 3.2 (blush-robin, deutan) in today's sorbet, where all three fills sit at L 0.906 because every ramp shares one lightness curve.

text_families.name: Cocoa (recommended)
text_families.why_on_brand: The cream's and butter's own shadow: chocolate on cream. The only on-palette ink that still looks coloured in all three simulations: distance from a same-lightness gray is 6.3 protan / 6.4 deutan / 7.8 tritan (7.0 normal). Body #694323: Lc 83.9 / 85.2 / 83.5 / 82.9 on cream, 87.2 on milk cards. Versus today's text #38342f (L 0.327, chroma 0.010, Lc 93.4) it is 0.09 lighter with seven times the chroma. Where it can land: #815939 (Lc 74.9, worst view 73.9) is the floor for paragraphs and suits muted text; #936b4a (Lc 67.1) for placeholders and labels at 16px semi-bold or larger; #a67c5b (Lc 59.0) is too light for anything but headings of 24px+. Body step on fills, normal (worst view): blush 61.2 (59.6), robin's egg 72.0 (69.2), lilac 61.9 (60.9), butter 70.3 (69.8).

text_families.name: Blueberry
text_families.why_on_brand: The midpoint of robin's egg (h 205) and lilac (h 300). The other hue window that stays coloured in every simulation: 7.1 / 7.7 / 6.3 from gray. Costs 2-3 Lc under protan (body 83.4 normal, 81.1 worst view), so its readable floor is one step deeper than the warm families (L 0.50 reads 71.9 worst view). On fills, normal (worst view): blush 60.7 (55.5), robin's egg 71.5 (70.7), lilac 60.9 (59.5), butter 69.8 (66.6). Cool ink on a warm page: the more striking option, slightly less safe.

text_families.name: Blackcurrant
text_families.why_on_brand: Lilac's own deep tone. Strongly coloured for a red-green reader (7.7 protan / 7.3 deutan from gray, it reads as dark blue) but gray under tritan (1.8). Body Lc 84.3, worst view 82.9. On fills: blush 61.6 (57.4), robin's egg 72.4 (70.7), lilac 61.8 (61.4), butter 70.7 (68.6). Drawback: same hue as the links, so links would differ from body text by underline only.

text_families.name: Aubergine
text_families.why_on_brand: Between lilac and blush, leaning lilac. A compromise: moderately coloured in every view (5.8 / 4.4 / 4.2 from gray) rather than strongly in some. Body Lc 84.3, worst view 83.2. On fills: blush 61.6 (58.7), robin's egg 72.4 (70.1), lilac 61.8 (61.2), butter 70.7 (69.8).

text_families.name: Plum
text_families.why_on_brand: The natural shadow of blush plus lilac, and for normal vision the most obviously 'on brand'. Equally legible (body Lc 84.4, worst view 83.3; on fills blush 61.7 (59.6), robin's egg 72.5 (69.8), lilac 61.9 (60.9), butter 70.8 (70.2)). Not recommended for this reader: under deutan it is 1.9 from gray (4.2 protan), i.e. it would read as the dark gray the owner is trying to leave.

text_families.name: Rosewood
text_families.why_on_brand: Blush's own deep tone. Legible (body Lc 84.3, worst view 83.1, and it gains under protan: 86.3; on fills blush 61.5 (60.1), robin's egg 72.4 (69.5), lilac 61.7 (60.6), butter 70.7 (69.9)). Rejected as body ink: 3.6 from gray under protan and 2.4 under deutan, and to normal vision reddish body text reads as an error state.

text_families.name: Petrol teal
text_families.why_on_brand: Robin's egg's own deep tone. Rejected as body ink: the weakest family in the sweep. Protan lightens teal, costing 2.5-3 Lc at every step (L 0.42 reads 82.6 normal, 80.1 worst view), so it needs one step deeper for the same legibility (#0e4b54: 86.6, worst 84.4), and it is 3.1 / 3.4 from gray under protan / deutan. On blush it is the worst combination measured: 63.9 normal, 58.8 worst view at L 0.38.

propose:colour-science.on_fill_text: One ink everywhere serves this reader better than tone-on-tone (a deeper tone of the fill's own hue). Use the cocoa step one deeper than body, #522e0b (L 0.34), for every label on a pastel fill. Measured Lc, normal / protan / deutan / tritan: on lilac 69.5 / 71.3 / 68.6 / 70.2, on blush 68.8 / 66.7 / 70.0 / 67.6, on butter 77.9 / 77.8 / 78.2 / 77.4, on robin's egg 79.6 / 83.6 / 76.9 / 79.8. All clear the 60 needed for short labels; it also still passes the retired WCAG 4.5:1 (7.3-10.2:1). Tone-on-tone at the SAME lightness changes the worst-view figure by -1.1 to +1.1 Lc (blush +0.8, robin's egg +0.8, lilac +1.1, butter -1.1): no reader benefit, because lightness sets legibility and hue contributes under 2 Lc. Tone-on-tone as usually practised, a mid tone around L 0.50, costs about 16 Lc (on blush 52.9, worst view 51.3; on lilac 53.2) and a mismatched tone is worse still (teal on blush 63.0). The deep fills (lilac, blush, L 0.86) take about 22 Lc off whatever is printed on them, which is why body ink #694323 reads only 61-62 there (worst view 59.6); fine for a bold button label, not for a paragraph, so paragraphs belong on cream or milk. If tone-on-tone is wanted for looks, it is harmless only at L 0.34 or deeper.

light.why: The card fill is only 2.0-2.5 from the page, so the edge does the separating. Shadow colour is 'caramel' #815b1f (rgb 129 91 31; L 0.50 C 0.09 h 75), a deep tone of the cream's own hue, never gray or black. The band right beside the card (1px ring plus half the tight blur, effective alpha 0.208) composites to #e4d5b8: 9.5 / 9.8 / 9.4 / 9.1 from the page and 11.4 / 12.0 / 11.2 / 11.0 from the card. The ring alone would be 5.0-5.5 (too faint), which is why the tight blur layer is there. A caramel shadow separates almost identically in every view because it is a lightness step along the yellow axis.

light.css:
background: var(--fill);            /* #d9c7fc | #fbbfc3 | #efdea1 | #bee9ee */
color: #522e0b;
box-shadow:
  inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.55),
  inset 0 -1px 0 rgb(var(--fill-deep) / 0.18),
  0 0 0 1px rgb(var(--fill-deep) / 0.26),
  0 2px 6px -1px rgb(var(--fill-deep) / 0.30);
/* --fill-deep (the fill's own hue at L 0.50):
   lilac  111 79 161  (#6f4fa1)
   blush  155 66 78   (#9b424e)
   butter 131 100 18  (#836412)
   robin    2 113 123 (#02717b) */
/* hover: ring alpha 0.26 -> 0.40, fill one step deeper
   (#d0bafa | #f9b1b7 | #e9d48b | #a8e2e9) */
light.why: Each fill is edged in a deeper tone of itself. The ring composited over cream, worst view from the page: lilac #d9cad0 11.6, blush #e4c6ba 12.2, butter #decfaa 11.1, robin's egg #bcd3c6 11.3. This is what rescues the light tier: robin's egg alone is 6.1 from cream under protan, with its ring 11.3. On a milk card the same rings measure 11.6-12.5. Hover at alpha 0.40 gives 17.3-18.8; label ink on the deeper hover fills stays at Lc 60.5 or better in the worst view.

A field on a card is milk on milk, so it is drawn as a soft well: an inner caramel ring plus an inner top shadow. The ring composites to #e1d5bf: 11.3 / 11.7 / 11.2 / 11.0 from the field and card, 9.1-9.6 from the page; with the inner shadow (effective alpha 0.293, #daccb3) 13.7-14.6. Typed text Lc 87.2, placeholder #936b4a Lc 69.3 worst view. Focus swaps the ring for lilac #8e6ac7 (37.5-41.2 from cream, Lc 61.1+) with a 3px lilac halo (#d7c4d7, 12.8-14.2 from the page).

light.element: (d) Unlabelled affordance: checkbox, radio, switch, slider
light.why: With no text to carry it, the control wears a firmer but still tinted ring: lilac at L 0.72, #af95df. It is 28.5 / 28.4 / 28.7 / 25.3 from the cream page (Lc 42.8 worst view), 27.0+ from milk (Lc 46.5), 23.1+ from the sunken track (Lc 38.1), and 14.3+ from the lilac fill, so the box is visible checked or not. To a red-green reader it is a blue line on a yellow page. State is never carried by colour alone: the tick is ink on lilac at Lc 68.6, and a switch's state is the thumb's position (thumb edge 15.2+ from the off track, 12.1+ from the on track; on track vs off track 13.7 / 13.4 / 13.5 / 9.0). The outer 3px halo (#ede0ed, 4.9-6.8) is softness only and is not relied on. Sorbet's old rule demanded 3:1 here, which forced a dark teal; this ring is 2.4:1.

dark.why: Measured cause of the old dark-mode problem: a black drop shadow at alpha 0.3 over this page is 3.5 from it (invisible) and at 0.5 only 5.2-5.7; the lighter surface on its own is 5.6-5.7. What replaces the shadow is a LIGHT rim in the cream's own colour (rgb 254 245 224) at low alpha, as if lit from above: outer ring -> #322921, 7.5 from the page; inner ring -> #3b3128, 10.8 from the page and 5.1 from the surface; top highlight (effective alpha 0.192) -> #574c42, 21.1 from the page and 15.4 from the surface. Identical in all four views (it is pure lightness). Elevation is then 'lighter surface plus brighter rim' (raised surface #3b2f25); the black layer is kept for depth only and is not relied on.

The pastels are the bright things on a dark page: 62.4-68.8 from it in the worst view, so no edge is needed for visibility. The same-hue glow softens the boundary instead of outlining it: the ring composites to blush #624946 (21.0 from the page), robin's egg #4f5653 (23.1), lilac #584c57 (21.8), butter #5e533c (23.3). Label contrast is exactly the light-mode figure because fill and ink do not change between modes.

A well darker than its card (9.3-9.6 from the surface) with a cream inner ring: #443d34, 18.9 from the well, 9.3 from the surface, 15.1 from the page (alpha 0.16 was tried and gave only 5.9 from the surface). The lower lip highlight is #443930, 8.3 from the surface. Text Lc 91.2, placeholder Lc 65.4. Focus ring #c6b1f0 (lilac L 0.80): 58.4+ from the page, Lc 64.6.

dark.element: (d) Unlabelled affordance: checkbox, radio, switch, slider
dark.why: In dark mode the pastel itself is the high-contrast element, so the ring is simply lilac at 60% alpha: over the well it is #8b7d9b, 43.6 from the well, 34.1 from the surface, 39.8 from the page, Lc 32.9-35.4; over a card #9586a2, 37.1 from the surface, Lc 37.3. Halo #473b3b is 9.4 from the surface. Checked fill is 64.6+ from the page, tick Lc 71.9, cream thumb 11.1-14.9 from the lilac track and 79.3 from the well.

measured_cvd_findings: Lightness decides legibility; hue is nearly free. At fixed L 0.40 and chroma 0.06, Lc on cream across 24 hues spans only 84.5-86.3. The worst-view figure runs from 82.2 (teal h 195, under protan) to 85.2 (plum/rose). Warm and purple inks gain slightly under protan; teal and blue inks lose 2-3 Lc.

Which inks still look coloured to this reader (distance from a same-lightness gray at L 0.42, protan / deutan / tritan; normal vision is 7.5 for all): cocoa h 60 6.3 / 6.4 / 7.8; blueberry h 262 7.1 / 7.7 / 6.3; blackcurrant h 295 7.7 / 7.3 / 1.8; aubergine h 320 5.8 / 4.4 / 4.2; plum h 340 4.2 / 1.9 / 6.4; rosewood h 12 3.6 / 2.4 / 10.1; teal h 210 3.1 / 3.4 / 7.3. Only two hue windows stay coloured in all three simulations: warm brown h 50-80 and blue h 240-265. Plum, rose and teal collapse to gray under deutan (0.7-2.0).

Today's sorbet puts all three fills at the same lightness (L 0.905-0.906, because every ramp shares one lightness curve). Measured consequence: pink #ffd2e1 vs aqua #adedf3 is 3.2 under deutan and 4.4 under protan; pink vs yellow #f3e096 is 2.2 under tritan; the primary aqua is 5.0 from the page under protan.

The new palette's ten pairs (four pastels plus cream), worst view each: cream-lilac 11.1, cream-blush 11.0, robin-butter 10.0, blush-lilac 7.6, cream-butter 7.2, blush-butter 6.4, lilac-butter 6.2, cream-robin 6.1, robin-lilac 6.0, blush-robin 5.9. Nothing under 5; nothing in the light tier over 10 against cream.

About 6 is the ceiling, not a tuning failure. The best worst-case pair found for any four pastels above L 0.86 on a cream page was 6.0-6.25, across ~4 million combinations, and it barely depends on chroma: 5.63 at a chroma cap of 0.05, 5.81 at 0.06, 6.03 at 0.07, 6.12 at 0.08. 'Truly pastel' costs this reader nothing in separation.

The three-way trap that sets the lightness tiers: at equal lightness (L 0.89) blush-robin is 4.8 protan / 4.0 deutan and robin-lilac is 5.0 protan / 2.2 deutan. Protan also moves them in opposite directions (blush 0.860 -> 0.830, robin's egg 0.905 -> 0.922), so robin's egg must be the lighter one.
Robin's egg is the hardest of the four to see against cream: 6.1 under protan, where it turns to a pale blue-gray #e2e5ee. Its own-hue edge ring lifts the element to 11.3.
A green pastel is unusable for a red-green reader in this set: mint at L 0.86-0.88 is 0.4-2.4 from blush under deutan. No mint lightness clears 4 against all five colours (best 3.8).

Does any of this matter for READING? No. Every text pairing is a lightness contrast and holds in every view: body ink #694323 on cream 83.9 / 85.2 / 83.5 / 82.9, on milk 86.6+, label ink #522e0b on the four fills 66.7 at worst. What the simulations threaten is telling one fill from another and seeing the two light-tier fills against the page, which is handled by edges, glyphs, words and position.
Coloured text cannot carry status. Danger text tone #812a39 vs body ink: 8.7 normal but 6.0 protan and 2.5 deutan; a warning tone #64470e is 1.3-2.8 from body ink in every view.
Links are the exception that works: violet #654199 vs cocoa body ink is 18.8 / 19.4 / 18.4 / 8.5, because brown vs blue is the axis red-green colour blindness keeps.

Tinted shadows are equally visible to every viewer. Caramel #815b1f at alpha 0.22 over cream is 10.0 / 10.4 / 9.9 / 9.7 from the page; the dark-mode cream rim is identical to the first decimal in all four views.

Text on this palette still passes the WCAG rule being retired (body 7.97:1 on cream, labels 7.3-10.2:1 on fills). What is actually dropped is WCAG's 3:1 for non-text shapes: the fills are 1.20-1.45:1 against the page.
risks: The colour-blindness type is not recorded. Everything is measured against all three simulations at full severity, which is a worst case and a model, not the owner's eyes. The cocoa recommendation is the one that does not depend on the type; blackcurrant would be an equally good body ink if the type is confirmed red-green. One look at a rendered sample sheet would settle more than further measurement.

Decision for the owner: ink family. Cocoa is recommended on measurement, but the owner asked to 'see where it can land', so cocoa, blueberry, blackcurrant and aubergine should be shown side by side at the body step (#694323, #364d76, #504374, #5f3f66) and at the floor step.

The four fills are only about 6 apart at worst, so colour can never be the only thing that says which role or status something is. Components must carry a label, glyph, or position. This is a component-contract change, not only a token change.

Statuses reuse brand pastels: danger shares blush with secondary, info shares lilac with primary. Measurement says a separate hue would be invisible to this reader anyway, but it is a product decision: a 'Delete' button and a secondary button share a fill and differ by glyph, word and the deep-rose bar.

Butter at L 0.90 (#efdea1) is deeper and more straw-like than a buttercream. The lighter #f5e7aa is prettier but 4.9 from cream under tritan (6.6-7.3 under protan/deutan). If the type turns out to be red-green, the lighter butter is safe to take.

Body ink on the two deep fills is only Lc 61-62 (worst view 59.6). The rule 'labels on fills use #522e0b, paragraphs never sit on lilac or blush' has to be enforced by tokens (on-primary etc.), not left to each component.

APCA is a draft method and its thresholds assume ordinary weights and sizes. Sorbet's rounded font at 14px regular wants more than Lc 75; for small text use the L 0.34-0.38 steps (#522e0b, #5d3917) rather than the body step.

Sorbet's builder cannot express this palette today: buildMode walks ramps for 4.5:1 and 3:1, every ramp shares one lightness curve, and tools/check-cvd.ts and the contrast gates encode WCAG. The refactor needs per-role lightness tiers and new gates (worst-view separation and Lc floors) or the build will fail or silently re-derive the old shades.

Dark mode is specified only as far as the edges needed: page, surface, well, text and the four recipes are measured; hover states, subtle tints and whether unchanged pastel fills feel too bright on a dark page are not. Dimming the fills to about L 0.82 is the likely adjustment and would need re-measuring.

The focus ring (#8e6ac7) and the control ring (#af95df) are deliberately not pastel. They are tinted and soft, but they are the two places where 'no outlines' gives way to finding a control by keyboard or without a label. If either reads as too harsh, the control ring can lighten to #bba3e8 (L 0.76: 21.2+ from cream, Lc 36.0 worst view) but no further without dropping under the Lc 30 floor.

Screens and night modes shift these numbers: a warm night filter pushes cream toward butter and removes blue from lilac. The light-tier margins (6-7) are the first to go; the text margins are not at risk.
Charts are out of scope. Eight categorical series cannot be made from pastels for this reader; sorbet's chart tokens need their own pass (direct labels, patterns, lightness ramps).

propose:soft-ui-edges.lens:
EDGES FIRST. Terms used throughout: "sep" = how far apart two colours look (OKLab distance x100 from the kit; under 5 is hard to tell apart, 10+ is clearly different). Four numbers in a row are normal / protan / deutan / tritan (the three simulated colour-blindness types); a single number is the WORST of those four. "Lc" = APCA lightness contrast (75+ body text, 60+ short labels, 30 the floor).

TAKEAWAYS
- A same-hue edge is a pure lightness step, so it is identical in every simulation: about 1 sep per 0.01 of OKLCH lightness. 0.05 darker than the fill is where an edge starts to register (sep 5); 0.11 darker is clearly different (sep 10-11). So every pastel gets a "shade" tone 0.14 darker (sep ~14 from its fill) and a "deep" tone near L 0.55 that is the shadow colour.
- A drop shadow alone cannot edge anything: it leaves the top and sides bare. Today's --sb-shadow-md on the new card measures top 3.6, side 5.5, bottom 8.7. Every recipe below has an all-round part (a halo or a 1px ring in the element's own shade) plus a contact shadow plus an ambient one.
- A translucent ring has a dead zone: at alpha 0.4-0.55 it composites to the fill's own lightness and disappears (sep 1-3 from the fill). 0.7 registers (6-8), 0.85 is clear (10-11).
- Unlabelled controls with nothing at 3:1: a 1.5px ring at L 0.72 (#b194de) measures sep 27.1 / Lc 48 / WCAG 2.49:1 against a card, and state is carried by a fill step of sep 13.1 plus a tick at Lc 69 - never by the shadow.
- Dark mode's old problem, measured: today's dark card is a fill step of 6.9 and its black drop shadow adds 0.4 at the top edge. Replacement: lighter surfaces + a top rim light + a luminous ring = 8.1-10.1 outside the card, 16.5 on its inner top rim, 15+ against the page.
- Consequence for roles: lilac is primary (best separation from cream in every simulation), blush secondary, butter accent, robin's egg the state colour.
- Consequence for ink: the obvious on-brand ink (plum) turns dark GRAY under the deutan simulation (chroma 0.015). Aubergine #5c3e71 stays a colour (0.065-0.076) and is the recommendation.

METHOD CHECK: the shadow numbers come from a model (CSS blur radius = Gaussian of half that radius; colour of the first pixel beside the edge, composited in sRGB). I then rendered the recipes in headless Chromium and sampled the real pixels: every predicted colour was within 1-2 RGB steps (e.g. card top edge predicted #ebd9ba, rendered #ebd8b9; butter button top #d3bd70, rendered #d3bd70).

FILES (scratch only, nothing in the repo touched): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-homelab/06652a5c-23e2-4a00-8579-52c3b446d84b/scratchpad/edge-lens/specimen.html (both modes, every recipe), specimen-light.png, specimen-dark.png, shadow.mjs (the edge model), render.cjs (the pixel check).

cream.why: The page. Chroma 0.034 against today's page #f8f7f5 at 0.003 - which is why today's page is a neutral off-white and not cream. Sep from pure white 5.2 / 5.6 / 5.0 / 4.6, so it reads as warm in every simulation. Held at L 0.96 so body ink still reaches Lc 82 and the four fills sit 0.045-0.10 below it.

surface.why: Cards and popovers: a warm white, LIGHTER than the page. Sep from the page is only 3.5 / 3.8 / 3.4 / 3.1 - deliberately not enough alone; the card shadow lifts the edge to 9.8-16.8. It is never the page's own colour: an element the colour of its background is the neumorphism failure (measured on cream: fill step 0, lit edge 2.9, shaded edge 7.6). Second surface, the sunken well #f8eacc (oklch 0.940 0.042 86) for text fields and switch/slider tracks: sep 5.1 from a card, 2.0 from the page, so its inner ring carries it.

blush.why: Sep from cream 10.7 / 11.0 / 8.5 / 10.5; from a card 11.0 worst. Hue 10 (a slightly warm pink) because the grid search found warmer blush stays further from robin and lilac under simulation. Under protan/deutan it keeps almost no chroma (0.002 / 0.017) and reads as light gray #cecdcc / #dbd7cb - for that reader it is the quiet fill, which suits a secondary.

robin.why: Sep from cream 11.5 / 6.8 / 10.5 / 13.6 - protan is its weak spot (it becomes pale gray-blue #dde3f3, chroma 0.023). Set 0.03 lighter than lilac on purpose, because under deutan the two differ by lightness alone; they still land at 4.1. Its one strong pairing is butter: 11.4 worst.

lilac.why: The best separator in the set: sep from cream 14.8 / 14.5 / 14.7 / 10.4; from a card 13.1 worst. Keeps its chroma under protan/deutan (0.070 / 0.064, appearing as light blue #bbcefe / #becefa - consistent with the owner once calling a purple image blue). L 0.859 is the floor of the pastel guide; as the deepest fill it sets the worst case for label contrast (Lc 61.5 body ink, 69.2 strong ink).

butter.why: The weakest against cream, because cream is itself a pale yellow: sep 7.2 / 7.7 / 6.9 / 5.0 (variants from L 0.91 to 0.93 measured 5.2-7.2 normal); from a card 8.2 worst. Taken to L 0.915 and chroma 0.09, the edge of the pastel guide, to buy those points. Keeps full chroma under protan/deutan (0.092 / 0.090) - with lilac, one of only two fills that still look coloured to a red-green reader.

roles.primary: Lilac #dac5fc. The main action fill and the checked/on state of unlabelled controls. Its deeper tones do the structural work: shade #b194de (L 0.72) is every control ring and every unlabelled track fill; deep #7d5aad (L 0.54) is the focus ring and the shadow colour.
roles.secondary: Blush #fec5cc. Secondary buttons and chips. Also the danger fill - told apart from a plain secondary by a deep-rose ring #b14e61 and an icon, not by hue.
roles.accent: Butter #f6e39e. Highlights, badges, 'new' marks; also the warning fill. Used small and mostly on cards, where it separates at 8.2 rather than 5.0 on the bare page.
roles.fourth_pastel_job: Robin's egg #a5e8f2 is the STATE pastel: the success status and the selected/current wash (selected row, active nav item, today's date, text selection). Always doubled by a non-colour cue - a tick, a heavier weight, a deep-tone marker. It never sits beside lilac or blush as a peer button, because those are exactly the pairs that collapse (4.1 and 5.4 under deutan).
roles.rationale: Decided by measurement, in this order. (1) Which pastel stands on the cream page by itself, worst simulation: lilac 10.4, blush 8.5, robin 6.8, butter 5.0. Against a card: lilac 13.1, blush 11.0, butter 8.2, robin 7.9. The primary is the fill that most needs finding, so lilac. (2) Which fills keep their colour for a red-green reader (chroma left under protan / deutan): lilac 0.070 / 0.064 and butter 0.092 / 0.090 keep it; blush 0.002 / 0.017 and robin 0.023 / 0.037 go gray. So primary and accent - the two 'look here' roles - are the two that still look coloured. (3) Which pairs collapse: robin~lilac 4.1 (deutan), blush~robin 5.4 (deutan), blush~butter 5.8 (tritan), blush~lilac 6.5 (tritan), lilac~butter 7.2 (tritan), robin~butter 11.4. Blush is a better neighbour for lilac (6.5) than robin is (4.1), so blush is secondary and robin is kept out of the button row. (4) The edge rule: the weakest separator must not be asked to stand alone as a button on the page, so butter is the accent, not the secondary. (5) What it implies: a grid search over every pastel inside the guide (L 0.86-0.94, chroma up to 0.09) topped out at a worst pair of 5.9 - no pastel set is tellable apart by fill colour alone, because the whole pastel lightness range is about 0.06 wide. Hierarchy is therefore carried by elevation and label (primary raised, secondary flatter), never by hue.
roles.focus_and_links: FOCUS: the one deliberately strong edge, because keyboard use depends on it. Light: box-shadow 0 0 0 2px <colour behind>, 0 0 0 4.5px #7d5aad - sep 42.3 from cream, 45.1 from a card, WCAG 4.75:1 on cream and 5.16:1 on a card, and 18 away from the ordinary control ring so it cannot be mistaken for it. Dark: the same shape in #dac5fc, sep 65.2 from the page. LINKS: #663e9e (oklch 0.46 0.15 300), Lc 78.3 on cream (76.8 worst simulation), 83.9 on a card. It is only 4.4-8.0 from the body ink, so a link is ALWAYS underlined - the underline is the signal, the colour is decoration. Dark link #dac5fc, Lc 76 on the page.
roles.statuses: Fills: success = robin #a5e8f2, info = lilac #dac5fc, warning = butter #f6e39e, danger = blush #fec5cc - no fifth hue. Worst-simulation sep between status fills: warning~success 11.4, warning~info 7.2, danger~info 6.5, danger~warning 5.8, danger~success 5.4, info~success 4.1. The collapse lands on the harmless pair (info vs success). The alternative, a mint green for success (#beecc6), was measured and rejected: danger~success fell to 2.6 under deutan - the one confusion that matters. Fill colour is therefore decoration. What actually tells statuses apart, none of it hue: (1) an icon with its own silhouette - circle-tick, circle-i, triangle-!, octagon-x - drawn in the strong ink (Lc 69-81 on the fills); (2) the status word as text, in ink, never in coloured text; (3) an EDGE-WEIGHT ladder: success and info take the standard 1px ring in their own shade; warning takes a 2px butter-shade ring #cdb55f (sep 13.6 from its fill, 21.4 from a card); danger takes a 2px blush-deep ring #b14e61 (sep 31.6 from its fill, 42.7 from a card, 23.3 from the warning ring, 26.9 from an ordinary field ring) - the darkest edge in the system after focus. These are lightness steps, so they are the same in every simulation.
roles.surfaces: LIGHT: page #fcf1d9 (L 0.960); card #fffbf2 (L 0.989), sep 3.1 from the page plus its shadow; sunken well #f8eacc (L 0.940) for fields and tracks, sep 5.1 from a card. DARK: page #1b1324 (oklch 0.206 0.035 305, the ink's own hue taken dark); card #2c2337 (L 0.276), sep 7.0 from the page; raised #3d324b (L 0.340), sep 6.4 from a card; sunken well #0f0916 (L 0.155), sep 12.0 from a card and 5.0 from the page. In dark mode elevation is spelled as LIGHTER surface, not as shadow.

text_families.name: Aubergine (deep lilac) - RECOMMENDED
text_families.why_on_brand: It is the primary lilac taken dark, so every primary label is tone-on-tone for free. Body step L 0.42: Lc on cream 82.2 (81.5 / 82.4 / 81.2 under protan / deutan / tritan), on a card 87.7, on the sunken well 78.2. On the fills: blush 64.6 (61.6 / 66.3 / 62.8), robin 70.0 (74.0 / 67.1 / 70.0), lilac 61.7 (62.2 / 61.5 / 62.1), butter 73.7 (72.1 / 74.6 / 72.2) - worst anywhere 61.5, so L 0.42 is the lightest step that holds 75+ on every surface AND 60+ on every fill in every simulation. THE DECIDING MEASUREMENT: it still looks like a colour to a red-green reader - chroma kept 0.076 protan / 0.065 deutan (it appears as a dark indigo #334973 / #3b4b70), 0.033 tritan. Lightest still readable, L 0.58 #8b6ba2: Lc 62.9 on cream (61.7 worst), 68.5 on a card - captions and placeholders on cream or a card only, never on a fill (42-55 there). L 0.62 (57.3) is too light for anything but large headings. Proposed tokens: strong #46285a (L 0.34, headings and labels on fills), body #5c3e71, muted #73548a (L 0.50, Lc 73.2), subtle #8b6ba2.

text_families.name: Dusk indigo (between robin and lilac)
text_families.why_on_brand: A fountain-pen blue-violet: the cool counterweight to the warm cream. The most colour-stable ink across all three simulations (chroma kept 0.078 / 0.081 / 0.044 at L 0.42). The cost: cool inks lose contrast under protan (about 2 Lc on cream, 4-5 on blush), so the body step has to be one notch darker - L 0.38: cream 85.7 (83.4 / 86.8 / 84.5); blush 68.2 (63.5 / 70.7 / 66.1), robin 73.5 (75.9 / 71.5 / 73.3), lilac 65.3 (64.1 / 65.9 / 65.4), butter 77.2 (74.1 / 79.0 / 75.5); worst 63.5. At L 0.42 it drops to 59.6 on blush under protan. Lightest still readable L 0.54 #616b9d: 67.4 (65.1 protan); L 0.58 falls to 59.6 under protan.

text_families.name: Cocoa (deep cream)
text_families.why_on_brand: The cream page's own hue taken dark - chocolate on vanilla. The safest pick if the colour-blindness type turns out not to be red-green: it keeps chroma in ALL three simulations (0.045 / 0.052 / 0.060), the best minimum of any family. It is also the quietest and the nearest to a warm dark gray, which is the thing the owner wants to move away from. Body L 0.42: cream 81.6 (82.1 / 81.2 / 81.0); blush 64.1 (62.2 / 65.1 / 62.6), robin 69.4 (74.5 / 65.8 / 69.8), lilac 61.2 (62.8 / 60.2 / 61.9), butter 73.1 (72.7 / 73.4 / 72.0); worst 60.2. Lightest still readable L 0.58 #937359: 62.2 (61.5 worst).

text_families.name: Plum (blush + lilac, deepened)
text_families.why_on_brand: The obvious on-brand ink for normal vision - mulberry on vanilla - and its contrast is as good as aubergine's: body L 0.42 on cream 82.2 (83.2 / 81.9 / 81.3); blush 64.7 (63.3 / 65.8 / 62.9), robin 70.1 (75.7 / 66.5 / 70.1), lilac 61.8 (63.9 / 60.9 / 62.2), butter 73.8 (73.8 / 74.1 / 72.3); worst 60.9. WHY IT IS NOT THE PICK: under the deutan simulation it keeps chroma 0.015 and sits 1.5 sep from a neutral gray of the same lightness (protan 0.034). For a red-green reader it IS the dark gray this refactor is trying to leave. Lightest still readable L 0.58 #9d6785: 62.9 (62.0 worst).

text_families.name: Petrol (deep robin's egg)
text_families.why_on_brand: Robin's egg taken dark - closest to today's sorbet link colour. Weakest of the six for this reader on both counts: it loses the most contrast under protan (3 Lc on cream, 5 on blush) so the body step must be L 0.38, and it goes gray-blue under protan/deutan (chroma 0.029 / 0.042 at L 0.42). Body L 0.38: cream 84.3 (82.0 / 86.4 / 82.5); blush 66.8 (62.1 / 70.3 / 64.1), robin 72.2 (74.5 / 71.1 / 71.3), lilac 63.9 (62.7 / 65.5 / 63.4), butter 75.9 (72.6 / 78.6 / 73.5); worst 62.1. Lightest still readable L 0.54 #3d7886: 66.4 (63.1 protan); L 0.58 falls to 57.8 under protan.

text_families.name: Rosewood (deep blush)
text_families.why_on_brand: Blush taken dark; the warmest ink and the one that gains most under protan (83.3 on cream, reds darken). Included to show the trap in full: under protan its chroma is 0.002 - a plain dark gray #454544 - and 0.020 under deutan. Body L 0.42: cream 81.9 (83.3 / 81.2 / 81.0); blush 64.4 (63.4 / 65.1 / 62.6), robin 69.7 (75.7 / 65.8 / 69.8), lilac 61.5 (64.0 / 60.2 / 61.9), butter 73.4 (73.9 / 73.4 / 72.0); worst 60.2. Lightest still readable L 0.58 #a16870: 62.8 (61.6 worst). Its real use here is not text: #b14e61 from this hue is the danger ring.

propose:soft-ui-edges.on_fill_text:
ONE INK EVERYWHERE serves this reader better than tone-on-tone labels (a deeper tone of the fill's own hue). The numbers, all at the same lightness L 0.42, shown as Lc normal (worst simulation):
- on blush: the one ink #5c3e71 64.6 (61.6) vs blush's own deep tone #703b44 64.4 (62.6)
- on robin: 70.0 (67.1) vs its own tone #175663 68.2 (67.2)
- on lilac: 61.7 (61.5) - here the ink IS the fill's own tone
- on butter: 73.7 (72.1) vs its own tone #5d4c00 72.5 (71.5)
Tone-on-tone is within 2 Lc everywhere and usually slightly worse, because contrast is decided by lightness, not hue. It would add four more inks to verify, and two of them (blush's and robin's) turn gray under protan/deutan, so the matching it exists for is invisible to this reader anyway.

Rule: body ink #5c3e71 on page, cards and wells; LABELS ON A FILL use the strong step #46285a - Lc 72.4 on blush, 77.7 on robin, 69.5 on lilac, 81.4 on butter; worst in any simulation 69.1 (blush, protan). Muted #73548a and subtle #8b6ba2 are never used on a fill (they drop to 52-65 and 42-55).
