Where the fill's own deeper tones DO belong is the edge model: rings, shadows, track fills - non-text.

One measured warning for states: darkening a fill costs label contrast, about 9 Lc per 0.05 of lightness (strong ink on lilac 69.2 -> 60.5 at 0.05 darker -> 55.1 at 0.08 darker; on blush 58.6 and 53.2). So hover and pressed should move the SHADOW (lift, then inset) and leave the fill alone, or darken it by no more than 0.05.

Dark mode: text #f3e7ce on the page Lc 91.9 (90.7 worst), on a card 89.6, on a raised surface 86.0; muted #d0c3a7 68.7 / 66.4 / 62.9 worst-simulation on page / card / raised; subtle #a59779 45.8 - large text and placeholders only. Labels on the pastel fills keep the dark strong ink #46285a (same numbers as light mode).

light.element: (a) Card / panel on the cream page
light.why: Shadow colour is caramel #a16e32 - the cream's own hue at L 0.58, not gray. No ring at all: the first layer is a 6px halo, which is what gives the top and sides an edge. First pixel outside the card: top #ebd9ba, side #e4cead, bottom #dac19b (rendered in Chromium: #ebd8b9 / #e4cead / #dac09a). Sep from the card, worst simulation: top 9.8, side 12.9, bottom 16.8; from the page 6.7 / 9.8 / 13.7; it fades to under 4 by the 7th pixel. Without it the card is 3.1 from the page. For comparison today's --sb-shadow-md on the same card: top 3.6, side 5.5, bottom 8.7.

light.css: background: var(--fill); color: #46285a; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / .55), inset 0 -1px 0 rgb(var(--deep) / .16), 0 0 0 1px rgb(var(--shade) / .85), 0 1px 2px rgb(var(--deep) / .35), 0 4px 10px -2px rgb(var(--deep) / .28); /* lilac: --fill #dac5fc; --shade 177 148 222 (#b194de); --deep 125 90 173 (#7d5aad) | blush: #fec5cc; 229 139 153 (#e58b99); 177 78 97 (#b14e61) | robin: #a5e8f2; 68 193 210 (#44c1d2); 0 135 149 (#008795) | butter: #f6e39e; 205 181 95 (#cdb55f); 151 124 0 (#977c00) */
light.why: Every tone is the fill's own hue: shade = fill minus 0.14 lightness, deep = L ~0.55. First pixel outside, sep from the fill (top / side / bottom, worst simulation), on cream: lilac 10.6 / 11.4 / 12.6, blush 11.1 / 11.7 / 13.0, robin 10.8 / 11.4 / 12.3, butter 11.2 / 11.8 / 12.7; from the page 15.9 or more. On a card: 10.1-12.7 from the fill, 17.7+ from the card. The ring is what rescues butter: with drop shadows only its top edge is 3.3 and its side 2.3. The ring alpha is not free - 0.4-0.55 lands on the fill's own lightness and vanishes (sep 1-3), 0.7 registers (6-8), 0.85 is clear (10-11). The inset white line gives the top an inner lip (sep 5-8 from the fill). Primary vs secondary hierarchy: keep all five layers on the primary, drop the last (ambient) layer on the secondary - elevation, not hue.

light.css: background: #f8eacc; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 2px rgb(161 110 50 / .32), inset 0 0 0 1px rgb(225 191 132 / .9), 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / .9); /* softest variant, no crisp ring: inset 0 1px 3px rgb(161 110 50 / .40), inset 0 0 4px 1px rgb(161 110 50 / .34), 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / .9) */
light.why: A sunken well: darker than the card, carved at the top, with an inner ring of biscuit #e1bf84 (the cream at L 0.82). First pixel inside the edge, sep from the field's own fill: top 16.6, side 13.6, bottom 11.8; from a card around it 21.8 / 18.6 / 16.9; from the bare page 18.7 / 15.5 / 13.7. The fill alone is 5.1 from a card and only 2.0 from the page, so on the page the ring is doing the work. The softest variant swaps the ring for a blurred inner halo and still measures 14.3 / 11.4 / 8.9. Body ink on the well: Lc 78.2 (77.4 worst); placeholder in the subtle step 59.0. Error state: replace the inner ring with inset 0 0 0 2px #b14e61 (sep 38.0 from the fill, 26.9 from the normal ring) plus the octagon icon and the message in ink.

With no text to carry it, the ring is the control. #b194de is lilac at L 0.72: sep 27.1 from a card, 24.3 from the page; Lc 48; WCAG 2.49:1 on a card and 2.29:1 on cream - below the 3:1 being retired, but far above the 10 that counts as clearly different, and the same in every simulation. A lilac-shade ring means 'you can operate this' everywhere in the system. Ladder if it proves too faint on a poor screen: L 0.68 #a686d6 = sep 31.1 / 2.90:1; L 0.64 #9b77cd = sep 35.3 / 3.44:1.

light.css: background: #dac5fc; color: #46285a; /* the tick or dot, 2px stroke */ box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / .55), 0 0 0 1.5px #b194de, 0 1px 3px rgb(125 90 173 / .45);
light.why: What unchecked vs checked looks like with nothing at 3:1: the interior goes from warm white to lilac, sep 15.7 / 15.8 / 15.6 / 13.1; a tick appears at Lc 69.5 (69.2 worst simulation); the box goes from carved-in to slightly raised. Glyph first, lightness second, shadow last - the shadow is never the only cue (the neumorphism failure is pressed and unpressed differing by shadow alone). The ring stays put, 14.0 from the fill, so the shape does not change with state.

light.css: /* track, off */ background: #f8eacc; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 2px rgb(161 110 50 / .35), 0 0 0 1.5px #b194de; /* track, on */ background: #b194de; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 2px rgb(125 90 173 / .45), 0 0 0 1.5px #b194de; /* thumb */ background: #fffbf2; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px rgb(177 148 222 / .9), 0 1px 3px rgb(125 90 173 / .45);
light.why: A thin track has little area, so 'on' uses the shade tone, not the pastel: off vs on track sep 26.4 / 26.2 / 26.6 / 22.6 (the pastel would give only 8.9 under tritan). The thumb is 27.1 from the on-track; on the off-track its ring measures 25.1-25.9 from the thumb and 20.6-21.4 from the track. State = thumb position + track lightness; add a tick inside the thumb when on (strong ink on #fffbf2, Lc 95).

light.css: /* track */ height: 8px; background: #f8eacc; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 2px rgb(161 110 50 / .35), 0 0 0 1px rgb(177 148 222 / .9); /* filled part */ background: #b194de; /* thumb */ background: #fffbf2; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1.5px #b194de, 0 1px 3px rgb(125 90 173 / .45);
light.why: Filled vs unfilled is sep 22.6 worst (26+ otherwise) - a lightness step, so it cannot collapse. The thumb is the same warm-white disc as the switch, 27.1 from the filled track.

light.css: box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--behind, #fcf1d9), 0 0 0 4.5px #7d5aad; /* append the element's own shadow layers after these */
light.why: The one deliberately strong edge. #7d5aad is lilac at L 0.54: sep 42.3 from cream, 45.1 from a card, 32.0 from a lilac fill, 18.0 from the ordinary control ring. The 2px gap is what separates it from a danger ring (12.5 apart in colour, so the structure has to differ).

light.element: Status edge ladder (alerts, status chips, destructive button)
light.css: /* success (robin) and info (lilac): recipe (b) unchanged */ /* warning (butter) */ box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / .55), 0 0 0 2px #cdb55f, 0 1px 2px rgb(151 124 0 / .35), 0 4px 10px -2px rgb(151 124 0 / .28); /* danger (blush) */ box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / .55), 0 0 0 2px #b14e61, 0 1px 2px rgb(177 78 97 / .35), 0 4px 10px -2px rgb(177 78 97 / .28);
light.why: Severity is spelled in edge weight because the fills cannot be told apart reliably (danger~success 5.4, danger~warning 5.8). Warning ring: 13.6 from its fill, 21.4 from a card. Danger ring: 31.6 from its fill, 42.7 from a card, 23.3 from the warning ring. Always with the icon and the word.

dark.css: /* surfaces */ --page: #1b1324; --card: #2c2337; --raised: #3d324b; --well: #0f0916; /* rim light and ring colour */ --rim: 239 230 255; /* #efe6ff */
dark.why: Measured baseline, today's sorbet dark: card vs page 6.9, border vs card 6.9, and the black drop shadow adds 0.4 at the top edge and 3.4 at the bottom - that is the 'no emphasis on edges' problem in numbers. A drop shadow cannot work on a dark page (the tinted pool under the new card measures only 0.8-1.6 against the page). Three things replace it: (1) elevation = a LIGHTER surface - card 7.0 above the page, raised 6.4 above the card, well 12.0 below the card; (2) a rim light - a 1px pale-lilac line inside the top edge, as if lit from above; (3) a luminous ring - a 1px pale-lilac ring outside, lighter than both the element and the page, so the edge is drawn with light instead of a dark line. All three are lightness steps, identical in every simulation.

dark.element: (a) Card / panel on the dark page
dark.why: First pixel outside, sep from the card: top 10.1, side 9.3, bottom 8.1; from the page 17.1 / 16.3 / 15.1. Inner top rim 16.5 from the card. Rendered in Chromium: ring #433b4f (top) and #3e3648 (bottom), rim #564e62. The ring alpha matters: at .12 the bottom edge fell to 1.1 because the dark pool cancels it; .18 is the measured floor. The pool layer is kept only for depth on raised layers.

dark.css: background: var(--fill); color: #46285a; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / .5), inset 0 -1px 0 rgb(var(--deep) / .3), 0 0 0 1px rgb(var(--fill-rgb) / .35), 0 0 14px -2px rgb(var(--fill-rgb) / .35); /* --fill-rgb: lilac 218 197 252 | blush 254 197 204 | robin 165 232 242 | butter 246 227 158; --deep as in light mode */
dark.why: Same pastel hexes as light mode. Against a dark page a pastel needs no help to be found: fill vs page 65.2 (lilac), butter vs a card 64.1. The glow is the 'similarly coloured shadow' turned into light - it takes the first pixel outside to L ~0.51-0.57 and fades to sep 3 by the 7th pixel. The inner bottom lip (sep 9.1-9.4 from the fill) keeps the button from reading as a flat sticker.

dark.css: background: #0f0916; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 3px rgb(5 2 10 / .7), inset 0 0 0 1px rgb(239 230 255 / .34), 0 1px 0 rgb(239 230 255 / .12);
dark.why: A well darker than everything around it, with a luminous inner ring. On a card: fill step 12.0; ring vs the well 16.4 / 22.4 / 26.9 (top / side / bottom); ring vs the card 4.5 / 10.4 / 14.9. On the bare page: fill step only 5.0, ring vs the page 11.5 / 17.4 / 21.9 - the ring carries it there. At alpha .20 the ring matched the card's own colour (sep 1.8) and disappeared; .34 is the measured setting. Text #f3e7ce on the well: Lc 92.7.
Same lilac-shade ring as light mode; here it is the LIGHT thing on a dark ground: sep 44.3 from a card, 51.3 from the page, WCAG 5.82:1 on a card. Dark mode is the easy mode for controls.

The pastel itself is the strong tone here: sep 65.2 from the page, 58.2 from a card.

measured_cvd_findings: What each fill becomes (protan / deutan / tritan): blush #fec5cc -> #cecdcc / #dbd7cb / #ffc1c7; robin #a5e8f2 -> #dde3f3 / #d0d8f2 / #89eeeb; lilac #dac5fc -> #bbcefe / #becefa / #d5cdd8; butter #f6e39e -> #f1e099 / #f6e6a0 / #ffd9d1; cream #fcf1d9 -> #f7f0d8 / #faf3da / #ffedea.

For a red-green reader only two of the four pastels still look coloured. Chroma left under protan / deutan: lilac 0.070 / 0.064 (reads as light blue), butter 0.092 / 0.090 (still yellow), robin 0.023 / 0.037 (pale gray-blue), blush 0.002 / 0.017 (light gray). Under tritan it flips: robin 0.095 and blush 0.072 keep their colour, lilac drops to 0.017 (grayish) and butter halves to 0.044 and turns pinkish.

Pairs between fills, sep normal / protan / deutan / tritan: robin~lilac 11.2 / 7.9 / 4.1 / 10.9 (collapses under deutan); blush~robin 13.3 / 7.1 / 5.4 / 16.8; blush~butter 11.3 / 10.5 / 8.4 / 5.8; blush~lilac 8.3 / 7.3 / 8.5 / 6.5; lilac~butter 17.3 / 17.0 / 16.8 / 7.2; robin~butter 13.5 / 11.4 / 13.2 / 14.0 (the only pair that is clearly different everywhere).

This is a property of pastels, not of these particular hexes: a grid search over hue, lightness and chroma inside the pastel guide found no set of four whose worst pair beats 5.9. The usable lightness range (0.86-0.92) is about 6 sep wide, and lightness is the only thing that survives every simulation.

Each fill against the cream page: lilac 14.8 / 14.5 / 14.7 / 10.4; blush 10.7 / 11.0 / 8.5 / 10.5; robin 11.5 / 6.8 / 10.5 / 13.6; butter 7.2 / 7.7 / 6.9 / 5.0. Against a card: lilac worst 13.1, blush 11.0, butter 8.2, robin 7.9.

Edges do not degrade at all. Every edge in the recipes is a same-hue lightness step, and those measure the same in all four views - e.g. lilac shade vs lilac fill 14.2 / 14.4 / 14.4 / 14.0; control ring vs card 27.1 worst; card halo vs card 10.2 / 10.9 / 10.0 / 9.8 at the top edge.

Text contrast barely moves. Recommended ink #5c3e71 on cream: Lc 82.2 / 81.5 / 82.4 / 81.2. The largest shift anywhere is on blush under protan (64.6 -> 61.6), because protan darkens the pink fill. Cool inks (indigo, petrol) lose 2-3 Lc on cream and 4-5 on blush under protan; warm and purple inks do not.

Whether the ink still looks like a colour, chroma left at L 0.42 under protan / deutan / tritan: aubergine 0.076 / 0.065 / 0.033; dusk indigo 0.078 / 0.081 / 0.044; cocoa 0.045 / 0.052 / 0.060; petrol 0.029 / 0.042 / 0.073; plum 0.034 / 0.015 / 0.078; rosewood 0.002 / 0.020 / 0.094. Plum and rosewood are dark gray to a red-green reader.

DOES IT MATTER FOR READING? No. Reading rides on lightness, and the worst body-text number anywhere in the system is Lc 61.5 (body ink on a lilac fill), 69.1 with the strong ink used for labels. What is lost is telling the FILLS apart by colour - so nothing may depend on that: roles are carried by the label, statuses by icon + word + edge weight, state by glyph + lightness + position, links by underline.

Status fills as assigned (success robin, info lilac, warning butter, danger blush): the pair that collapses is info~success at 4.1 (harmless). A mint green for success was measured and rejected: danger~success 2.6 under deutan.
risks: The colour-blindness type is not recorded. The simulations are full-strength (Machado, severity 1.0), which is the worst case for the common partial forms, but the recommendation of aubergine ink leans on the reader being red-green: under tritan aubergine keeps only 0.033 chroma and cocoa (0.060) or dusk indigo (0.044) would be the better ink. Worth settling with a five-minute look at the specimen, or by asking.

The unlabelled-control ring is 2.49:1 on a card and 2.29:1 on cream - below WCAG's 3:1 on purpose. It measures sep 24-27 and Lc 42-48, but those are numbers, not the owner's eyes on the owner's screens. Fallback steps are measured (L 0.68 = 2.90:1, L 0.64 = 3.44:1).

Rings are still 1px lines. They are the element's own hue rather than gray or black, and they are box-shadows, but the owner may still read a 0.85-alpha ring as an outline. Ringless variants are measured for the card (halo, 9.8-16.8) and the field (8.9-14.3); the button has no ringless version that keeps butter's top edge above 3.3.

The 5 / 10 thresholds describe patches of colour; a 1px line needs more difference than a patch to be seen. That is why control rings are specified at 24-27 and several-pixel halos at about 10 - a judgment, not a measurement.
Butter on the bare cream page is 5.0 at worst (tritan) and robin 6.8 (protan). Both depend on their ring (15.9+) when they sit directly on the page. Butter should stay an accent, not a large surface.

Pale-on-pale edges are the first thing lost on a washed-out display or in sunlight - the standing criticism of soft-shadow interfaces. The mitigations here are the contact shadow hugging the edge, state never carried by shadow alone, and a focus ring at sep 42; they reduce the risk, they do not remove it.

Danger shares the blush fill with the secondary button. It is separated by the 2px deep ring #b14e61 (31.6 from the fill), the octagon icon and the word - all hue-free - but a destructive button now LOOKS gentler than today's solid red #cb2c31. That is the direct cost of 'truly pastel'.
Success is robin's egg, not green. Conventional for nobody, but measured: a pastel green and the blush danger fill are 2.6 apart under deutan.

Dark mode: muted text on a raised surface is Lc 62.9 at worst and subtle text is 45.8 - subtle is for large text and placeholders only. A field on the bare dark page has a fill step of only 5.0; its ring (11.5+) carries it.

Recipes are measured on flat cream, card and dark-page backgrounds. Over photos, or nested inside a pastel panel, the numbers change; shadows are per-hue, and a mismatched pairing (a butter button with a lilac shadow) was not measured.

Size of the refactor this implies in sorbet (read, not changed): tokens/rules.ts is a list of WCAG 4.5:1 and 3:1 pairings that fails the build; semantics.ts picks shades by walking a ramp until 4.5:1 and has the pastel/'-solid' split built around 3:1; emit.ts makes five shadows from ONE tint per preset and plain black in dark mode. This proposal needs per-hue shade/deep tokens, ring and rim tokens, a surface ladder, and a new gate (APCA Lc floors for text, sep floors for edges, each checked under the three simulations) in place of rules.ts. Until that gate exists, nothing enforces these numbers.

Hover and pressed states were not designed in full. Only the constraint is measured: every 0.05 of fill darkening costs about 9 Lc of label contrast (strong ink on blush falls to 58.6 at hover-dark, 53.2 at pressed-dark).

judge:measured-legibility.lens:
CAN THIS READER READ IT. Everything below was re-measured with colorkit.mjs; nothing in the repo was touched. Scripts: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-homelab/06652a5c-23e2-4a00-8579-52c3b446d84b/scratchpad/judge-read/ (m1-m11.mjs).

Units: Lc = APCA lightness contrast (0 invisible, ~100 black on cream). sep = how far apart two colours look (OKLab distance x100; under 5 hard to tell apart, 10+ clearly different). 'kept' = chroma (colourfulness) left after a colour-blindness simulation; 0 is gray, and today's sorbet text #38342f keeps 0.010. Four numbers in a row = normal / protan / deutan / tritan; 'worst' = lowest of the four.

TAKEAWAYS
- The proposals' arithmetic is sound: 152 of 152 ladder steps reproduce (hex, Lc, WCAG), and every palette separation I re-ran matches. The errors are in the inferences, not the numbers.
- All three judge text against 'Lc 75 paragraphs / Lc 60 labels' without checking sorbet's real sizes. APCA's own page (fetched) ties Lc 75 to 18px regular, 16px medium or 14px bold, and Lc 60 to 16px bold or 24px regular. Sorbet sets body 16px/400, button labels 14px/600, chips 14px/500, badges and field hints 12px. So body at L 0.42 (Lc 82-84) is right on the line, not comfortably over it; the 'lightest readable' steps are not paragraph ink at sorbet's size; and button labels at Lc 67-70 are under.
- Labels on lilac and blush have a hard ceiling no ink can beat: pure black on lilac #dac5fc is only Lc 77.8, on blush 80.8. Today's sorbet prints labels at Lc 79-81 (fills at L 0.906); every proposal drops the primary button label to 69-70. Nobody flagged that as a regression.
- To a red-green reader every ink from hue 262 to 310 is the SAME ink: blueberry, indigo, blackcurrant, grape and aubergine sit 0.2-2.2 apart under protan/deutan. The real choice is three looks: dark blue (any of those), olive-brown (cocoa), or slate-gray (plum, rosewood, teal).
- More colour is free: grape at chroma 0.14 reads Lc 84.1 against 83.7 at 0.09. The proposals capped ink chroma at 0.045-0.09 for no measured reason.
- Role assignment is unanimous and holds: lilac primary, blush secondary, butter accent, robin's egg for success/selected.

scores.strongest: Most trustworthy palette structure and the only type-independent ink argument. Its two lightness tiers give the best worst-case fill separation of the three: every one of the ten pairs is 5.9+ in every view (re-measured exactly), against 3.2 for B and 4.1 for C. Its recommended cocoa #694323 reads Lc 83.9 / 85.2 / 83.5 / 82.9 on cream and keeps colour in all three simulations (kept 0.057 / 0.064 / 0.079), so it does not depend on the unrecorded colour-blindness type. Label ink #522e0b on the fills matches to the decimal (worst 66.7 blush, 68.6 lilac, 76.9 robin, 77.4 butter).
scores.weakest: Worst on-fill reading of the three, caused by its deep blush (L 0.860): body ink on blush is 59.6 worst view (under its own 60 line), labels 66.7, and its hover fills take the label down to 60.5 on blush. 'All clear the 60 needed for short labels' is applied to 14px/600 buttons and 12px badges, sizes APCA's Lc 60 does not cover. Its paragraph 'floor' #815939 is 73.9 worst view, under 75. Five of seven families quote on-lilac figures 0.5-0.7 Lc too low (stale lilac hex), and the WCAG range for labels on fills is quoted 7.3-10.2:1 where the four fills measure 7.60-9.17:1.

recommended_synthesis.roles: Primary lilac #dac5fc, secondary blush #fbc7c9, accent butter #f5e3a2, robin's egg #aaeff7 for success and selected/decorative, never a lone button. All three proposals chose this independently and it holds: lilac is the furthest fill from cream in every view (worst 11.1) and with butter one of the two fills still coloured for a red-green reader (lilac keeps 0.070 / 0.064, butter 0.086 / 0.085; blush 0.007 / 0.021 and robin 0.021 / 0.034 go pale gray). It survives best on A's two lightness tiers: this palette's worst pair is 5.8 in the red-green views (robin~lilac, deutan) and 5.5 in any view (blush~butter, tritan), against 3.2 for B and 4.1 for C as written. Reading rules that follow: (1) labels on fills use the family's L 0.30 step, not L 0.34 - grape #372052 gives 72.2 lilac / 72.1 blush / 81.8 robin / 82.1 butter worst view, 3 Lc more than the proposals' label inks; (2) the primary is the darkest fill, so its label is the weakest text in the system - set button labels 16px/600 or 14px/700, not today's 14px/600; (3) 12px text (badges, hints) only on cream or milk, where the L 0.34 step reads Lc 90-95; no ink reaches that on any fill; (4) statuses reuse the four pastels with icon + word, status text in the normal ink; (5) links always underlined - with a purple ink the link is only 3.3-4.3 from body text; with cocoa ink a grape link is 13.1 / 13.4 / 13.2 / 7.0 away.

text_families.note: Body L 0.42 #574075: Lc on cream 83.7 / 82.8 / 84.2 / 82.5, milk 87.6, fills 61.5-73.6. Kept 0.081 / 0.073 / 0.023: reads as dark indigo to a red-green reader, gray under tritan. No protan contrast penalty, unlike the blues. Label step L 0.30 #372052. Lightest step holding Lc 75 worst view: L 0.485 #695289 (18px regular or 16px medium only). recommended_synthesis.edges: Not re-measured here (shadow composites are outside this lens); these are the reading constraints an edge recipe must respect. (1) Text fields on milk #fffbf1 with an inset tinted ring (A and B), not C's sunken well: 87.6 against 78.2 for typed text. (2) Hover and pressed move the shadow, not the fill (B and C): each 0.02 of fill darkening costs the label about 4 Lc, and A's hover fills land at 60.5 on blush. (3) Lilac stays at L 0.859: lightening it to 0.88 buys the label +4 Lc but drops robin~lilac to 3.5 under deutan; revisit only if primary labels still feel thin at the larger type. (4) Own-hue tinted shadows and rings as all three propose; unlabelled controls ringed in lilac near L 0.72 (#af95df / #b194de re-measured: 25-29 from cream, Lc 43-48). (5) Dark mode: B's text ladder (#f2e7ce 91.5, muted #d7c9ae 73.4 on page, 71.8 on card); A's and C's muted inks are 65-69.

refuted_claims: B: plum #643d60 'stays a colour ... does not turn into the dark grey you are leaving'. Under deutan it keeps chroma 0.033 and is 3.2 sep from a same-lightness gray (under the 5 'hard to tell apart' line). It ranks 10th of 19 offered body inks for colour kept in the red-green views.

B: 'not black or grey is only true for this reader with plum, grape or ink blue'. A's cocoa #694323 keeps 0.057 / 0.064 / 0.079, more than B's plum (0.046 / 0.033 / 0.056) in every view. B's cocoa looked gray because it was given chroma 0.045 against plum's 0.075; at equal chroma 0.08 cocoa keeps 0.067 / 0.073 and plum 0.050 / 0.036.

A, B and C: on-fill labels 'clear the 60 needed for short labels'. Sorbet's button label is 14px/600, chips 14px/500, badges 12px/600.

A and B: L 0.50 as the paragraph floor 'on the 75 line'. Worst view is 73.3-74.2 for every family (A cocoa 73.9, B plum 73.6), and Lc 75 is APCA's minimum for 18px regular or 16px medium; sorbet body is 16px regular, where the line sits near Lc 82 (my interpolation between APCA's 18px at 75 and 14px at 90).

A: five families quote on-lilac figures from a stale lilac. A: label ink 'passes the retired WCAG 4.5:1 (7.3-10.2:1)' on fills. Measured on the four fills: 7.60 / 7.71 / 8.91 / 9.17:1. Also 'teal on blush 63.0' in one place and 63.9 in another; 63.9 is correct.

A: 'hue is nearly free, under 2 Lc'. True on cream (82.6-84.4 across families at L 0.42). Not true on blush under protan, where cool inks lose 4-5: blueberry 55.5 against cocoa 59.6 at the same lightness.

C: the six families are six choices. For a red-green reader, hues 262-310 collapse: blackcurrant~grape 0.2 / 0.5, grape~aubergine 0.6 / 0.4, indigo~grape 1.5 / 1.2, blueberry~grape 2.2 / 0.9 (protan / deutan). Same holds across A's and B's lists.

Unflagged by all three: the primary button label gets WORSE than today. Today's text on today's fills reads Lc 78.6-81.1; the proposals put it at 68.6-69.6 on lilac, and black itself cannot exceed 77.8 there.

Too dark to be worth showing: every L 0.30 step (Lc 93.3-94.9 on cream) is at or above today's text contrast (93.4), so it is no move away from 'dark'. The teal ones (#00353c, #023536, #004049, #003f4b) have a zero red channel and read plain dark gray under protan (kept 0.005-0.03).
open_risks: Colour-blindness type is still unrecorded. Grape is the pick only if red-green (it goes gray under tritan, kept 0.023); cocoa is the pick that does not depend on it. The plum-beside-grape row on the ladder sheet answers it in one look.

Label contrast on lilac and blush is capped by the fills, not the ink (black = 77.8 on lilac). Reaching a comfortable label means a type change in sorbet (button labels to 16px/600 or 14px/700; 12px badges and hints off the fills). That is a component change no proposal scoped.

The 'Lc 82 for 16px regular' line is my interpolation between two published APCA anchors; the second source fetch failed (session limit), so the per-size lookup table itself is unverified. APCA thresholds are its authors' rules of thumb, not a measurement of this reader.

Body ink at L 0.42 has no headroom: Lc 82-84 on cream is on the line for 16px regular, so 'see how light it can land' has an honest answer of about L 0.42 for paragraphs, L 0.485 only at 18px regular or 16px medium, and L 0.58-0.60 for large headings only.

The synthesis blush, robin and butter are new hexes (0.5-1.0 from proposal values). They are measured but appear in no rendered specimen; B's and C's specimen images show their own palettes, not this one.
Robin's egg on bare cream is 6.0 under protan and butter 5.6 under tritan: both depend on their own-hue ring. I did not re-measure any shadow or ring composite.
Simulations are Machado 2009 at full severity, a worst case and a model. Most colour-blind people have the milder form, so real separations are likely better and real 'kept' colour higher.
Dark mode was checked for text only (page, card, muted, caption). Whether full-strength pastel fills glare on a dark page, and dark hover states, are unmeasured by anyone.

Sorbet's build still enforces WCAG 4.5:1 and 3:1 in tokens/rules.ts and semantics.ts (read, not changed). Until a replacement gate exists (Lc floors per text size, sep floors for edges, each under the three simulations) nothing enforces any number in this review.

judge:pastel-fidelity.lens:
IS IT WHAT WAS ASKED FOR: "truly pastel, led by a cream backdrop, blush pink, robin's egg blue, lilac purple, butter yellow", soft same-colour edges, an on-brand ink that is not black or grey.

TERMS: "sep" = how far apart two colours look (OKLab distance x100; under ~5 hard to tell apart, 10+ clearly different). Four numbers in a row = normal / protan / deutan / tritan (the three simulated colour-blindness types at full severity). "Lc" = APCA lightness contrast (75+ paragraphs, 60+ short labels, 30 the floor). L / C / h = OKLCH lightness 0..1 / chroma (how colourful) / hue angle.

TAKEAWAYS
- Every number I re-ran matched the kit to the decimal (all three palettes, all 21 ink families, the pair tables, the reference distances). What fails is seven interpretive claims, listed in refuted_claims.
- The three proposals agree far more than they differ: cream within 1.2 sep of each other, card surface identical (#fffbf1), lilac within 0.5, butter within 2.2. The only real disagreements are robin's egg (up to 5.2 apart) and blush (2.9).
- B is the most faithful to the five names, but puts blush and robin's egg on the wrong lightness tiers: worst pair 3.2. A has the right tiers but washes robin's egg out (chroma 0.045) and dulls butter toward straw. C has the best ink and the best dark mode but the least soft light-mode edges.
- Roles are unanimous (lilac primary, blush secondary, butter accent, robin's egg as the state colour) and I found nothing to overturn.

WHAT I WOULD CHANGE IN THE BEST PROPOSAL (B)
1. Blush 0.018 darker: #fbcbcd -> #f9c3c6. Still 1.0 sep from classic blush #f4c2c2.
2. Robin's egg 0.035 lighter, same chroma, hue 190 -> 197: #98e3dd -> #a6edee. Worst pair in the palette goes from 3.2 to 5.2 and no named colour is given up.
3. Ink: swap B's plum pick (3.2 from grey under deutan) for aubergine hue 310 (7.7 / 6.5 from grey under protan / deutan), which is C's pick and near B's own runner-up.
4. Dark mode: take C's edge recipe (every side 12.9+ from the page) in place of B's (6.6 at the bottom edge).
5. Butter and robin's-egg buttons need a stronger own-colour edge than B's .16 ring; lilac and blush do not.

Also the only ink measured as still coloured in all three simulations: cocoa #694323 is 6.3 / 6.4 / 7.8 sep from a grey of the same lightness, and it gives links the best separation from body text (18.8 / 19.4 / 18.4 / 8.5).

refuted_claims: B: 'blush vs robin's egg cannot be tuned away inside pastel; a search over 15,552 combinations topped out at 4.8' and 'no lightness offset helps both protan and deutan'. REFUTED. A's own palette holds 9.4 protan / 5.9 deutan. A name-faithful variant (blush #f9c3c6 at L 0.866, robin's egg #a6edee at L 0.900, hue 197, chroma 0.070) holds 8.8 / 5.4. The lever is putting robin's egg at least 0.034 lighter than blush; B has it 0.019 darker.

B: plum ink #643d60 'stays a colour under red-green simulation ... does not turn into the dark grey you are leaving'. REFUTED for deutan: 3.2 sep from a grey of the same lightness (#4d4d4d), under the kit's 'hard to tell apart' line; 5.2 under protan. B's own runner-up grape #574173 is 7.7 / 6.9 and C's aubergine #5c3e71 is 7.7 / 6.5.

B: the button recipe's 'measured weakest side' figures (lilac 10.8, blush 8.5, robin 7.8) are presented as what the edge delivers. They are identical to the bare fill-versus-page separations (lilac~cream 10.8 tritan, blush~cream 8.5 deutan, robin~cream 7.8 protan). The .16 ring adds nothing on that side; only butter's .24 ring does real work (5.6 -> 10.1).

B: the dark card is 'the fix for the old dark-mode problem'. Only at the top. Bottom edge is 6.6 sep from the page and 1.7 from the card (B's own rendered figure is 6.5), against a bare fill step of 5.0. C's recipe measures 12.9 from the page and 6.0 from the card on the same check.

A: 'each fill is edged in a deeper tone of itself'. Not after compositing over cream: the lilac ring lands as #d9cad0 with chroma 0.019 (near neutral), the robin's-egg ring as #bcd3c6 at hue 161 (a sage grey, not hue 205), and the blush ring is 1.5 / 1.3 sep from its own fill under protan / deutan. The rings still separate from the page (11.3-13.3), so the function holds; the 'own colour' description does not.

A: robin's egg must stay at low chroma because 'more chroma pulled it toward lilac under deutan'. The cost is small: 6.0 at chroma 0.045 vs 5.2 at chroma 0.07. What it gives up is the name: at 0.045 the colour is 7.2 sep from sorbet's own 'true robin's-egg' aqua-300 #82dfe7 and 3.1 from powder blue.

recommended_synthesis.roles:
Unanimous across the three proposals, and my measurements agree.
- PRIMARY: lilac #dbc6fa. The heaviest fill (14.9 sep from cream) and one of two that stay coloured for a red-green reader.
- SECONDARY: blush #f9c3c6. 8.0 / 7.5 / 8.2 / 6.5 from lilac.
- ACCENT: butter #f9e49f. Used small or on cards (10.2 from a card vs 7.5 from the page). 17.0 / 16.7 / 16.6 / 7.0 from lilac, the best-separated pair.
- FOURTH: robin's egg #a6edee is the state colour (success, selected, progress, decoration). Never a lone button on the bare page: 5.7 from cream under protan.
- STATUSES: the four pastels, no fifth hue (success robin's egg, warning butter, danger blush, info lilac). Told apart by icon shape plus the word, never by colour (danger~success 5.4, info~success 5.2 at worst). Danger adds B's soft rose rim (lands #dca5a1: 20.5 / 21.9 / 19.5 / 20.4 from the page, 9.4 from the blush fill), not a dark ring.
- FOCUS: C's #7d5aad behind a 2px gap, 45.6 / 45.9 / 46.2 / 43.0 from cream. The one deliberately firm edge.
- LINKS: #663e9e, always underlined; only 7.6 / 8.0 / 7.5 / 4.4 from the body ink, so the underline is the signal.
- VISUAL WEIGHT (normal-vision sep from cream): blush 12.0, robin's egg 11.1, lilac 14.9, butter 7.5; on a card 13.6 / 11.7 / 15.4 / 10.2. All four sit at L 0.86-0.92 and chroma 0.062-0.090; none shouts. Worst pair anywhere in the palette: 5.2 (robin~lilac, deutan), against 5.9 for A, 3.2 for B, 4.1 for C.

LIGHT
- Card: C's ringless caramel halo (shadow colour #a16e32, the cream's own hue taken dark). Top edge lands #ebd9ba: 7.0 sep from the page, 10.2 from the card; sides #e4cead: 10.1 / 13.3. Butter and robin's egg are 5.6 and 5.7 from cream at worst and need more: use C's own-hue 'shade' tone (the fill minus 0.14 lightness), but as a short blurred halo rather than C's 1px ring at .85. Low-alpha rings of a dark tone (A .26, B .16) turn near-grey over cream (lilac ring chroma 0.018-0.019).
- Hover and pressed: move the shadow, leave the fill (B and C agree; darkening a fill by 0.05 costs about 9 Lc on its label).
- Fields: B's inset well on a milk fill (#fffdf8, ring lands #e4d8c5), not C's tan well #f8eacc, which costs body text 9.5 Lc.

- Danger: B's soft rim (#dca5a1) plus octagon icon plus the word. Not C's 2px #b14e61 ring or A's #ac505c bar, both seen as neutral dark grey under protan.
DARK
- C's recipe unchanged: page #1b1324, card #2c2337 (7.0 apart), raised #3d324b, well #0f0916; top rim rgb(239 230 255 / .22) at 16.5 from the card; ring at .18 lands 15.5 from the page and 12.9 at the bottom edge. Text #f3e7ce Lc 91.9 on the page, 89.6 on a card. The page takes the ink's hue (305), so it pairs with the aubergine ink; if cocoa is chosen, use A's brown page #201710 with C's surface steps.

open_risks: Nobody has SEEN the synthesis. Blush #f9c3c6 and robin's egg #a6edee are measured, not rendered, and the blurred own-hue halo for butter and robin's-egg buttons is a design suggestion with no pixel measurement behind it. It needs one specimen sheet with pixel sampling before any token is written.

Ink family is a decision for the owner's eyes, not the kit: aubergine #5c3e71 vs cocoa #694323 at the body step, plus aubergine at chroma 0.09 / 0.11 / 0.13 and at L 0.42 / 0.46 / 0.50. The measurements only say all of these are readable.

Colour-blindness type is still unrecorded. The synthesis is tuned for normal plus red-green; its tritan worst cases are butter~cream 5.6 and blush~lilac / blush~butter 6.5, and aubergine ink is only 3.3 from grey under tritan (cocoa is 7.8). All simulations are full severity, a worst-case model rather than the owner's eyes.

Robin's egg on the bare cream page is 5.7 sep under protan (6.5 on a card). It depends on its edge and on never standing alone; the lighter tier that separates it from blush and lilac is exactly what costs it against the page.

Body ink on blush is Lc 59.9 in the worst view, just under the 60 label line (62.0 on lilac). The rule 'labels on fills use the L 0.34 step #46285a, paragraphs never sit on a fill' has to live in tokens, not in each component.

Fills are 5.2-5.4 apart at worst, so colour can never be the only thing that says which role or status something is. That is a component contract change (icon, word, position), not just a token change.
Dark mode keeps full-strength pastels (lilac 65.6, butter 72.5 from the dark page). Large pastel areas may glare; B's dimmed set was not measured against this palette.
Danger looks gentle: blush fill with a soft rim. A destructive button no longer looks alarming, which is the direct cost of 'truly pastel'.

Lilac at hue 303 is as close to periwinkle #ccccff (2.4) as to pale lilac (2.5). A pinker, more literal lilac costs separation from robin's egg (4.9 at hue 309). If the owner reads it as too blue, that is the trade to revisit.

Sorbet cannot express this today: every ramp shares one lightness curve and the build fails on WCAG 4.5:1 and 3:1 pairings (tokens/rules.ts, semantics.ts). Until a replacement gate exists (Lc floors for text, sep floors for edges, checked under the three simulations) nothing enforces any of these numbers.

judge:system-fit.lens: Will it work across the whole component library, in both modes. Terms: "sep" = how far apart two colours look (OKLab distance x100 from the kit; under 5 is hard to tell apart, 10+ is clearly different). Four numbers in a row are normal / protan / deutan / tritan (the three simulated colour-blindness types); a single number is the worst of the four. "Lc" = APCA lightness contrast (75+ paragraphs, 60+ short labels, 30 the floor). "top/side/bottom" = the first CSS pixel beside that side of an element. METHOD: nothing taken on trust. (1) Every palette, text and state claim re-run through colorkit.mjs. (2) Every edge recipe of all three proposals pasted verbatim into one page and rendered in headless Chromium at 2x: 197 placements (card on page, popover on a card, field on a card and on the page, checkbox, switch, slider, thumb, four buttons, card on a lilac and a butter wash; light and dark), real pixels sampled on three sides and measured against the fill and against what the element sits on, in all four views. (3) A second render of 56 synthesis candidates on a hybrid palette. Proposals are called A (colour science), B (fidelity), C (edges first). Nothing in /Users/homelab/code/sorbet was edited. Scratch files: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-homelab/06652a5c-23e2-4a00-8579-52c3b446d84b/scratchpad/judge-lib/ - stress-round1.png and stress-{A,B,C}-{light,dark}.png (the three proposals as rendered), round2.png (synthesis candidates), recipes.mjs (the recipes as data), samples-round1.json / samples-round2.json (sampled pixels), analyse.mjs, states.mjs, text.mjs, harsh.mjs, hybrid.mjs, misc.mjs, final.mjs (the measurements).

scores.strongest: Palette and ink are the most library-proof. Its staggered lightness tiers are the only palette where the success and danger fills stay apart (blush~robin 12.2/9.4/5.9/15.1; B's is 3.2 under protan, C's 5.4 under deutan), and all ten pairs re-measure at 5.9 or more. Cocoa ink #694323 is the only body ink 6+ from a same-lightness gray in all three simulations (6.3/6.4/7.8), and it leaves violet free as a second text colour: link #654199 vs body is 18.8/19.4/18.4/8.5. That matters library-wide because sorbet uses primary-text as a state cue in 17 places; with B's or C's purple inks that difference falls to 3.3-8.0. Controls use INSET rings (27.0 from a card), so they survive overflow-clipping parents and add no size. Buttons are soft but present: rendered 12.3-13.4 top, 14.2-15.6 side, 17.2-18.5 bottom.
scores.weakest: Dark mode, which is the owner's named complaint. Rendered: card on the dark page 6.7 top / 5.7 side / 4.0 bottom outside (the black pool cancels the cream ring at the bottom), with a 5.6 fill step; a popover on a dark card 5.8/4.7/2.1 with a 4.5 fill step. C's recipe measures 16.3/15.5/14.4 and 14.0/12.5/10.4 in the same spots. Dark focus ring #c6b1f0 is 6.2 from a lilac fill. Switch on vs off is pastel vs cream: 9.0 worst (13.4 red-green) where B and C get 20.9-22.6. Gaps: no invalid-field recipe, no divider tone, one elevation only. Light card top edge is a 1px line at 7.1.

scores.proposal_lens: B - fidelity to the five names
scores.strongest: Its recipes were genuinely rendered and re-measure within 1 (card 7.0/10.2/14.1, field on a card 11.6-15.5, checkbox ring 22.4-26.3). Strongest state steps for unlabelled controls: checked fill #ae8bdc is 29.8+ from unchecked, switch on vs off 20.9+. The only proposal with a 'deep cream' tone #efdcb5 (6.8 from the page, 9.1 from a card), which the library needs for hover washes and tracks because the sunken tone is only 2-5 from everything. Correct hover rule (lift the shadow, leave the fill: darkening a fill by 0.03 lightness costs 5-6 Lc of label contrast, verified). Controls are inset, focus is a real outline, hexes are closest to what the five names mean.
scores.weakest: Palette and ink give up the most for this reader. blush~robin is 3.2 under protan and 4.5 under deutan, so the danger and success fills are the same colour; lilac~robin is 4.2. Plum ink #643d60 is 3.2 from a same-lightness gray under deutan: the dark gray the owner is leaving. Links are 3.3-4.3 from body ink. Dark mode: the focus ring is the lilac fill's own hex (0.0 apart; 4.2 from robin), card edge 8.6/7.5/6.5, popover on a card 7.7/6.3/4.1, and the dark switch thumb is unspecified (read literally as plum it is 15.2 from the off track; A's and C's cream thumbs are 79+). The 50% danger rim on a field lands 7.2 from B's own focus ring and 9.4 from the resting ring, so invalid and focused look alike. Milk tick on the checked fill is Lc 55.0.

scores.strongest: The only complete edge system and the only dark mode that fixes the stated problem: card on the dark page 16.3/15.5/14.4 with a 7.0 fill step, popover on a dark card 14.0/12.5/10.4. I re-rendered the same recipe on a cocoa-hue ladder with a cream rim and it transfers (17.3/16.5/15.2; popover 14.8/13.2/11.1). Per-hue 'shade' tones give sorbet the shape-maker colours it needs for progress tone bars, toast stripes, stars and switch tracks: shades on a sunken track measure 15.4-23.2, where the pastel fills themselves are 4.1-9.3. Its dead-zone finding is real (a ring at alpha .4-.55 lands 1.8-5.4 from the fill it surrounds; .85 gives 10.4). The halo card has actual width (1.5 / 3 / 5.5 px at sep 5+) instead of a 1px line.
scores.weakest: It is the least soft, and has three mechanical defects for a library. (1) Lines: button rings are crisp 1px at 15.9-23.1 from the page (A 12-15, B 9-14). The danger ring #b14e61 is 4.92:1 and 42.7 from a card, the same strength as today's border-strong (4.83:1, 44.8), and under protan it simulates to neutral gray #626261 (chroma 0.002): the harsh gray outline, back, on every destructive button, danger alert and invalid field. (2) Control rings are OUTER shadows: clipped by overflow parents (tabs list, table wrap, carousel, combobox panel) and they grow a 20px box to 23px. (3) Focus is a box-shadow: removed by Windows forced-colours mode, clipped, needs to know the colour behind it, and competes with every component's own shadow (31 focus-ring includes). Also: the sunken-well field costs typed text 9 Lc (78.2 vs 87+), placeholder falls to 58.1, and a sunken fill is how sorbet draws a DISABLED field today; robin as the selected/current wash is the weakest choice for this reader (6.0-6.8 full strength, 3.0-3.5 at 50%, under protan); dark focus ring equals the lilac fill (0.0); lilac~robin 4.1; links 4.4-8.0 from body ink.

recommended_synthesis.roles: All three proposals reached the same assignment independently and it re-measures: primary = lilac, secondary = blush, accent = butter, robin = success plus decoration. It maps onto sorbet's existing token names with no structural change: success = robin, warning = butter, danger = blush, info = lilac. What has to be ADDED to the model, per role: (1) {role}-solid = the fill's own hue 0.14 darker (lilac #b095d9, blush #dc8a91, butter #c9b367, robin #57c4ca) - the shape-maker for anything with no text: control rings, switch-on track, slider fill, tab bar, progress bars, toast stripes (15.4-23.2 from a sunken track; lilac's is 27.2 from a card at 2.49:1). (2) {role}-edge = the same hue at L 0.55 (#7f5fab, #ac505c, #876f00, #008287), used ONLY inside shadows at low alpha; this is the existing --edge knob in atoms/_button.scss. (3) {role}-subtle = the fill at 50% over the surface, for alerts, toasts and selected rows: body ink reads Lc 72.8-78.7 there, against 59.6-60.3 on the full lilac or blush fill, so paragraphs go on the wash and only labels on the fill. (4) on-{role} = one strong ink in both modes (worst Lc on lilac 68.0, blush 66.7, butter 78.9, robin 75.9). Changes to what the proposals said: SELECTED / CURRENT / text selection use LILAC, not robin (lilac is 11.1-13.1 from its surface; robin is 6.0-6.8 under protan), plus a 3px inset bar in #b095d9 (27.2 from a card, 20.7 from the lilac wash) and semibold weight - that fixes the hue-only current-page and highlighted-option defects in the digest. FOCUS = one tone in both modes, #8e6ac7 (L 0.60), as a 3px outline at 2px offset: 37.1 from cream, 39.2 from a card, 26.1+ from every pastel fill, 39.2 / 32.2 / 25.8 from the dark page / card / raised surface. LINKS = violet #654199, underlined. Statuses: fills are decoration (status fills are 5.8-13 apart at worst), so every status carries its own icon shape and its word; that is a component-contract change (Alert, Toast, Badge, the danger Button, the menu danger item). Danger additionally gets a 2px edge in rose #d77784 (L 0.68): 30.4 from a field, 17.0 from the resting ring, 14.1 from the focus ring, 2.96:1 - firm, but a third lighter than C's #b14e61.

recommended_synthesis.edges: ONE RULE, THREE PLACES. (1) Containers get a halo, no ring: card = 0 0 6px 1px rgb(161 110 50 / .26), 0 2px 4px rgb(161 110 50 / .18), 0 10px 28px -8px rgb(161 110 50 / .26) - rendered on this palette 7.7 top / 10.9 side / 14.8 bottom, the band 1.5 / 3 / 5.5 px wide. Floating panels (popover, menu, modal, toast) need a second, stronger tier because milk on milk has no fill step: 0 0 10px 2px rgb(161 110 50 / .30), 0 4px 8px rgb(161 110 50 / .20), 0 18px 44px -10px rgb(161 110 50 / .36) = 9.6 / 13.7 / 19.7 on a card, 4.5-8 px wide. Shadow colour is caramel, the cream's own hue taken dark; it measures the same in every simulation. (2) Text-shaped controls stay milk with an inset hairline: inset 0 0 0 1px rgb(129 91 31 / .24), inset 0 2px 3px rgb(129 91 31 / .14), 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / .9) = 11.4-15.6 on a card where the fill step is 0. (3) Unlabelled controls get an INSET 1.5px ring in #b095d9 (27.2 from a card, 25.1 from the page, 2.49:1); checked = lilac fill + the same ring + ink tick (interior change 13.1 worst, tick Lc 68.0); switch-on and slider fill use #b095d9 itself (23.2 from the off track, thumb 27.2 from it). Dividers and table rules, which ARE the line: cream hue at L 0.87, #e3d2b0 (12.0 from milk, 9.7 from cream). Hover = shadow lift, never a darker fill. DARK (C's recipe, on a ladder in the ink's own hue at L 0.206 / 0.276 / 0.340 / 0.155; for cocoa: page #1e150e, card #30251d, raised #42352b, well #120a06): inset 0 1px 0 rgb(254 244 220 / .22), 0 0 0 1px rgb(254 244 220 / .18), 0 10px 28px -6px rgb(5 2 10 / .7) = 17.3 / 16.5 / 15.2 on the page, 14.8 / 13.2 / 11.1 for a popover on a card. Do not go below .18: at .12 the bottom edge of a popover falls to 4.3. Fills and label ink are identical in both modes. MECHANICS that decide whether it survives a library: keep rings inset on controls; keep a 1px transparent border on every control and card so forced-colours mode still draws one; focus stays an outline; build each element's shadow from custom properties (--edge-shadow, --state-shadow) so focus and invalid add a layer instead of replacing the edge; add box-shadow to the color-transition mixin; give clipping parents (carousel viewport, tabs list) padding equal to the halo. THE THREE TREATMENTS TO SHOW SIDE BY SIDE, all rendered on this palette in round2.png: (a) HAIRLINE (A) - 1px own-hue ring at alpha .26 plus a tight shadow: buttons 11.0-11.9 top / 13.0-13.7 side / 15.3-16.5 bottom, band 1px. Quietest; closest to no outline. (b) HALO (C's card idea extended to buttons) - no ring, a 4px own-hue glow: 0 0 4px 1px rgb(deep / .34), 0 1px 2px rgb(deep / .32), 0 4px 10px -2px rgb(deep / .26) = 10.5-11.4 / 14.9-16.0 / 20.0-21.4, band 2-4 px. The literal reading of 'similarly coloured box shadow'; my recommendation. (c) SHADE RING (C) - crisp 1px ring at alpha .85: 15.5-21.5 / 16.1-22.4 / 17.1-23.5. Safest on a washed-out screen, and it reads as an outline. Two smaller pairs worth one row each: field as milk + hairline (11.4-15.6) vs C's sunken well (12.8-17.5, but typed text drops to Lc 78); dark card rim at .18 vs .12.

refuted_claims: B: 'blush vs robin cannot be tuned away inside pastel; a search of 15,552 combinations topped out at 4.8'. False. A's blush #fbbfc3 against A's robin #bee9ee measures 9.4 protan / 5.9 deutan, both inside the pastel bounds; the hybrid above measures 9.5 / 5.8. The cure is a lightness gap of about 0.04, which B's own pair (L 0.884 vs 0.865, the wrong way round for protan) does not have. B's own figure of 3.2 is correct for B's hexes.

B: plum ink 'does not turn into the dark grey you are leaving'. Under deutan #643d60 is 3.2 from a gray of the same lightness (chroma kept 0.033); under protan 5.2. Cocoa is 6.3/6.4/7.8 and aubergine 7.7/6.5/3.3.

B and C: the dark-mode focus ring is 'the pastel itself, 64-65 from the page'. True against the page, but it is the lilac fill's own hex: 0.0 from a primary button or any lilac-filled element, 4.1-4.2 from robin under deutan. It only shows where a dark gap separates ring and fill, and sorbet draws focus INSET (negative offset) on sidebar items, tabs, table sort and calendar days. A's #c6b1f0 is 6.2 from lilac. One mid tone, #8e6ac7, is 25.8+ from everything in both modes.

C: 'the button has no ringless version that keeps butter's top edge above 3.3'. A ringless 4px halo layer rendered at 11.0 top / 15.4 side / 20.6 bottom on butter (11.6 / 16.0 / 21.9 on a card), 2-4 px wide. Drop shadows alone fail; a zero-offset glow does not.

C: the danger ring as part of a soft-edge system. #b14e61 at 2px is 4.92:1 and 42.7 from a card; today's border-strong, the line being retired, is 4.83:1 and 44.8. Under protan it simulates to #626261, chroma 0.002: a dark gray outline. A's 4px danger bar #ac505c is 5.01:1 and simulates to #63625c, though as a bar on one side rather than an outline.

C (and A in part): robin as the selected / current / text-selection wash. Under protan robin is 6.0 from cream and 6.8 from a card at full strength, 3.0-3.5 at 50%; lilac is 11.1 and 13.1 (5.3-6.4 at 50%). It would leave the digest's hue-only 'current page' and 'selection' defects in place.
A: the card edge is '9.5 / 9.8 / 9.4 / 9.1 from the page'. Rendered, the top edge is 7.1 (side 11.1, bottom 15.4) and the band is 1px wide. The figure is a modelled average, not the weakest side.

A: dark card 'outer ring 7.5 from the page'. Rendered 6.7 top / 5.7 side / 4.0 bottom; the black drop pool cancels the cream ring at the bottom, the effect C measured and A did not. A popover on a dark card is 5.8 / 4.7 / 2.1.

B: button edges 'weakest side, worst view: lilac 10.8, blush 8.5, robin 7.8'. Those three are exactly the fill-vs-cream separations; the rendered top edges are 9.2, 8.7 and 8.6 (butter's 10.1 matches). Minor.

A: hover as 'fill one step deeper'. A's stated hover fills are 2.5-3.3 from the resting fills, which is not a visible change; the ring going from alpha .26 to .40 is what carries hover. B's and C's 'move the shadow' rule is the correct one.

B: the 50% rose rim as the danger cue that 'holds in every view'. On a field it lands #d8a3a6: 9.4 from B's resting ring and 7.2 from B's own focus ring, so an invalid field and a focused one differ mainly by 1px of thickness.
open_risks: The colour-blindness type is still unrecorded. Everything above holds in all three simulations for READING; the choices that lean on red-green are lilac as primary and aubergine as an ink (both go gray under tritan). Cocoa ink and the caramel edges do not depend on the type. One look at a rendered sheet settles more than more measurement.

Statuses now reuse brand fills (danger = secondary's blush, info = primary's lilac, warning = accent's butter), 5.8-13 apart at worst. That is a component-contract change, not a token change: Alert, Toast, Badge and the danger Button need a mandatory icon and word. Two places in sorbet signal danger by text colour ONLY today and would lose their one cue under a single ink: the menu danger item and the token-studio failures list.

Alerts are paragraphs on a status fill. Body ink on the full lilac or blush fill is Lc 59.6-60.3, under the 75 paragraph line. They need the 50% wash tokens (body 72.8-78.7), and a wash is only 3.5-7.9 from a card, so it needs its own-hue edge too. None of the three proposals specified these.

Disabled is opacity 0.55 in 23 places. Measured on this palette: a disabled butter or robin button fill is 2.9-4.4 from the page (the shape disappears) while its label stays at Lc 42-51. Readable as 'off', but it should be looked at, not assumed.

Edges that are box-shadows are clipped by overflow parents (.sb-card, table wrap, tabs list, carousel viewport, combobox panel) and removed entirely by Windows forced-colours mode. Inset rings, a transparent border and an outline focus ring cover the controls; a card inside a carousel still loses its halo at the clip line unless the viewport is padded.

box-shadow is one property. control-glow, focus and invalid states all write it today, so a soft edge on the same element is deleted on focus unless every component composes its shadow from shared custom properties. This is the largest mechanical piece of the refactor and touches input, number-input, combobox, date-range and the button.
input-group joins neighbours by removing one border side; an inset ring has no per-side off switch. It needs per-side inset shadows or a deliberate 1px seam.

Dark mode is measured for surfaces, edges, text and controls only. Full-strength pastel fills are 63-70 from the dark page and may glare as large areas; a 20% wash over a dark card measured 13.0-14.6 from the card with text at Lc 77.7-79.8, but that is one data point, not a designed set.

The 5 / 10 thresholds describe patches. A 1px line needs more than a patch to be seen, which is why I prefer the 2-6 px halo to a hairline at the same sep; that preference is a judgement about the owner's eyes and screens, not a measurement. Every card treatment here tops out near 7-8 at the top edge.

src/tokens/rules.ts fails the build on anything under 3:1 or 4.5:1, and buildMode shares one lightness curve across ramps. Palette, builder and gate have to change in one commit, and the gate needs replacing (Lc floors for text, sep floors for edges and state pairs, each under the three simulations) rather than deleting, or nothing enforces these numbers. The other four presets (ocean, forest, noir, midnight) go through the same builder.
Not examined by anyone: chart series colours, the scrim (hard black at 0.6), tooltips beyond contrast, and the token-studio contrast report that currently displays the WCAG results.
APCA is a draft method and its 75 / 60 lines assume ordinary sizes and weights. Sorbet's small text (12-14px) should take the L 0.34-0.38 steps, not the body step.
